units.title: Science and Technology - Nature and Scope, Relevance to Daily Life, National S&T Policy, Institutions and Prominent Indian Scientists

rows.title: Nature, scope and characteristics of science and technology; science vs technology

secs.t: Technology terms - definitions (biometrics, digital embossing, geospatial, 3D printing, RFID, wearables)

x: Biometrics identifies a person using distinctive physical or behavioural characteristics such as fingerprints, iris patterns or facial features.
FASTag uses passive RFID; the tag receives power from the electromagnetic field generated by the toll reader.
Wearables may be worn as accessories or clothing, implanted or tattooed on the skin, and generally combine sensors, software and wireless connectivity as part of the Internet of Things.

secs.t: Characteristics of science and science vs pseudoscience

x: Exam angle: "which has NOT been considered a science" - astrology.
Science is empirical, testable or falsifiable, reproducible, systematic and self-correcting.
Nanotechnology deals with phenomena and structures at approximately 1–100 nanometres.
The Nano Science and Technology Initiative of the Department of Science and Technology was launched in 2001; it was followed by the Nano Mission in 2007.

secs.t: Science vs technology - definitions, basic vs applied research, invention vs innovation

x: Science produces laws and theories; technology produces products and processes; basic research is curiosity-driven; applied research addresses a set problem.
Translational research
takes results obtained in the laboratory and moves them towards practical use.
The future of research is associated with interdisciplinary work and translational research that carries laboratory results towards application.

secs.t: Scientific method - steps from observation to theory and law

x: The sequence is observation, question, hypothesis, experiment, analysis and conclusion.
After a conclusion,
replication and peer review
help check the reliability and acceptance of the findings.
Both statements are true, and the distinction between explanation and description explains why a theory does not transform into a law.

secs.t: Scope - branches of science and interdisciplinary fields

x: Biotechnology combines biology and engineering; geoinformatics combines geography and IT; data science combines statistics and computing; cyber-physical systems combine computing with physical systems through sensors.
ESSO, established in 2007 under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, covers ocean science and technology, atmospheric and climate science, geoscience, polar science and the cryosphere.

secs.t: Technology development stages - lab to market, Technology Readiness Levels

x: The Technology Readiness Level scale ranges from
TRL 1 to TRL 9
and originated with NASA.
The RDI Scheme finances projects at
TRL 4 and above
, along with strategic technologies and a Deep-Tech Fund of Funds.
The convener of the Inter-Ministerial Board is the Joint Secretary of the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).

secs.t: Scientific temper - Fundamental Duty article and movements

x: Article 51A(h) lists the Fundamental Duty to
develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform
Kerala Sastra Sahitya Parishad dates to 1962; the Statement on Scientific Temper to 1981; the Maharashtra Anti-Superstition Act to 2013; and National Science Day is observed on 28 February.
Vigyan Jyoti is intended to encourage
girls
to pursue Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The 1950s–1970s focused on institution-building and scientific temper, the 1980s on self-reliance, the 2010s on innovation, and the present phase on artificial intelligence, quantum technology and semiconductors.
India's 2025 Global Innovation Index rank was 38th, while its Network Readiness Index rank was 49th in 2024 compared with 79th in 2019.

rows.title: Relevance of science and technology to day-to-day life - health, food, transport, communication, household

secs.t: Harmful chemicals in daily-use products → product or source

x: Exam angle: product → banned chemical matching from recent state bans.
Aristolochic acid occurs in Aristolochia plants used in some herbal medicines and is associated with
kidney damage and urinary-tract cancer
Lead is associated with old paints, pipes, some cosmetics and lead-chromate-adulterated spices, not MRI contrast agents.
BPA, triclosan and phthalates have endocrine-related concerns, while lead is neurotoxic and especially harmful to children.

secs.t: Health technologies - telemedicine, dialysis, imaging, indigenous devices

x: X-ray uses ionising electromagnetic radiation; CT reconstructs multiple X-ray images; MRI uses magnetic fields and radio waves; ultrasound uses sound waves and echoes.
Dense bone absorbs more X-ray radiation, making X-rays useful for detecting fractures.
A CT scan reconstructs multiple X-ray images by computer to produce cross-sectional views and generally involves a higher radiation dose than an ordinary X-ray.

secs.t: Food technology - additives, adulterants, preservation, fortification, irradiation, cold chain, packaging

x: MoFPI funds multi-product irradiation units under the Cold Chain scheme of PM Kisan Sampada Yojana.
Fortification adds micronutrients: iodised salt, rice fortified with iron, folic acid and B12, and oil and milk fortified with vitamins A and D. The FSSAI '+F' logo identifies fortified foods.
Anna Chakra optimises Public Distribution System routes to 4.37 lakh fair price shops and is reported to save about ₹250 crore annually.

secs.t: Positive vs negative impacts of technology on daily life

x: Wearables support health tracking; digital payments relate to e-governance, while screen time and cyber fraud are negative consequences.
Improved communication
is a positive impact.
In August 2026, the Supreme Court sought the Centre's reply on a plea concerning high-risk AI, including biometric surveillance and risk-scoring in food, health, pension and scholarship delivery.

secs.t: Geospatial technology in public health

x: Geospatial tools support contact tracing, hotspot mapping and the selection of suitable locations for PHCs and hospitals.
The
Integrated Health Information Platform
, or IHIP, of IDSP supports GIS-enabled real-time disease surveillance.
The mission joins the
Health, Animal Husbandry, Environment and Science and Technology
ministries to address zoonoses and antimicrobial resistance.

secs.t: Household appliances → working principle

x: Microwave ovens use microwaves of about
2.45 GHz
, which make water molecules rotate and thereby generate heat.
Higher pressure raises the boiling point of water to about 120°C
, allowing food to cook at a higher temperature.
Induction stove demand rose by about
three-fold
in March 2026 amid fears of LPG shortages.

secs.t: Smart materials and sensors → daily application

x: Hydrogels are water-absorbing polymers used in
contact lenses, wound dressings, diapers and drug delivery
An accelerometer can detect sudden deceleration for airbag deployment and can also support screen rotation and step counting.
The graphene oxide sensor is described as
a low-cost flexible sensor
using pencil-drawn electrodes.
Graphene- or carbon-fibre-electrode flexible batteries can power
wearables and flexible displays

secs.t: Transport technologies - EVs, FASTag, metro, GPS tracking, hydrogen

x: FASTag uses passive RFID and obtains power from the reader's field; it does not require an independent battery for its basic operation.
Driverless cars and smart factories are examples of cyber-physical systems, in which computational systems interact with physical processes.
Electric vehicles use motors driven by lithium-ion batteries and have no tailpipe emission.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Supreme Court notice on unregulated welfare AI was reported on 14
August 2026

x: PYQ practice only.

secs.t: General science PYQs - Chemistry (elements, compounds, acids and bases, metals, everyday chemicals)

x: PYQ practice only.

x: PYQ practice only.

x: PYQ practice only.

rows.title: Science, Technology and Innovation Policy - 1958 Resolution, 1983, 2003, 2013 policies and the STIP draft
sub: Group-II M2-B-1: National Science and Technology Policy - evolution from 1958 to the recent STI Policy

secs.t: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

x: Exam angle: match policy-year-PM, or "which was the first/fifth policy".
All three statements correctly describe the Technology Policy Statement, 1983, associated with technological competence, self-reliance, technology absorption and reduced import dependence.
The STI Policy, 2013 made innovation central and set the objective of placing India among the top five scientific powers by 2020.
The 2013 policy envisaged direct STI intervention in about ten high-impact sectors and the use of modern science for traditional knowledge.

secs.t: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

x: Exam angle: "which is NOT an outcome/objective" of a given policy.
The Draft STIP 2020 envisioned India becoming
one of the top three scientific superpowers in the coming decade
and proposed a people-centric STI ecosystem.
Atal Innovation Mission
was not an outcome of STIP 2020; it was set up by NITI Aayog in 2016 as a separate initiative promoting innovation among students.
Periodic review and exit strategies
were proposed to improve accountability and enable the discontinuation or restructuring of programmes when necessary.

secs.t: GERD targets stated in each policy - comparison

x: The recommendations called for GERD to reach 2% of GDP within four to five years through the private sector, proposed NISPG, and suggested a unified fellowship called Vigyan Nidhi.
The RDI Fund has a ₹1 lakh crore size, includes ₹20,000 crore for FY 2025–26, promotes private R&D and operates through a Special Purpose Fund in ANRF.

secs.t: Implementation bodies - PM-STIAC, Principal Scientific Adviser, ANRF Act 2023

x: The office was created in 1999, A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was its first holder, and the PSA advises the Prime Minister and Cabinet on science and technology.
DST dates from 1971, DBT from 1986, CSIR from 1942, and the Secretary of DSIR serves as the Director-General of CSIR.
CSIR and the Department of Biotechnology act as India’s lead agencies for BRICS science and technology cooperation during India’s chairship.

secs.t: Decade of Innovation (2010-2020)

x: The National Innovation Council was established in 2010 under Sam Pitroda, with inclusive innovation as its goal.
The National Innovation Council promoted inclusive innovation through state and sectoral innovation councils.
The period 2010–2020 was declared India's “
Decade of Innovation

secs.t: S&T in Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog documents

x: NITI Aayog
is the nodal agency for improving India’s GII rank and publishes the India Innovation Index.
The report states that approximately
of ANRF funds go to IITs and also points to slow approvals.
DRDO was formed in 1958 by merging the Technical Development Establishments, the Directorate of Technical Development and Production, and the Defence Science Organisation.

secs.t: AP State Council of Science and Technology (APCOST) - state-level role

x: State S&T councils frame state S&T policy, provide research grants and popularise science.
APCOST works under the Andhra Pradesh
Environment, Forests, Science and Technology Department
APCOST and similar state councils receive support under the Department of Science and Technology’s
State S&T Programme
The stated institutional information does not specify APCOST’s founding year or current programmes.

secs.t: DST research-infrastructure schemes → full form + purpose

x: INSPIRE stands for Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research and covers a continuum from school awards to PhD fellowships and faculty posts to attract young talent to science.
SATHI provides shared infrastructure, FIST upgrades laboratories, PURSE uses research-publication performance for grants, and SAIF provides regional access to high-end instruments.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The draft policy proposes increasing public health-research spending from 0.024% of GDP to 0.072% by 2037 and 0.15% by 2047.
The 2% GERD target has not been achieved under any policy, and ANRF grants have been criticised for favouring IITs; this is a distributional criticism distinct from health-research spending targets.
The DST-STI Hub at SPMVV, Tirupati focuses on
sericulture, agriculture and livelihoods for SC/ST women
through a three-year project.

rows.title: Research and development spending in India; GERD, innovation indices, patents ecosystem

secs.t: GERD as % of GDP - India vs USA, China, Israel, South Korea

x: India's GERD was
of GDP in FY 2023–24, described as a 15-year high after reversing a decade-long decline.
South Korea
's GERD is about 5.3% of GDP, compared with about 5% for Israel, 3.5% for the USA, 2.4% for China and 0.84% for India.
The earlier figure of 0.64–0.65% relates to
data; the later FY 2023–24 figure is 0.84%.

secs.t: R&D spending share - government vs private, department-wise

x: Private industry accounted for
of R&D expenditure in FY 2023–24 and overtook public funding for the first time.
India's private share was about 36%, compared with about 70% in the USA and 76% in South Korea.
Private R&D spending nearly tripled, rising from ₹44,800 crore to ₹1.26 lakh crore.
The identified reasons are private risk aversion, weak lab–industry linkages and a shortage of deep-tech capital.

secs.t: Global Innovation Index - publisher, India's rank trend, pillars

x: The Global Innovation Index is published by the World Intellectual Property Organization (
WIPO
India ranked 38th among 139 economies in the 2025 Global Innovation Index.
The GII has seven pillars, comprising five input pillars and two output pillars.

secs.t: India Innovation Index - publisher, state categories, AP position

x: The India Innovation Index is released by NITI Aayog in association with the Institute for Competitiveness.
The 2021 leaders were Karnataka among Major States, Manipur among North-East and Hill States, and Chandigarh among UTs and City States.

secs.t: Patents ecosystem - Patents Act 1970, National IPR Policy 2016, filings rank, resident vs non-resident

x: The National IPR Policy, 2016 uses the slogan “
Creative India; Innovative India
” and seeks to promote awareness, enforcement and innovation through IP protection.
SIPP provides free facilitation for start-ups filing patents, trademarks and designs; more than 95% of applications are filed online.
India ranked 38th in GII 2025, sixth globally in WIPO 2023 patent filing activity, and 49th of 133 in the Network Readiness Index 2024.

secs.t: Researchers per million, publications rank, PhDs

x: India had approximately 262 FTE researchers per million people.
India ranked
third
globally in scientific publications; its nanoscience publications also ranked third after China and the USA.
Indian agencies fund less than 10% of applications, while the corresponding figures cited are 26% for the US NSF and 19% for UKRI.

secs.t: Startup and innovation ecosystem - unicorns, Startup India, incubators, agri-startups

x: India is the
third
-largest start-up hub and had 1.59 lakh DPIIT-recognised start-ups according to the cited figure.
All three are associated with India's deep-tech start-up ecosystem: the National Deep-Tech Startup Policy, February 2026 eligibility notification and Startup Fund of Funds 2.0.
The Atal Innovation Mission promotes innovation through school tinkering labs, incubation centres and a mentor network.

secs.t: R&D funding reforms - RDI scheme, ANRF funding share

x: The RDI Scheme was approved on 1 July 2025, provides a ₹1 lakh crore fund, places the ANRF as custodian and is intended to operate over seven years.
The RDI Scheme is designed to provide
concessional finance for private-sector research and development
in identified frontier and strategic areas.
The PM Research Chair seeks to bring Indian-origin researchers back to India, thereby promoting brain gain.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The criticism is that research funding remains slow and IIT-heavy, indicating both inadequate pace and institutional concentration.
The criticism is that improved rankings can coexist with weak R&D intensity, low researcher density and poor commercialisation of research.
IISER Tirupati was placed
20th
among Indian institutions in the Nature Index 2026.

rows.title: S&T institutions - CSIR and its laboratories, DST, DBT, DSIR, SERB

secs.t: CSIR laboratories → location, founding year, field

x: Exam angle: "headquarters of X is located in" - Nagpur, Hyderabad, Lucknow and Bhavnagar recur.
Saheli, a centchroman-based weekly oral contraceptive, was developed by the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow.
The National Physical Laboratory (
NPL
), New Delhi, maintains national measurement standards and keeps Indian Standard Time.
IMTECH, Chandigarh, works in microbial technology and hosts the MTCC gene bank, an IDA under the Budapest Treaty.

secs.t: DBT - autonomous institutes → location, and BIRAC

x: BRIC was established in 2023 as an apex body integrating 14 DBT institutions, with the Union S&T Minister as Chair and the DBT Secretary as ex officio Director-General.
BIRAC, or Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council, is a not-for-profit Section 8 company of DBT established in 2012 to fund biotechnology start-ups.

secs.t: CSIR technologies in news → developing lab

x: NCL, Pune
, developed and scaled up methanol-to-DME technology, with DME serving as an LPG substitute.
HANSA-3 (NG) is a
trainer aircraft developed by NAL
, and Letters of Intent were reported for 114 aircraft.
CSIO transferred the MSCOPE motor stethoscope, power-quality analyser and Su-30 HUD optics.
CMERI, Durgapur
, developed the beam catcher for the FAIR accelerator in Germany.

secs.t: CSIR - setup year, ex-officio president, structure, number of labs

x: CSIR was set up in September 1942 as an autonomous body and is registered as a society.
The CSIR network consists of
37 national laboratories, 39 outreach centres, 1 innovation complex and 3 units
CSIR, DAE, DoS, ICMR and ICAR
were allowed to bypass GeM for scientific equipment.

secs.t: Other national research institutes → location, founder/year

x: IISc, Bengaluru, was founded in 1909 with the vision of
Jamsetji Tata
The National Centre for Earth Science Studies (NCESS) was established in Kerala in 1978 and has been under the Ministry of Earth Sciences since 2014.
The Bose Institute is located in Kolkata, functions as a DST autonomous institute and is India’s nodal body for FAIR.

secs.t: DST - establishment, mandate, autonomous institutes, flagship schemes

x: Bose Institute, JNCASR, Raman Research Institute and Wadia Institute are among the autonomous bodies associated with DST.
INSPIRE
is a flagship scheme of DST associated with promoting scientific interest and talent.
DST is nodal for the RDI Scheme, and LENSD, VIS and CDX are associated with it.
FAIR is funded equally by DST and DAE, in a
proportion.

secs.t: DSIR - PSUs (CEL, NRDC), in-house R&D recognition

x: DSIR controls two public sector undertakings, NRDC and CEL.
DSIR recognises more than 2,000 in-house R&D centres, more than 900 SIROs and more than 500 public-funded institutions.
DSIR recognition makes the recognised institutions eligible for
income tax and customs duty exemptions
PRISM, PACE, BIRD-crf and A2K+ are all components of DSIR’s Umbrella Industrial R&D scheme.

secs.t: SERB - grants and status after ANRF

x: Core Research Grant and
SERB
-POWER are grants associated with the Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB).
The SERB Overseas Fellowship is intended for
diaspora researchers
The
Ramanujan Fellowship
is a return fellowship intended to repatriate scientists to India.
The Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship is a return fellowship in
life sciences
The monthly amount mentioned for the Prime Minister’s Research Fellowship is

secs.t: CSIR and DBT laboratories in AP and Telangana

x: CCMB, IICT and NGRI
are CSIR laboratories or centres located in Hyderabad.
CDFD is a DBT institution in Hyderabad.
INCOIS
is a non-CSIR institution located in Hyderabad.
The NIO Regional Centre in Andhra Pradesh is located at
Visakhapatnam
The MoU focuses on converting shrimp waste into
chitin and glucosamine

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The proposals included reserving half of the top posts for mid-career scientists and evaluating laboratories through patents and technology transfer.
The Andhra Pradesh angle includes the
shrimp-waste value chain with IICT and research at AIIMS Mangalagiri
HANSA-3 (NG) is
the first indigenously developed aircraft to be commercially manufactured in India

rows.title: S&T institutions - ICAR, ICMR, ICFRE, DRDO, ISRO, DAE, DoS and their mandates

secs.t: ICAR institutes → location, founding year; first Krishi Vigyan Kendra

x: ICRISAT is at Patancheru, IARI at New Delhi, CRRI/NRRI at Cuttack and CIFA at Bhubaneswar.
ICAR was established in 1929 and functions as an autonomous body under the
Department of Agricultural Research and Education
(DARE).
The stated ICAR structure includes 72 research institutes, 6 national bureaux, 12 NRCs and 22 directorates/ATARIs.

secs.t: ICFRE - founding year, headquarters, institutes → location

x: ICFRE is an autonomous council under the
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
(MoEFCC).
TFRI is at Jabalpur, CSFER at Prayagraj, HFRI at Shimla and IFB at Hyderabad.
The Arid Forest Research Institute is at Jodhpur, the Rain Forest Research Institute at Jorhat and the Institute of Forest Productivity at Ranchi.

secs.t: DAE units → function; BARC products

x: The Heavy Water Board produces heavy water, IREL handles beach-sand minerals and rare earths, and AERB regulates nuclear and radiation safety.
The stated NPCIL fleet comprises 23 reactors with 7,480 MW, while 9 reactors totalling 7,500 MW were under construction.
HBNI was ranked
7th among research institutions, 12th among universities and 20th overall
in the stated NIRF 2025 rankings.

secs.t: ICMR - parent department, institutes → location, Vision 2030

x: ICMR functions under the Department of Health Research of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and is the apex body for biomedical research.
NIV is at Pune, NIN at Hyderabad, and both NIE and NIRT are located at Chennai.
The stated foundations are strengthening health research capacity, leveraging traditional medicine and aligning with the National Health Policy.

secs.t: Mega-science projects → Indian lead institutions

x: The Thirty Meter Telescope is located at Mauna Kea, Hawaii, and India’s TMT Centre is at IIA Bengaluru, with DST and DAE as Indian partners.
All four are associated with IIA Bengaluru under DST: the VELC payload, Hanle Dark Sky Reserve, Himalayan Chandra Telescope and Kodaikanal Solar Observatory.
LIGO detected gravitational waves in 2015, and the Nobel Prize was awarded in 2017 to Rainer Weiss, Barry Barish and Kip Thorne.

secs.t: Institution → parent ministry/department pairing

x: ICAR is placed under the Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), Ministry of Agriculture.
ICMR is under DHR, ISRO under DoS, DRDO under the Department of Defence R&D, and CSIR under DSIR.
ICFRE is under the
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
(MoEFCC).

secs.t: Commissions - Atomic Energy Commission, Space Commission

x: The Atomic Energy Commission was set up in 1948.
The Atomic Energy Commission undertakes policy and strategic planning, oversees BARC, NPCIL and AERB, and is chaired by the Secretary, DAE.
The Space Commission was constituted in 1972, is linked with DoS, and its Secretary also serves as ISRO Chairman; DoS reports to the Prime Minister.

secs.t: ISRO and DRDO - year, HQ, mandate

x: INCOSPAR and TERLS were established in 1962, ISRO was formed in 1969, the Space Commission was constituted in 1972, and ISRO came under DoS on 1 June 1972.
Antrix dates from 1992 and received Miniratna status in 2008; NSIL was established in 2019, and IN-SPACe in 2020 with headquarters at Ahmedabad.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The memo barred resignations of Group-A staff working on Gaganyaan after approximately 100 personnel had exited.
APSARA was Asia’s first research reactor, while the first Krishi Vigyan Kendra was established in Puducherry in 1974.
The KVK farmer–scientist meeting was held at Karakambadi in Tirupati on 24 August 2026.
The KVK upgrade plan was reported on
10 September 2026

rows.title: Academies and promotion bodies - INSA, IASc, NASI, Vigyan Prasar, National Innovation Foundation

secs.t: Vigyan Prasar - parent department and science communication platforms

x: Exam angle: "two new science communication platforms" =
DD Science and India Science
, not Gyan Darshan/Gyan Vani or DD Kisan.
Vigyan Dhara is a DST umbrella scheme merging schemes concerning S&T institutional and human capacity building, research and development, and innovation, technology development and deployment.
DD Science is the one-hour daily slot on DD National and India Science is the Internet-based channel run by Vigyan Prasar.

secs.t: Science days → date and event commemorated

x: National Science Day is observed on 28 February, National Technology Day on 11 May, and National Mathematics Day on 22 December.
National Science Day commemorates C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect in 1928.
National Mathematics Day commemorates
Srinivasa Ramanujan
's birth anniversary.
NCSTC uses National Science Day for outreach through science kits, the VIGYANOTSAV quiz, rallies and sessions for differently-abled students; these activities reached over 6.35 lakh people.

secs.t: Educational science channels - Gyan Darshan, Vyas, SWAYAM Prabha

x: SWAYAM Prabha is a group of free DTH educational channels of the Ministry of Education.
Gyan Darshan was launched on
26 January 2000
as an educational television channel involving MHRD, IGNOU and Prasar Bharati.
Vyas is the higher-education channel of the
UGC-CEC
, the Consortium for Educational Communication.
Gyan Vani is the
FM radio counterpart of Gyan Darshan
and is associated with IGNOU.

secs.t: National Innovation Foundation (NIF) - parent department, status, competitions, origin

x: NIF-India was set up in March 2000 with the support of the
Department of Science and Technology
and functions as an autonomous body of DST.
NIF's mandate is
to scout, support and spread grassroots technological innovations and outstanding traditional knowledge
STIP 2020 envisages helping grassroots innovators with intellectual property rights and patent filing through higher education institutes.

secs.t: Indian Science Congress Association (ISCA) - first session, recent sessions, themes

x: The first session of the Indian Science Congress was held in 1914 at the Asiatic Society in Kolkata and was presided over by Sir Ashutosh Mukherjee.
The association was founded in 1914 on the initiative of British chemists
J.L. Simonsen and P.S. MacMahon
The 108th session was held in January 2023 at
RTM Nagpur University

secs.t: Science outreach bodies and exhibitions → organiser

x: NCSM has its Central Research & Training Laboratory at Kolkata and follows a three-tier national, regional and sub-regional structure; it does not function exclusively through state-level centres.
Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan was launched in 2015 by the Ministry of HRD, now the Ministry of Education, to encourage practical and inquiry-based science and mathematics learning in schools.

secs.t: Science academies → headquarters, founder, founding year

x: Exam angle: order of founding NASI (1930) → IASc (1934) → INSA (1935); Raman = IASc, Saha = NASI.
INSA originated as the National Institute of Sciences of India in 1935, is headquartered at New Delhi and adopted the name INSA in 1970.
NASI was founded in 1930 by Meghnad Saha as the Uttar Pradesh Academy of Sciences and is regarded as the oldest science academy in India.

secs.t: Popular science awards and forums - India International Science Festival (IISF)

x: IISF began in 2015 in New Delhi and is organised by the Ministry of Science & Technology and the Ministry of Earth Sciences with Vijnana Bharati (VIBHA).
ICMR-SHINE, expanded as Science & Health Innovation for the Nextgen Explorers, is an outreach initiative for
students of Classes 9–12
The 2026 restructuring was institute-led and priority-aligned, ICMR-SHINE targets Classes 9–12, and DHR released the draft National Health Research Policy, 2026.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The
National Council of Science Museums
won two PRSI National Awards in 2025.
A. S. Kiran Kumar, former chief of ISRO, addressed the National Science Day 2026 events at VIT-AP.
The first Indian Science Congress was held in Kolkata in 1914.

secs.t: Women in science schemes → target group

x: Exam angle: senior women scientists + interdisciplinary =
WIDUSHI
; Vigyan Jyoti =
women/girls
in STEM.

CURIE relates to research facilities for 22 Women PG Colleges; WiSLP works with early- and mid-career women scientists and the British Council; SEED has established STI Hubs for SC/ST communities; GATI promotes institutional gender equity.
Vigyan Jyoti
targets meritorious girls of Classes IX–XII and seeks to address the under-representation of women in STEM.

secs.t: INSPIRE - full forms of components and target groups

x: INSPIRE, or Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research, is a flagship programme of the
Department of Science and Technology
launched in 2008.
SHE is the higher-education scholarship component, while AORC covers research-career opportunities through INSPIRE Fellowship and INSPIRE Faculty.
AORC stands for
Assured Opportunity for Research Careers
and includes the INSPIRE Fellowship for PhD scholars and INSPIRE Faculty support.

secs.t: Fellowships and brain-gain schemes → target group and awarding body

x: The Ramanujan Fellowship, administered by SERB and now under ANRF, is intended to attract Indian scientists working abroad back to India.
The Swarnajayanti Fellowship began in 1997 to mark
50 years of India’s Independence
and supports young scientists with a proven record.
The Prime Minister’s Research Fellows scheme supports PhD scholars in
IITs, IISc, IISERs and other top institutions

secs.t: Startup and innovation support - NIDHI, Startup India Seed Fund, TIDE 2.0

x: NIDHI, or National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations, was launched in 2016 by the
Department of Science and Technology
NIDHI includes PRAYAS, Entrepreneur-in-Residence, Seed Support System, Technology Business Incubators, Accelerators and Centres of Excellence.
The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme supports proof of concept, prototyping and market entry.
The correct order is Swarnajayanti Fellowship (1997), INSPIRE (2008), NIDHI (2016), and TIDE 2.0 (2019).

secs.t: Student-scientist and hackathon programmes → partner bodies and objective

x: JIGYASA
was started through CSIR–Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan collaboration in 2017.
JIGYASA is intended to establish a student–scientist connect by taking Kendriya Vidyalaya students into CSIR laboratories.
The Smart India Hackathon is partnered by the Ministry of Education’s Innovation Cell and AICTE and addresses problems posed by ministries and industry.
VIPNET, associated with Vigyan Prasar, aims to build a network of science clubs across India.

secs.t: National technology missions - NSM (PARAM systems), NQM, NM-ICPS

x: PARAM Shivay is hosted by IIT (BHU) Varanasi, PARAM Brahma by IISER Pune, PARAM Pravega by IISc Bengaluru and PARAM Ganga by IIT Roorkee.
MeitY launched a 3.1-petaflop PARAM Shakti system at IIT Madras on C-DAC RUDRA servers.
The IISER Tirupati TIH, IITTNiF, is associated with
Positioning and Precision Technologies

secs.t: Atal Innovation Mission - parent body and components

x: ATLs operate in schools, AICs support start-ups, and ACICs focus on rural and underserved areas.
ATLs are established in schools for students in grades 6–12 and provide exposure to technologies such as IoT, 3D printing and robotics.
LIPI, 2,500 new ATLs, 10 Atal Sectoral Innovation Launchpads and the Deeptech Reactor are all associated with AIM 2.0.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All four statements correctly describe the RDI Scheme’s approval, funding, first-year allocation and institutional steering arrangement.
The 8th Youth Co:Lab challenge 2026 is a UNDP–Atal Innovation Mission initiative.
The RDI Scheme was approved on 1 July 2025, has DST as nodal department, involves the ANRF Governing Board and includes a Deep-Tech Fund of Funds.

sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-8

secs.t: National Supercomputing Mission - PARAM systems, agencies, AIRAWAT

x: Exam angle: machine → host pairs (PARAM Shivay is NOT at IIT Guwahati).
PARAM Shivay is at IIT (BHU), PARAM Porul at NIT Tiruchirappalli, PARAM Pravega at IISc Bengaluru and PARAM Ananta at IIT Gandhinagar.
BharatGen is a government Indian-language multimodal AI project; Bhashini is associated with MeitY; BharatGPT was developed by CoRover; and AIRAWAT is the C-DAC Pune AI supercomputer.

secs.t: National Quantum Mission - approval, outlay, hubs, qubit targets

x: Quantum Computing is hosted by IISc Bengaluru, Quantum Communication by IIT Madras, Quantum Sensing and Metrology by IIT Bombay, and Quantum Materials and Devices by IIT Delhi.
The Central Fabrication Facilities are established at
IIT Delhi, IISc, IIT Bombay and IIT Kanpur
, with an indicated allocation of about ₹720 crore.
The National Quantum Mission has an outlay of ₹6,003.65 crore for eight years and targets intermediate-scale quantum computers with 50–1,000 physical qubits.

secs.t: Indian supercomputer history

x: India’s supercomputing programme began in the
late 1980s
Vijay Bhatkar is recognised as the
father of Indian supercomputing
Flosolver is associated with NAL Bengaluru, Anupam with BARC, Pratyush with IITM Pune and Mihir with NCMRWF, Noida.
TIFRAC was India’s first indigenous computer.

secs.t: Bio-E3 Policy

x: The Bio-E3 Policy is intended to
build a bio-manufacturing ecosystem
Inter-city quantum key distribution
is a National Quantum Mission objective, not a Bio-E3 thematic sector.
Biopharma SHAKTI has an outlay of
₹10,000 crore over five years
and concerns biologics and biosimilars.
DBT’s next plans include
biomanufacturing hubs, biofoundries and Moolankur hubs

secs.t: Anusandhan National Research Foundation

x: The Prime Minister
is the ex officio President of the ANRF Governing Board.
ANRF subsumed the Science and Engineering Research Board, or
SERB
ANRF is the custodian of the ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund through a
two-tier Special Purpose Fund

secs.t: Mission → ministry + approval + outlay

x: The IndiaAI Mission is under MeitY with an outlay of ₹10,371.92 crore.
The IndiaAI Mission includes provision for more than
10,000 GPUs
NM-ICPS was approved in 2018 under DST and provides for 25 Technology Innovation Hubs.
The National Geospatial Mission is associated with DST through the Survey of India, appears in Budget 2025–26 and runs till 2031.

secs.t: AP quantum push - Amaravati Quantum Valley

x: The Amaravati NIELIT Quantum and AI campus involves ₹730.70 crore from MeitY, with classes scheduled from September 2026 at Acharya Nagarjuna University.

The #AIForAll strategy dates to 2018, the IndiaAI Mission to 2024, the NIELIT campus is associated with August 2026, and the Quantum Reference Facility test beds were opened on 14 April 2026; therefore, the order is A, B, C, D only if the campus reference is treated as August 2026.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: India-Germany quantum and deep-tech cooperation is being pursued through the Indo-German Science and Technology Centre (IGSTC) and the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF).

rows.title: Prominent Indian scientists - C.V. Raman, J.C. Bose, S.N. Bose, Ramanujan, Meghnad Saha, Homi Bhabha

secs.t: Women scientists - FIRST achievements and field

x: Anandibai Joshi became the
first Indian woman to earn a degree in Western medicine
, obtaining an M.D. from the Woman's Medical College of Pennsylvania in 1886.
Asima Chatterjee was an organic chemist who obtained the first woman D.Sc. from an Indian university in 1944 and worked on Ayush-56 and anti-malarial drugs.

secs.t: C.V. Raman - discovery, Nobel year, institutions, day commemorating

x: From 1907, C.V. Raman worked at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science outside office hours while employed in the
Accountant General's Office, Calcutta
Amrit Lal Sircar
invited C.V. Raman to work at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science.
The Bose Institute was founded in 1917, the Indian Academy of Sciences in 1934, TIFR in 1945 and the Raman Research Institute in 1948.

secs.t: Homi Bhabha - titles, institutions, programme, awards

x: The Atomic Energy Establishment at Trombay was founded in 1954 and was renamed BARC after Homi Bhabha's death in 1966.
Homi Bhabha received the Adams Prize in 1942, became a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1941, received the Padma Bhushan in 1954 and presided over the 1955 Geneva conference.

secs.t: J.C. Bose - inventions, plant-life work, institute, books

x: J.C. Bose invented the
crescograph
to measure plant growth.
J.C. Bose pioneered microwave and millimetre-wave radio research and worked with a coherer and a galena semiconductor detector.
J.C. Bose founded the Bose Institute at Kolkata in 1917.
The Nervous Mechanism of Plants
was written by J.C. Bose.
Response in the Living and Non-Living is a work of J.C. Bose.

secs.t: Srinivasa Ramanujan - works, collaborator, commemorations

x: Srinivasa Ramanujan was born on 22 December 1887 at Erode in Tamil Nadu.
Srinivasa Ramanujan worked with the British mathematician
G.H. Hardy
at Cambridge.
Thermal ionisation of elements
is associated with Meghnad Saha.
The number 1729 is known as the
Hardy-Ramanujan number

secs.t: Scientist → area of work matching

x: S.N. Bose is associated with quantum statistics and bosons.
M. Visvesvaraya, associated with engineering, served as the Diwan of Mysore from 1912 to 1919.
C.V. Raman worked on light scattering, optics and acoustics.

secs.t: Meghnad Saha - equation, principle, institute, river planning

x: The Saha equation helps interpret stellar spectra by indicating the
temperature and ionisation state of stars
Meghnad Saha invented an instrument to measure the
weight and pressure of solar rays
Meghnad Saha was regarded as the chief architect of river planning in India and prepared the original plan for the Damodar Valley Project.

secs.t: Awards and honours - Nobel, Bharat Ratna, FRS, Padma

x: C. V. Raman received the Nobel Prize in 1930, was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1954 and was knighted in 1929.
All three pairs are correctly matched.
Bhabha received the FRS in 1941 and Padma Bhushan in 1954, while S. N. Bose received Padma Vibhushan in 1954 and FRS in 1958.

secs.t: S.N. Bose - statistics and particle class, collaborator

x: S. N. Bose sent the paper to
Albert Einstein
, who translated it into German and arranged its publication.
Bose sent the paper to Einstein; Einstein translated it into German, after which it was published in Zeitschrift fur Physik in 1924.
Bose–Einstein statistics emerged from
S. N. Bose
’s work on the statistical treatment of light quanta.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: IACS was founded in Kolkata in 1876 by
Mahendra Lal Sircar
IACS is described as the oldest institute for basic research and is funded by the Department of Science and Technology and the Government of West Bengal.
Janaki Ammal and Anna Mani
are cited as women scientists who were left out of public memory.

rows.title: Prominent Indian scientists - Vikram Sarabhai, A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, M.S. Swaminathan, Har Gobind Khorana, Venkatraman Ramakrishnan, C.N.R. Rao

secs.t: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan - birthplace, Nobel, discovery, Royal Society role

x: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan is known for determining the
atomic structure of the 30S ribosomal subunit
, which provided insight into protein synthesis.
The 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Venkatraman Ramakrishnan,
Thomas A. Steitz and Ada Yonath
for studies of the ribosome.
He became an FRS in 2003, received the Padma Vibhushan in 2010 and was knighted in 2012.

secs.t: Scientist → area of work matching

x: Birbal Sahni is associated with palaeobotany, P. Maheshwari with plant embryology, K.C. Mehta with cereal rusts and G.N. Ramachandran with protein structure.
Jagdish Bhagwati is associated with economics, particularly trade, not palaeobotany.
Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar was associated with chemistry and was the founder-director of CSIR.

secs.t: Har Gobind Khorana - Nobel year, discovery, co-laureates

x: Khorana shared the 1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with
Robert W. Holley and Marshall W. Nirenberg
Khorana was recognised for interpreting the genetic code and explaining its role in protein synthesis.

secs.t: M.S. Swaminathan - Green Revolution, titles, commission, foundation, Bharat Ratna

x: Swaminathan was associated with high-yielding dwarf crops, chaired the National Commission on Farmers and founded MSSRF in Chennai.
The National Commission on Farmers was set up on
18 November 2004
and its reports came to be known as the Swaminathan report.
M.S. Swaminathan was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2024 for his contribution to agriculture.

secs.t: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam - space and missile roles, books, presidency, aircraft, awards

x: Abdul Kalam was the project director of SLV-3, which placed the Rohini satellite in orbit in 1980.
Kalam led the
Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme
, associated with missiles such as Agni, Prithvi, Akash, Trishul and Nag.
The correct order is SLV-3 placing Rohini in orbit in 1980, Pokhran-II in 1998, the beginning of Kalam’s presidency in 2002 and the renaming in 2015.

secs.t: Vikram Sarabhai - institutions, awards, facilities named after him

x: Sarabhai received the Bhatnagar Award in 1962, Padma Bhushan in 1966 and the Padma Vibhushan posthumously in 1972.
The Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station was renamed the
Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre
at Thiruvananthapuram.
The COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal, constituted in 1990 by COSPAR and ISRO, recognises
space scientists from developing countries

secs.t: C.N.R. Rao - field, Bharat Ratna, advisory roles

x: C.N.R. Rao is one of the foremost scientists in
solid-state and materials chemistry
, including structural chemistry.
C.N.R. Rao received the Bharat Ratna in 2014, headed the Scientific Advisory Council to the Prime Minister and received the Energy Frontiers Award.

secs.t: Other modern scientists → organisation led and contribution

x: K. Kasturirangan served as ISRO Chairman from 1994 to 2003 and chaired the drafting committee of NEP 2020.
Tessy Thomas of DRDO was the project director of Agni-IV and is popularly known as the “Missile Woman.”.
Satish Dhawan was associated with the launch of Aryabhata, and SHAR was renamed the Satish Dhawan Space Centre.

secs.t: Scientists from AP → discovery or field

x: Yellapragada SubbaRow was born at
Bhimavaram
Yellapragada SubbaRow contributed to understanding the role of
ATP and phosphocreatine
in muscle through the Fiske–SubbaRow method.
SubbaRow contributed to folic acid synthesis and was associated with methotrexate, aureomycin and Hetrazan.
Yelavarthy Nayudamma was a prominent scientist in
leather technology
Nayudamma died in the Kanishka bombing in 1985, not 1986.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Annapurni Subramaniam
won the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal in 2026, becoming the first Indian woman and the fourth Indian recipient.
The award was presented at the 46th COSPAR Assembly held at Florence in 2026.
The debate invoked Vikram Sarabhai, Satish Dhawan, Brahm Prakash, U.R. Rao and A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
Vikram Sarabhai
was the first Chairman of ISRO.

secs.t: Nobel laureates of Indian origin or citizenship - field, year, discovery; FIRST scientist laureate

x: Exam angle: "first Indian scientist to win Nobel" = Raman (not Khorana/Chandrasekhar); Khorana and Chandrasekhar were US citizens when awarded .
Abhijit Banerjee, along with Esther Duflo and Michael Kremer, received the 2019 Economics Nobel for
an experimental approach to alleviating global poverty
S. Chandrasekhar received the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics for theoretical studies of the physical processes governing the structure and evolution of stars, particularly white dwarfs.

secs.t: Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize - body, field, age limit, disciplines, recent awardees

x: CSIR has awarded the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize since 1958 for outstanding contributions to science.
The seven disciplines include biology, chemistry, earth/atmosphere/ocean/planetary sciences, engineering, mathematics, medicine and physics.
The former recognition now appears within the Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar framework as VY-SSB for scientists up to 45 years.
Ecologist Madhav Gadgil was associated with People's Biodiversity Registers and chaired the 2010 Gadgil Commission on the Western Ghats.

secs.t: Nobel Prize - origin, first award year, categories

x: The Nobel Prize was instituted by the will of
Alfred Nobel
, the Swedish chemist and inventor of dynamite.
The original five categories were
Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature and Peace
The Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences is awarded by the
Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded by the Norwegian Nobel Committee, and the ceremony is held in
Oslo

secs.t: Awards → field of contribution

x: The J.C. Bose Fellowship or Grant supports
science and engineering research
and is associated with ANRF.
The Infosys Prize covers engineering and computer science, humanities and social sciences, life sciences,
mathematical sciences
and physical sciences.
The COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal recognises
space research by scientists from developing countries
and has been awarded since 1990.

secs.t: S. Chandrasekhar - limit, stellar evolution, telescope named after him

x: The Chandrasekhar limit is approximately
1.4 solar masses
, the maximum mass of a stable white dwarf.
Beyond the Chandrasekhar limit, a white dwarf can collapse into a neutron star or a black hole.
Pulsars are rotating neutron stars with radiation beams, black holes trap light, and low- or medium-mass stars can end as white dwarfs.

secs.t: Mathematics, statistics and computing awards - Indian-origin winners

x: The years are Raj Reddy—1994, S.R. Srinivasa Varadhan—2007, Manjul Bhargava—2014 and C.R. Rao—2023; hence D, A, B, C. Wait, among the options this sequence is option a, not b.
Jainendra K. Jain was recognised for the
composite fermion model for the fractional quantum Hall effect
and was the first Indian-origin recipient of the Wolf Prize in Physics.

secs.t: Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar - categories, awards it replaced

x: Vigyan Yuva-SSB recognises
young scientists up to 45 years of age
The Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar replaced multiple ministry awards, incorporated the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize as Vigyan Yuva-SSB, and spans 13 domains.
Annapurni Subramaniam received the
Vigyan Shri
in 2024 for space science.
The Vigyan Ratna of the Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar 2025 was conferred posthumously.

secs.t: International science popularisation awards - Kalinga Prize Indian winners

x: The Kalinga Prize is a UNESCO prize for the
popularisation of science
The Kalinga Prize was instituted in 1952 with a donation from Biju Patnaik through the Kalinga Foundation Trust.
Jagjit Singh received it in 1963, Narender K. Sehgal in 1991, Jayant V. Narlikar in 1996 and Yash Pal in 2009.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The 2025 Padma Awards totalled 139, comprising 7 Padma Vibhushan, 19 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri awards; these awards are not titles under Article 18.
The first Nobel Prize was awarded in 1901, C. V. Raman became the first Indian scientist laureate in 1930, and the first Indian-origin Wolf Prize in Physics recipient was recorded in 2026.

units.title: Information and Communication Technology - Nature and Scope, ICT in Daily Life, ICT and Industry, ICT and Governance, Netiquettes, Cyber Security

rows.title: Nature and scope of ICT; basics of hardware, software, memory and operating systems

secs.t: Memory and storage - primary vs secondary, capacities, storage units

x: RAM temporarily stores data and instructions currently in use and loses its contents when power is removed.
EPROM
is erased by exposure to ultraviolet light, whereas EEPROM is erased electrically.
Magnetic tape
is a sequential-access medium commonly used for backup and archival purposes.
A single-layer CD stores about 700 MB, a single-layer DVD about 4.7 GB and a single-layer Blu-ray disc about 25 GB.

secs.t: Hardware - input vs output, CPU components, processors, readers, printers

x: Barcode readers read bars, MICR reads magnetic-ink characters, OMR reads marked sheets and OCR converts text into editable form.
A conventional barcode consists of
machine-readable vertical bars of varying widths
Graphics processing units are designed for highly parallel computations used in graphics and many AI workloads.
Print quality is measured in dots per inch (dpi), while speed may be expressed in pages per minute (ppm).

secs.t: Software types - system, application, utility, open-source

x: Antivirus software is a utility designed to maintain or protect the computer system.
Operating systems, disk-cleanup tools and word processors are correctly classified.
A compiler is a language translator and therefore system software; the other three are application programs.
Open-source software makes source code available for viewing, modification and sharing under the applicable licence.
LibreOffice
is an example of open-source software; Firefox is another example.

secs.t: Operating systems - functions, types, interfaces, examples

x: An operating system manages hardware resources, processes, memory, files and drivers.
Real-time operating systems are designed to respond within fixed deadlines, which is essential in such applications.
Batch systems group jobs and run them without continuous user interaction.
Time-sharing systems allocate CPU time among multiple users or processes; UNIX is an example.

secs.t: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates

x: Dennis Ritchie is associated with C, Bjarne Stroustrup with C++, James Gosling with Java and Guido van Rossum with Python.
A compiler processes the complete program before execution, while an interpreter translates and executes line by line, making debugging easier.
Pseudocode expresses program logic in an English-like form without requiring the exact syntax of a programming language.

secs.t: File formats and acronyms → expansion or type

x: MP4 stands for MPEG-4 Part 14 and is a video file format.
MP3 expands to
MPEG-1 Audio Layer 3
and is an audio format.
ASCII is a 7-bit code representing 128 characters, while Unicode extends the range of character representation.
JPEG, or Joint Photographic Experts Group, is an image format commonly associated with lossy compression.

secs.t: Computing history - generations, inventors

x: First-generation computers, broadly dating from the 1940s to 1956, used vacuum tubes.
The correct sequence is vacuum tubes, transistors, integrated circuits and microprocessors, corresponding broadly to the first through fourth generations.
The fifth generation is associated with artificial intelligence, ultra-large-scale integration and parallel processing.
“Technology preservation” is associated with a
computer museum
, where earlier technologies are retained and displayed.

secs.t: Computer performance terms - word length, bandwidth, clock speed, MIPS, FLOPS

x: Word length is the number of bits that the CPU can handle at once, such as 32-bit or 64-bit processing.
Clock speed is measured in
hertz
, commonly expressed as gigahertz (GHz).
The Linpack, or HPL, benchmark measures floating-point power in solving large dense linear systems and is used for world supercomputer rankings.

secs.t: Computer types - analog, digital, hybrid, PC, supercomputer, quantum

x: Analog
computers or systems represent continuous quantities; speedometers and thermometers are examples.
Param Shakti at IIT Madras was launched by MeitY, has 3.1 petaflops capacity, uses C-DAC RUDRA servers and runs open-source AlmaLinux.
Q-Day denotes the anticipated point when quantum computers can break RSA-2048 public-key encryption through Shor’s algorithm, proposed in 1994.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: ICT covers devices and applications used to
access, store, transmit and manipulate digital information
, including mobiles, networks, software, the internet and satellites.
Privacy risks, the digital divide, job insecurity and over-reliance on technology are identified concerns.
ICT aims at efficient human-human, human-machine and machine-to-machine communication.

rows.title: Networks and the internet - LAN/WAN, protocols, IP, DNS, web technologies

secs.t: Web technologies - HTML tags, web server vs browser vs search engine, URL, WWW, W3C, Web 3.0

x: Exam angle: "which one displays webpages" (browser) vs "which one stores them" (server).
The server stores and serves pages, the browser displays them, and the search engine indexes them for discovery.
W3C develops and maintains web standards so that webpages function consistently across different browsers.
The dark web is a small hidden subset of the deep web and is associated with anonymous access through tools such as Tor or I2P.
The deep web accounts for approximately 90–95%, the surface web about 4–5%, and the dark web is a small hidden subset.

secs.t: Internet history - ARPANET, WWW inventor, first Indian ISPs

x: ARPANET was developed under the
United States Department of Defense
in 1969 and became the forerunner of the Internet.
ERNET began in 1986, public internet was launched by VSNL on 15 August 1995, and Satyam Infoway became the first private ISP in 1998.
ERNET
was India’s academic network established in 1986.

secs.t: IP and MAC addressing - IPv4 vs IPv6, MAC length, notation, classes

x: IPv6 is 128 bits long and is written as eight hexadecimal groups separated by colons.
A MAC address is a 48-bit physical address, equal to 6 bytes or 12 hexadecimal digits, generally burnt into the network card and used at the data link layer.
DNS acts as the Internet’s directory by translating human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses.

secs.t: Wireless standards - Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi bands and versions, 2.4 GHz devices

x: Bluetooth class 2 devices have a short range of approximately 10 metres, while Wi-Fi generally covers a larger area.
Li-Fi transmits data using LED light and is described as offering better bandwidth and security than Wi-Fi.
Wi-Fi Direct enables compatible devices to communicate directly without being connected through a conventional local area network.

secs.t: Protocols → function; protocol elements

x: Within
TCP
/IP, TCP ensures reliable delivery, while IP addresses and routes packets.
HTTP transfers webpages, while HTTPS encrypts browser-server traffic using TLS.
IMAP
keeps mail on the server and synchronises it across devices.
Syntax specifies the format of data, semantics specifies the meaning of each field, and timing specifies when and how fast data is sent.

secs.t: Network types and topologies - PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN

x: PAN
stands for Personal Area Network and connects an individual's nearby devices, commonly through Bluetooth.
A Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) generally covers
a city
, placing it between a LAN and a WAN in geographical extent.
In a star topology, all nodes depend on the central hub or switch; its failure can stop the entire network.

secs.t: Internet governance - ICANN, NIXI and .in, Universal Acceptance, IDNs (BhashaNet)

x: NIXI was established in 2003, functions as a not-for-profit organisation under MeitY, and runs Internet exchange points, the .in registry and IRINN.
Universal Acceptance ensures that applications and e-mail systems correctly accept all valid domain names and e-mail IDs, including IDNs.
BhashaNet promotes Universal Acceptance and the use of Indian-language Internet domain names and e-mail IDs; it is associated with MeitY-NIXI and the year 2022.

secs.t: Network devices and transmission - router, switch, hub, modem, duplex, DSL/cable/fibre

x: A hub broadcasts to all ports, a switch forwards frames by MAC address, a router routes using IP, and a modem converts between digital and analogue signals.

The Presentation layer handles encryption, compression and formats; the Session layer opens and closes sessions; the Transport layer uses TCP and UDP; and the Data Link layer handles MAC-based frame operations.

secs.t: OSI model - seven layers → protocols/devices

x: Exam angle: device-to-layer matching (switch = 2, router = 3).
From the top layer downward, the OSI model is Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link and Physical.
A modem is associated with the Physical layer because it modulates and demodulates signals; it is not a Transport-layer device.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: ISPs may block sites through DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering on HTTPS.
Internet connections increased from 25.15 crore in 2014 to 96.96 crore in 2024.
BharatNet fibre reaches approximately
2.18 lakh
gram panchayats according to the stated 2025–26 figure.
The discussion concerned
last-mile connectivity, data centres and an undersea cable landing station
for Andhra Pradesh.

rows.title: ICT in day-to-day life - mobile telephony, social media, e-commerce, digital media

secs.t: Social media - platforms → founder/parent, content terms

x: LinkedIn was founded by
Reid Hoffman
in 2003 and is used mainly for professional networking.
SMO stands for Social Media Optimisation and involves
raising reach through social platforms
LinkedIn was founded in 2003, Facebook in 2004, LinkedIn came under Microsoft ownership in 2016, and Twitter was renamed X in 2023.

secs.t: Mobile telephony - first handheld call, SIM, MNP, Android, QR, NFC, market rank

x: QR means Quick Response; Denso Wave designed the codes in Japan in 1994 for the car industry, and phone cameras can read them quickly.
NFC works over a few centimetres, supports approximately 106–424 kbps, and generally offers easier pairing and lower power use than Bluetooth.
The Reserve Bank of India allowed offline UPI Lite payments over NFC.

secs.t: Mobile applications by sector - m-health, m-agriculture, m-learning, m-governance

x: Agrimarket uses GPS, obtains data from Agmarknet, covers markets within 50 km, and provides information in English and Hindi.
The
Sugamya Bharat
app crowdsources reports of inaccessible places and belongs to the m-governance sector.
Agrimarket is an m-agriculture application. eSanjeevani provides telemedicine, Tele-MANAS concerns tele-mental health, and Doctor on Demand is a US health application.

secs.t: Digital media and multimedia - components, e-journals, editing software, TV broadcasting

x: Multimedia may contain text, images or graphics, audio, video and animation.
Adobe Premiere Pro
is video-editing software; Apple Final Cut Pro is another example.
Terrestrial broadcasting
is a traditional television broadcasting method.
ANI, established in 1971, was the first Indian news agency to offer syndicated video news.

secs.t: Digital-age disorders and terms

x: Digital detox
means taking a deliberate break from digital devices.
Doomscrolling
refers to endless scrolling through bad or distressing news.
Cyberchondria
is health anxiety fed by online searches for symptoms and diseases.
FOMO
stands for the fear of missing out on what others are doing online.
The
World Health Organization
lists Gaming Disorder in ICD-11.

secs.t: State initiatives on screen and gaming addiction

x: Karnataka
introduced the ‘Digital Detox Centre – Beyond Screens’ initiative.
D-DAD stands for
Digital De-Addiction
centres operated by Kerala Police.
Agmarknet is related to agricultural market information.
A plan exists to widen Tele-MANAS to cover
digital addiction
as part of central measures addressing technology use.

secs.t: E-commerce - models, FDI, Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020

x: B2B denotes business-to-business transactions, B2C business-to-consumer transactions, C2C consumer-to-consumer transactions, and D2C direct brand-to-consumer sales.
The beta testing of ONDC took place in
Bengaluru
The stated textbook position permits 100% FDI under the automatic route in the marketplace model but does not permit FDI in the inventory model.
The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 were framed under the
Consumer Protection Act, 2019

secs.t: E-mail and video conferencing - address parts, attachments, components

x: SMTP is used for sending e-mail.
BCC
, or blind carbon copy, sends copies while hiding the recipients' addresses from one another.

secs.t: Digital platforms regulation - IT Rules 2021, Online Gaming Act 2025, gig workers

x: The IT Rules, 2021 cover social media, OTT and digital news platforms, and contain both a Code of Ethics and a three-tier grievance redressal mechanism.
The 2023 amendment links failure to comply with government orders on false content with loss of safe-harbour protection under
Section 79
of the IT Act.
The draft dated 30 March 2026 proposed enabling the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting to send takedown notices to individual users.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The DPDP Act treats anyone below
18 years
as a child and requires verifiable parental consent for processing the child's personal data.
The proposed approach favours graded limits based on age instead of imposing a blanket ban on all persons below a specified age.
Australia
introduced the world's first nationwide under-16 social-media ban, effective from 10 December 2025.

secs.t: Robotics - types, Indian robots → developer + purpose, standards bodies

x: Daksh was developed by DRDO as a remotely operated robot for
handling and defusing IEDs and bombs
Bandicoot is a robot designed for
sewer and manhole cleaning
and seeks to end manual scavenging.
A MeitY inter-ministerial committee comprising representatives of DoT, DSIR, DST, DPIIT and NITI Aayog is drafting the strategy.

secs.t: Internet of Things - full form, layers, applications

x: IoT consists of sensor-equipped devices connected through networks that exchange data without human intervention.
The perception layer contains devices such as sensors and RFID systems that collect information from the physical environment.
The MeitY-NASSCOM IoT Centres of Excellence are located at
Bengaluru, Gurugram, Gandhinagar and Visakhapatnam
mMTC means massive machine-type communication and is intended to support dense IoT sensor deployments in 5G networks.

secs.t: Industrial revolutions 1.0 to 4.0, Industry 5.0, SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0

x: Industry 1.0 involved steam-powered mechanisation; Industry 2.0 electricity and mass production; Industry 3.0 computers and electronics; and Industry 4.0 cyber-physical systems.
Klaus Schwab, founder of the World Economic Forum
, coined the term ‘Fourth Industrial Revolution’ in 2016.
SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0, meaning Smart Advanced Manufacturing and Rapid Transformation Hub, is a Ministry of Heavy Industries initiative that promotes Industry 4.0 through demonstration centres.

secs.t: RFID and wearables - passive vs active tags, wearable functions

x: An active RFID tag has its own battery and transmitter, broadcasts by itself and generally offers a longer range.
A semi-passive tag’s battery powers its chip, but it still uses the reader’s field to send its response.
Wearables track health and fitness indicators, support biometric authentication and function as typical IoT end-devices.

secs.t: Extended reality - VR, AR, MR, metaverse

x: The metaverse is a persistent and shared 3D virtual space that uses extended reality, avatars and digital assets.
Pokémon Go overlays digital elements on the real-world environment and is therefore an example of
Augmented Reality
The IMAGE CoE is located at Hyderabad and focuses on gaming, visual effects, computer vision and artificial intelligence.

secs.t: Semiconductor Mission - fabs/OSAT → state, indigenous chips → developer

x: The stated support levels are 40% for CMOS silicon fabs, 35% for compound/display fabs, 35% for advanced OSAT/ATMP and 25% for conventional packaging.
The reported figures are 24 design startups, 122 academic tape-outs, 56 chips fabricated at 180 nm, and 397 universities reached by Chips to Startup.
DHRUV64 was developed by C-DAC, SHAKTI by IIT Madras, AJIT by IIT Bombay and Vikram 3201 by ISRO’s Semi-Conductor Laboratory, Chandigarh.

secs.t: Drones and UAVs - types, swarms, rules, PLI, Kisan drones, Namo Drone Didi, AP

x: A drone swarm consists of many drones coordinated through software and may be used for surveillance, light shows or strikes.
The measures include liberalised Drone Rules, 2021, DigitalSky, PLI, Drone Shakti, DGCA-approved training institutes and Bharat Drone Mahotsav.
Sri Sathya Sai district
, near Bengaluru, was offered for aerospace, drone and semiconductor manufacturing.

secs.t: 3D printing - additive manufacturing, applications

x: Additive manufacturing builds objects layer by layer from a digital CAD model, whereas subtractive machining removes material.
4D printing adds materials designed to change shape over time.
Additive manufacturing is one of the course areas under
FutureSkills PRIME
3D printing is used for prosthetics and implants, bio-printed tissues, rapid construction and defence spares.

secs.t: Automation terms - PLC, SCADA, digital twin, cyber-physical systems, cobots

x: PLC controls machines as a rugged industrial computer; SCADA enables remote monitoring; a digital twin is a virtual replica; and a cobot works collaboratively with humans.
A
digital twin
is a virtual replica of a physical object or system used for simulation and monitoring.
A cyber-physical system integrates computing closely with physical processes and is a core element of Industry 4.0 and the NM-ICPS mission.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The proposed centre in Andhra Pradesh would be India’s third, after the centres in Mumbai and Telangana.
The criticism is that automation and AI can replace both intellectual and manual work, thereby raising concerns about job displacement.

secs.t: AI concepts - narrow vs general AI, ML, DL, NLP, generative AI, LLMs, recommenders, AI hardware

x: Natural Language Processing, or NLP, enables machines to
understand and generate human language
and supports chatbots and translation.
LLMs are general-purpose models trained on massive datasets and can perform multiple language tasks without task-specific retraining.
A GPU is the massively parallel workhorse of AI training, an FPGA is field-programmable and reconfigurable, and a TPU is Google's AI chip.

secs.t: AI tools, chatbots and assistants → developer

x: Pratham was developed by Assert AI, Hanooman is associated with the BharatGPT ecosystem and Seetha Mahalakshmi Healthcare, Krutrim with Ola, and OpenHathi with Sarvam AI.
Bhashini is linked to MeitY and the National Language Translation Mission, was launched in July 2022, covers 22 scheduled languages and uses crowdsourcing through Bhasha Daan.

secs.t: AI applications - agriculture in AP, health, anti-drone, facial recognition

x: The Microsoft–ICRISAT AI sowing application was piloted in
Kurnool
district in 2016 to provide yield-oriented sowing advisories.
AI-based reading of X-rays, MRI and CT scans could reduce diagnostic errors by up to
40 percent
The AI4AP Police Project is being piloted in
Chittoor, Guntur and Annamayya
for traffic management, crime prediction and investigation.

secs.t: National AI strategy and compute - NITI strategy, IndiaAI pillars, AIRAWAT, hubs

x: Compute Capacity provides affordable GPU compute, the Innovation Centre develops indigenous foundation models and LMMs, the Datasets Platform provides public-sector datasets, and FutureSkills supports courses and labs.
The IndiaAI Mission was launched in 2024 with an outlay of ₹10,371.92 crore and includes sovereign compute of more than 10,000 GPUs, AI start-ups, Indian datasets and foundation models.

secs.t: Ethical concerns - bias, deepfakes, privacy, facial recognition, jobs, explainability

x: Predictive policing raises concern when algorithmic predictions threaten due process or influence policing without adequate safeguards.
Deep models are often described as ‘black boxes’;
explainability
concerns the ability to understand and justify their decisions.
Deepfakes can occur as text, voice, image or video, and facial-recognition accuracy can vary with lighting and pose.

secs.t: AI education and challenges - first AI degrees, AP university, competitions

x: The NIELIT campus is a MeitY-linked deemed-university initiative, described as India’s first dedicated Quantum and AI university campus, with 8.5 acres and a ₹730.70 crore five-year grant.
Classes are scheduled to begin in September 2026 at a temporary site in
Acharya Nagarjuna University, Guntur
GPU shortages, dependence on imported chips and a shortage of frontier-AI skills are all identified as challenges.

secs.t: Global AI governance - summits → host city, GPAI, EU AI Act

x: India is a founding member of GPAI, joined it on 15 June 2020 and was elected Incoming Council Chair.
The EU AI Act sorts AI systems into unacceptable, high, limited and minimal risk categories. ‘
Unlimited risk
’ is not one of those categories.
Deepfakes are synthetic media, while drone swarms involve coordinated autonomous drones.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The issue concerned the lack of a statutory framework for high-risk AI used in
welfare delivery
The criticism is expressed as ‘safety is declining, and big money is on the rise’, indicating a shift from safety emphasis towards scale and investment.
The Economic Survey 2025–26 favours
small, application-specific models and a state-built AI-OS modelled on UPI and Aadhaar

secs.t: AI - pioneers and core terms

x: John McCarthy is regarded as the father of AI and coined the term at the Dartmouth Conference in 1956.
The Turing test examines whether a machine’s responses can be distinguished from human replies.
LLMs are trained on very large collections of text and are designed to generate or process language.
GPUs are well suited to parallel computation, while FPGAs can be reprogrammed for customised acceleration.

secs.t: AI applications and platforms in India → developer

x: CAIR is a DRDO laboratory dealing with AI and robotics and is located in Bengaluru.
The three Centres of Excellence concern Healthcare, Agriculture and Sustainable Cities.
NM-ICPS
Technology Innovation Hubs
include AI and machine-learning verticals.

secs.t: Quantum computing - qubit, superposition, entanglement, supremacy

x: Entanglement sudden death denotes abrupt total loss of entanglement, and the Raman Research Institute demonstrated that a suitably timed local quantum flip could delay or prevent it.
Quantum computing has applications in cryptography, drug discovery, climate modelling and optimisation;
manual typesetting
is not among them.
Q-Day denotes the future point when quantum computing becomes capable of breaking widely used public-key cryptography.

secs.t: Nanotechnology and advanced materials → developer

x: The spherical C60 fullerene molecule is commonly called a
buckyball
Kevlar is an aramid fibre widely associated with bullet-proof protective vests.

IIT Mandi developed the biodegradable nanoparticles; IISc Bengaluru worked on carbon-nanotube transistors; C-DAC on graphene flexible electronics; and IIT Delhi on perovskite displays and conductive nanofibres.
DRDO’s DYSL-Smart Materials is located in Hyderabad, not Bengaluru.

The NIELIT Quantum and AI campus at Amaravati is associated with an area of
8.5 acres

rows.title: Big data, cloud computing, edge computing and data centres

secs.t: Big data - Vs, data mining, data warehouse, metadata, data lake

x: A data warehouse
is a central repository of cleaned, structured data used for analysis and reporting.
A data lake stores raw data in its native format and may contain structured as well as unstructured data.
India is a member of the UN Committee of Experts on Big Data and Data Science and holds a seat on its Advisory Board.

secs.t: Cloud computing - service and deployment models, cloud storage → company

x: SaaS delivers ready-to-use software over the web; such software may be accessible on mobile and may allow customisation of the user interface and fields.
MeghRaj or GI Cloud is the Government of India's cloud initiative, hosting e-services on the NIC cloud and promoting interoperability and security standards.
On-demand self-service, ubiquitous network access, metered use, elasticity and resource pooling are the five stated characteristics of cloud computing.

secs.t: Data analytics for environment and governance - large datasets with AI and quantum computing

x: Together, these technologies can analyse large datasets, predict pollution, optimise resource use and support governance decisions.
eTaal 3.0 recorded more than 4,451 e-services and 21,206.13 crore e-transactions in July 2025.
The MoSPI units specifically identified are the Data Innovation Lab and the Research and Analysis Division.
The Economic Survey 2025–26 refers to
UDISE+, AISHE and ABDM
surveys combined with AI to identify health hotspots.

secs.t: Edge vs fog vs cloud computing - latency, use cases

x: Edge processing occurs on or near the device, fog operates between the edge and cloud, and cloud processing occurs in distant centralised data centres.
Edge computing
processes data on or near the device and therefore provides the lowest latency for real-time applications.
Fog computing provides an intermediate layer between edge devices and the cloud, especially when edge devices lack adequate processing power.

secs.t: Serverless computing, virtualisation, containers - terms

x: Virtualisation allows one physical server to run multiple virtual machines, with each virtual machine having its own operating system.
Containers package an application with its dependencies and share the host OS kernel; Docker is an example.
In serverless computing, the provider manages and scales the servers, while the developer writes functions and is billed according to usage.

secs.t: Data centres - policy, tiers, energy and water, capacity hubs

x: All four statements reflect proposals in the draft National Data Centre Policy: a 20-year tax holiday, GST input credit on capital assets, Permanent Establishment status for qualifying foreign firms, and location and renewable-energy incentives.
Data centres consume about 1% of global electricity, cooling requires substantial water, and DeepMind AI cut Google's data-centre energy use by up to 40%.

secs.t: Data governance - NDGF, India Datasets Programme, open government data

x: The policy established the India Data Management Office and the India Datasets Programme for anonymised non-personal data.
The OGD Platform India was launched under the National Data Sharing and Accessibility Policy (NDSAP) in 2012 and provides free datasets.
The platform held more than 2.34 lakh dataset APIs and 3,471 visualisations as of 31 July 2025.
The IndiaAI Datasets Platform is also referred to as
AI-Kosh

secs.t: Data centre and AI hub investments in AP (Visakhapatnam) → company

x: AP-Transco has counted 16 projects with about 9.10 GW of IT load and plans a 765/400/220 kV grid to carry more than 15 GW by 2034.
Nara Lokesh
set a policy for developing multi-gigawatt data-centre capacity along the Vizag–Kapuluppada corridor.
The identified advantages are a submarine cable landing station, sea-breeze cooling, Seismic Zone II and nearness to Southeast Asia.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Economic Survey 2025–26 links rising data-centre capacity with cloud computing, artificial intelligence, IoT and 5G.
Hyperscale data centres raise concerns about power and water strain, while India also relies on foreign cloud providers for AI compute.
Data centres are criticised for their pressure on power and water resources, while India is noted as lacking a binding data-centre sustainability policy.
