rows.title: Blockchain and distributed ledger technology; cryptocurrency and CBDC (e-rupee)

secs.t: Blockchain terms - distributed ledger, block, hash, node, immutability, consensus

x: A blockchain is a time-stamped series of immutable records managed by a cluster of computers rather than a single owner.
A
distributed ledger
is a shared ledger replicated across many nodes without a central validator.
A node is a computer that holds a copy of the blockchain ledger.
Consensus
is the rule or mechanism through which nodes agree on valid transactions.

secs.t: Blockchain types and features - public/private, permissioned/permissionless, visibility

x: Public or permissionless blockchains are open to anyone, while private or permissioned blockchains admit only authorised entities.
Bitcoin represents the public/permissionless model, while private/permissioned systems may be controlled by an organisation or consortium; AP DigiVerify is an example cited for the latter.
Relevant stakeholders can be given visibility while replicated copies and consensus protect the records from unauthorised alteration.

secs.t: Cryptocurrency - Bitcoin creator, tracking and regulation, VDA taxation

x: Bitcoin was introduced in 2009 by the pseudonymous creator
Satoshi Nakamoto
Cryptocurrency is decentralised and peer-to-peer, uses keys and wallets, and may use mining for validation.
Stablecoins are pegged to fiat, commodities or crypto-assets in an attempt to provide relative price stability.
Virtual digital asset service providers were brought under the PMLA in
March 2023
Turkmenistan
legalised cryptocurrency mining using gas-based power.

secs.t: NFTs, smart contracts, Web 3.0, DeFi - terms

x: NFTs are unique tokens and can represent physical assets digitally.
Smart contracts are self-executing code deployed on a blockchain.
Smart contracts can reduce intermediaries and monitor supply chains.
DeFi provides services such as lending and trading through smart contracts without relying on banks.
Tokenisation
converts ownership rights in an asset into a blockchain token.

secs.t: Consensus mechanisms - proof of work vs proof of stake

x: Proof of Work uses puzzle-solving miners, while Proof of Stake selects validators based on staked coins.
Bitcoin is associated with
Proof of Work
, in which miners solve complex computational puzzles.
Ethereum's move to Proof of Stake in September 2022 was called '
The Merge

secs.t: Applications - land records, supply chain, certificates, voting, health records

x: Unregulated creation of sovereign currency
is not one of them.
The Distributed Centre of Excellence in Blockchain includes C-DAC, IDRBT Hyderabad and VJTI Mumbai.
The Centre produced a property-registration pilot in
Shamshabad, Telangana
The Centre produced a Proof-of-Existence framework for
certificates
Drunix is an open-source private blockchain re-engineered from Hyperledger Fabric.

secs.t: National Strategy on Blockchain - publisher, Vishvasya stack

x: The National Strategy on Blockchain was published by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology in
December 2021
NeGD
had earlier released an approach paper related to blockchain before the National Strategy was published.
Vishvasya was introduced in 2024, is hosted across NIC data centres and builds on the National Blockchain Framework.

secs.t: AP blockchain pilots - land records and e-governance

x: The Mee Bhoomi-Blockchain pilot was launched by Chief Minister Naidu on 23 July 2026.
AP DigiVerify is a permissioned-blockchain PaaS designed for tamper-proof certificate verification.

The issue of tamper-proof pattadar passbooks under Mee Bhoomi-Mee Hakku was reported on
10 April 2026

x: However, the reported reduction in Andhra Pradesh land disputes does not constitute the stated reason for the Supreme Court's suggestion.

Optical fibre
provides faster data transmission than copper cable, radio waves and satellite signals.
NOFN was funded by USOF, used GPON technology, relied on fibre of BSNL, RailTel and Power Grid, and had an estimated cost of Rs 20,000 crore.

secs.t: Telecom bodies - role (DoT, TRAI, TDSAT, C-DOT, TEC), 1980s reforms, EMF limits for towers

settle disputes and hear appeals against TRAI

India’s tower EMF limits since 2012 are set at
one-tenth
of the ICNIRP limits.

secs.t: Mobile generations 1G-6G - core technology, speed, GSM family terms

x: 2G was digital and supported GSM/CDMA and SMS, while 3G used CDMA-based technologies such as WCDMA and CDMA2000.
GPRS is associated with 2.5G and EDGE with 2.75G, both representing faster GSM data developments.
LTE and OFDMA are associated with 4G, and VoLTE denotes voice carried over the LTE data network.

secs.t: Li-Fi and Visible Light Communication - full form, medium, vs Wi-Fi

x: All four statements correctly describe Li-Fi, including its LED-based optical transmission, the origin of the term and its stated advantages over Wi-Fi.
FSO communication sends data through laser or light beams without using fibre cables.
The reported link was the world’s first 2 Tbit/s free-space optical link, using small terminals for satellites and high-altitude platform stations.

secs.t: 5G - spectrum bands, network slicing, uses, indigenous stack, launch, hackathons

x: TRAI prefers Cellular Vehicle-to-Everything (
C-V2X
) for vehicle communication over the stated 4G/5G alternatives.
TTDF was introduced in 2022, receives 5% of Digital Bharat Nidhi collections—about Rs 500 crore annually—and has funded 5G Stack, 6G and quantum-encryption projects.
Andhra Pradesh has an Industry Policy 4.0, IIITDM Kurnool topped the stated 5G Use Case Labs assessment, and Efftronics with JNTU Kakinada launched an industry-sponsored M.Tech in IoT.

secs.t: Wireless and alternative access - WLAN, RFID, CCTV, Project Loon, PM-WANI, Wi-Fi 6/7

x: NFC is a very short-range wireless communication technology, generally operating over a distance of
a few centimetres
Project Loon attempted to deliver internet connectivity using
high-altitude balloons
Google/Alphabet's Project Loon, which used high-altitude balloons for internet access, was shut down in 2021.
The number of PM-WANI public Wi-Fi hotspots mapped on the Gati Shakti National Master Plan platform was
3.15 lakh

secs.t: 6G - Bharat 6G Vision, Bharat 6G Alliance, target year

x: The Bharat 6G Vision document was released in March 2023 and aims for India to lead the design, development and deployment of 6G by 2030.
The Bharat 6G Alliance brings together public and private firms, academia and standards bodies.
The Bharat 6G Alliance has signed MoUs with
global 6G alliances
to promote cooperation in the development of next-generation communications.

secs.t: Spectrum - auctions, Telecommunications Act 2023, satellite spectrum

x: TRAI recommended auctioning all available spectrum across nine bands, a uniform 35% spectrum cap, and reducing the new-entrant net-worth requirement from Rs 100 crore to Rs 50 crore per service area.
The Department of Telecommunications rule requires all telecom data and logs of infrastructure providers to be stored
in India

secs.t: Satellite communication - GEO vs LEO (Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper), GMPCS

x: The
GSAT series
is cited as an example of GEO satellites, and GSAT-7 and GSAT-7A are associated with defence applications.
Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb and Amazon Kuiper
are identified as LEO constellations.
Approximately
20–25 percent
of Indians live in areas that are difficult to reach through terrestrial networks, highlighting the importance of satellite connectivity.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Chief Minister directed telecom operators to complete new towers within 100 days.
The fibre-optic network reviewed by the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister was for
Amaravati
India rose to 49th in the Network Readiness Index 2024 from 60th earlier.

rows.title: Emerging ICT applications - AI, big data, cloud, blockchain, IoT and 5G
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-19

secs.t: Terms and full forms (IoT, IIoT, SaaS, PaaS, IaaS, NFT, DLT, RFID, Li-Fi, 5G NR, Web 3.0)

x: Exam angle: "What does IoT stand for?" - Internet of Things.
RFID stands for Radio Frequency Identification and uses
tags and readers communicating through radio waves
Li-Fi means Light Fidelity, uses LEDs for data transmission and is noted for better bandwidth and security than Wi-Fi.
Wi-Fi 7 is based on IEEE 802.11be, supports Multi-Link Operation and is specified with speeds up to 46 Gbps.

secs.t: IoT - layers, smart agriculture and smart city uses, wearables

x: The three layers are perception, which uses sensors; network, which transmits data; and application, which provides user services.
Traffic monitoring, air-quality monitoring and waste collection are examples of smart-city IoT applications.
Fitness trackers and health monitors are wearable IoT devices.
Smart grids, logistics tracking and smart buildings
, including HVAC systems, are additional IoT applications.

secs.t: Blockchain - features, tokenization, governance uses

x: Blockchain is characterised by a decentralised distributed ledger, immutability and transparency.
Tokenization can create NFTs representing unique digital assets and tokens representing real-world assets such as land and bonds.
Blockchain governance uses include land records, digital certificates and farm insurance, among others.
E-Notary is described as a
blockchain e-Sign
application.

secs.t: Other digital technologies - digital twin, metaverse, facial recognition, RFID, AR/VR, edge computing

x: Augmented Reality overlays digital information on the real world, while Virtual Reality provides a fully simulated environment.
The metaverse is a shared immersive virtual world that uses AR and VR technologies.
Edge computing processes data near its source, which can reduce latency, save bandwidth and support privacy.
Fog computing occupies an intermediate position between edge devices and cloud computing.

secs.t: 5G - generations, features, hackathons, indigenous stack, Bharat 6G Vision

x: 5G can provide latency as low as 1 millisecond, massive device connectivity and high reliability.
Network slicing creates multiple virtual networks over one physical network using Software-Defined Networking and Network Functions Virtualization.
The recognised categories are eMBB, URLLC and mMTC. eMBB means enhanced Mobile Broadband, not exclusive Mobile Blockchain.
Airtel's ‘Priority Postpaid’ offering raised a debate on
net neutrality

secs.t: Big data - defining Vs, analytics in governance

x: Visibility
is not included in that list.
Veracity refers to the reliability, accuracy or trustworthiness of data within the big-data framework.
The AP State Data Lake cross-links RCH health data with POSHAN data and housing data with land pattas to help plug leakages.
I4C's NCAP uses AI and big data to analyse
crime trends

secs.t: Fourth Industrial Revolution - technologies grouped

x: Artificial intelligence, robotics, the Internet of Things and quantum computing are identified with the Fourth Industrial Revolution.
Smart factories use
cyber-physical systems
that integrate physical production processes with digital technologies.
All three statements correctly describe the principal technological bases of the First, Second and Third Industrial Revolutions.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: IIITDM Kurnool
topped the Department of Telecommunications’ 5G labs ranking in July 2026.
Network slicing has generated a debate concerning its compatibility with
net neutrality
Facial recognition is associated with privacy concerns, while network slicing is associated with the net-neutrality debate; both are identified as important ICT debates.
The Andhra Pradesh–Google AI/cloud task force concerns
artificial intelligence and cloud
technologies.

sub: Group-II M2-B-18: Digital India Mission - pillars, key initiatives and impact

secs.t: MMPs in news - Passport Seva, MCA21, eCourts, e-District, CCTNS, e-Procurement

x: MCA21 is a Ministry of Corporate Affairs initiative for online company filing and is a G2B service.
e-Procurement uses
online tenders
, which are intended to help prevent collusion.
IVFRT is run by the Bureau of Immigration with
NIC
The e-Panchayat MMP provides
core panchayat software
under the Panchayati Raj domain.
The GS NIRNAY app covers Gram Sabha decisions and is associated with the e-Panchayat initiative.

secs.t: Implementing bodies - NIC, NeGD, MeitY, CSC e-Governance Services

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2017 key gave
NITI Aayog
for the drive to make 100% of G2C transactions digital.
The NeGP was drafted by DeitY, now MeitY, with the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (
DARPG
NeGD, or National e-Governance Division, is
MeitY’s programme-management arm under Digital India Corporation
CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd. is the special purpose vehicle and implementing agency of CSCs.

secs.t: e-Kranti - principles, MMP count, relation to NeGP

x: Mobile first, language localisation, process re-engineering in every MMP and cloud by default are all stated principles of e-Kranti.
All three statements correctly describe e-Kranti, which was approved in 2015, became a Digital India pillar and adopted the stated tagline.
All four statements correctly describe e-Kranti, including its status as NeGP 2.0, approval in March 2015, 44 MMPs and its stated vision.

secs.t: NeGP - approval, components, MMP categories

x: The three tiers are CSCs at the front end, SWAN as the network, and SDC at the back end.
CSCs are the front-end village ICT kiosks operated by local entrepreneurs.
Land Records and e-District are State MMPs, while eCourts is an Integrated MMP.
Meghraj is the
GI Cloud
component associated with NeGP.

secs.t: E-governance concepts - models, four pillars, Gartner phases, benefits vs challenges

x: MCA portal and GSTN provide Government-to-Business services, represented by
G2B
NIC solutions serving government departments represent Government-to-Government interaction, or
G2G
Online HR tools for employees fall under the Government-to-Employee model, or
G2E
Online fraud
is a challenge of e-governance; data costs and funding gaps in some States are also identified challenges.

secs.t: Digital India - nine pillars, three vision areas, launch

x: Exam angle: "not a pillar" options are usually initiatives (Aadhaar, DigiLocker, UPI) or look-alike names.
Electronic Governance, National Knowledge Network, Cyber Security and the
IndiaAI Mission
are included among the stated Digital India sub-schemes.
Digital India is an umbrella programme preferring PPP, seeks a knowledge-based economy and digitally empowered society, and is associated with the expression “IT + IT = IT”.
Early Harvest Programmes comprise quick-win projects such as biometric attendance and Wi-Fi in universities; they are not defined as long-term university research grants.

secs.t: Digital divide - rural connectivity, language (Bhashini), accessibility

x: Rural digital gaps particularly concern Gram Panchayat fibre connectivity through BharatNet and 4G coverage in villages.
Bhashini is
an AI language platform integrated with NIC tools such as CollabFiles
, supporting access to services in Indian languages.
Vision Area 3
aims at universal digital literacy.

secs.t: Key initiatives → launch sequence

x: Exam angle: chronology Aadhaar → MyGov → PM eVIDYA → ONDC (APPSC 2024 key: 1-2-3-4).
Exam angle: APPSC 2024 asked the order Aadhaar → MyGov → PM eVIDYA → ONDC.
The DBT pilot began in 2013, MyGov was launched in 2014, Digital India/DigiLocker in 2015, ABDM in 2021 and ONDC in 2022.

secs.t: Digital education platforms → purpose + coverage

x: SWAYAM
provides free massive open online courses for higher education, including courses from IITs, IIMs and central universities.
DIKSHA is the national school e-content repository and includes QR-coded textbooks and teacher training.
PM eVIDYA uses the One Class, One TV Channel approach through DTH, radio and podcasts, and integrates DIKSHA and SWAYAM.

secs.t: India Stack and DPI - UPI-BHIM, DigiLocker, Aarogya Setu, CoWIN, Bhashini, BhashaNet

x: India Stack consists of open and interoperable public digital rails, including Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker, CoWIN, ONDC and Account Aggregator.
Aadhaar is the identity layer, UPI is the payments layer, and DEPA or Account Aggregator is the consent-based data layer.
DigiLocker had
56.06 crore users and 970.70 crore documents
DigiLocker provided an initial capacity of 10 MB, extendable to
1 GB

secs.t: Impact indicators - internet, UPI volumes, digital literacy (PMGDISHA)

x: UPI transaction volume increased approximately
over the stated period, during which UPI became 10 years old.
Approximately
500 million
people came online during 2016–2021 as data costs fell from about 4 dollars to under 30 cents per GB.
PMGDISHA is a rural digital literacy scheme launched in 2017, with the aim of covering one person per household.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A Singapore delegation studied Andhra Pradesh's RTGS Data Lake and Command Centre.
Andhra Pradesh pioneered e-Seva under the
SMART governance model
The identified concerns include the digital divide, shared devices in rural areas and data privacy.
DPI was reported to have raised the digital economy's share to approximately
of GDP.

rows.title: National Policy on Information Technology - objectives and outcomes
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-20

secs.t: National Policy on Information Technology 2012 - vision, key objectives

x: The twin goals were universal access to the benefits of ICT and making India a global hub and destination for IT and ITES services by 2020.
The policy sought to spread IT activity to Tier II and Tier III cities because the major established hubs were highly concentrated and nearing saturation.
Digital India, Aadhaar, UPI, BharatNet and DigiLocker are all identified as initiatives that put the policy vision into practice.

secs.t: Policy targets → revenue, exports, skilled manpower, e-literacy

x: Exam angle: match target figure to category; "$300 bn by 2020" is the most-asked figure.
The policy target was to raise IT-ITES revenue from US$100 billion in 2012 to
US$300 billion by 2020
IT-ITES revenue was targeted at US$300 billion; IT exports at US$200 billion; skilled manpower at 10 million additional workers; and e-literacy at one e-literate person in every household.

secs.t: Earlier IT milestones (IT Task Force, IT Act 2000, NeGP)

x: The milestones occurred in the order NIC in 1976, National Task Force in 1998, IT Act in 2000 and NeGP in 2006.
C-DAC was established at Pune in 1988 to build the
PARAM supercomputer
The IT Act, 2000 gave legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures, and its 2008 amendment addressed e-signatures and cybercrime-related provisions.

secs.t: National Policy on Electronics 2019 - targets, schemes

x: NPE 2019 targeted US$400 billion in electronics manufacturing, 1 billion mobile handsets annually and exports of 600 million handsets annually by 2025.
MPMS has a stated outlay of ₹62,500 crore, replaces PLI for large-scale electronics and targets ₹39 lakh crore production and ₹15 lakh crore exports.
Electronics production reached
₹13.11 lakh crore
in 2025–26, described as sevenfold growth under PLI.

secs.t: India Semiconductor Mission - fab and ATMP units → location + company

x: CMOS silicon fabs receive up to 40% capital subsidy, compound and display fabs 35%, advanced packaging 35%, and R&D up to 75% of project cost.
RRP Electronics is associated with a semiconductor and OSAT facility in Sri Sathya Sai district of Andhra Pradesh.
C2S aims to develop chip-design talent by training 85,000 B.Tech, M.Tech and PhD students over five years.

secs.t: IT institutions → role

x: MeitY handles policy and Digital India coordination; NASSCOM represents IT-BPM firms and partners in IoT CoEs; STPI runs export-oriented parks and CoEs; NIC provides government IT and e-governance services.
MeitY handles policy on IT, electronics, the internet other than ISP licensing, and cyber security, and coordinates Digital India.
C-DAC’s stated roles include R&D involving PARAM supercomputers, implementation of C2S and a centre at Amaravati Quantum Valley.

secs.t: Outcomes - IT share of GDP and exports, global delivery centres

x: TCS, Infosys and Wipro
are identified as major Indian IT-service companies contributing to India's position as one of the world's largest IT-service exporters.
The IT and e-commerce sectors employed
14.67 million
persons in 2022–23.
GCCs perform functions for their parent multinational corporations, whereas outsourcing vendors provide services to other organisations; therefore; .

secs.t: AP IT policy - IT and GCC incentives; IT hubs and data centres

x: The policy aims
to make Andhra Pradesh a global knowledge economy hub and an IT and GCC powerhouse
The policy promotes
IT parks, co-working spaces and neighbourhood workspaces
Visakhapatnam is associated with AI data projects with Anakapalli, a cable landing station and an Infosys campus expected to create about 7,000 jobs.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Semicon 2.0, identified in September 2026, and MPMS, identified in August 2026, replace the NPE-era schemes.
The continuing offline population shows that digital access is not yet universal.
IT and electronics attracted more than
₹18,210 crore
in one Andhra Pradesh Cabinet round.

rows.title: E-governance programmes and services - UMANG, DigiLocker, e-Sign, e-Hospital, Common Service Centres
sub: Group-II M2-B-19: E-governance programmes and services - central initiatives and Andhra Pradesh initiatives

secs.t: Citizen service platforms - ministry + service

x: Exam angle: "national e-authentication service of DeitY" =
e-Pramaan
; new driving licence =
SARATHI
(not VAHAN).
UMANG is a unified service app, DigiLocker stores documents, and e-Sign facilitates Aadhaar-based electronic signatures.
e-Sanjeevani is the national telemedicine service of the Health and Family Welfare sector. e-Hospital is associated with Health and NIC, MyGov with MeitY, and e-Office with MeitY/NIC.
AP Online is a G2C web portal, e-Procurement handles online tenders, APSWAN provides state-wide connectivity, and e-Office enables paperless file movement.

secs.t: State e-governance projects - state + service, state FIRSTs

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2022 asked for the wrong pair: "Khajane = land records" is wrong, because Bhoomi does land records.
All four pairs are correct. e-Mitra, e-Sewa and Sewa Setu are state service-delivery platforms of Rajasthan, Punjab and Assam respectively, while Project Ganga is associated with Uttar Pradesh.
Project Ganga is described as a digital expressway providing
last-mile rural broadband through local Digital Service Providers
in Uttar Pradesh.

secs.t: Government secure messaging and e-mail - Sandes/GIMS, NIC mail, regional-language e-mail

x: GIMS stands for Government Instant Messaging System.
NIC Mail is integrated with CollabFiles, e-Sign, Bhashini and the Parichay single sign-on service.
NIC Mail is the official government e-mail service and is integrated with several government digital platforms.

secs.t: Education e-services - launching body or operator

x: DIKSHA is associated with NCERT and the Ministry of Education, while Bharti Airtel runs its online platforms end to end.
SWAYAM is the Ministry of Education’s MOOC platform.
PM eVIDYA was introduced by the Ministry of Education in 2020 as a
unified multi-mode digital education
initiative.
e-Pathshala is an NCERT platform providing e-textbooks and educational resources.

secs.t: Health e-services - ABDM components (ABHA, HPR, HFR)

x: ABDM was launched in 2021 by the
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
to create a national interoperable digital health ecosystem.
ABHA had 79.91 crore IDs, exceeding the 67.19 crore linked records and the counts of HFR and HPR entries.
The reported figures are 79.91 crore ABHA IDs, 4,18,964 HFR entries and 6,79,692 HPR entries.

secs.t: DigiLocker and e-Sign - legal validity, Aadhaar eKYC, documents

x: DigiLocker provides an Aadhaar-linked cloud account, includes driving licences and vehicle RCs, and has provided CBSE mark sheets since 2015.
Driving licences and vehicle Registration Certificates were linked with DigiLocker through the
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
in September 2016.
e-Sign is PKI-based, provides legally acceptable non-repudiation, uses Aadhaar eKYC and OTP, and is legally supported by the IT Act, 2000.

secs.t: Sectoral portals - sector

x: GeM is the platform for government procurement of goods and services.
e-Procurement handles online government tenders; DACNET is the Agriculture Department’s e-governance network; e-NAM enables agricultural commodity trading; Kisan Suvidha is a farmer app.
AgriStack is agriculture digital public infrastructure concerned with farmer IDs and credit.

secs.t: Common Service Centres - SPV, VLEs, services

x: CSCs provide more than 400 services, including government, financial, Aadhaar, welfare, education, telemedicine, travel and utility-bill services.
There were 5.97 lakh functional CSCs, of which 4.73 lakh were at the Gram Panchayat level as of April 2025.
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj’s ‘Seva Se Samriddhi’ workshop was held in
Guwahati
in 2026 and honoured top VLEs and Champion CSCs.

secs.t: Grievance platforms - CPGRAMS, RTI online

x: SAMADHAN DIDI is
an AI voice chatbot built with Bhashini
and linked to CPGRAMS.
RTI Online is the DoPT portal for filing RTI applications and appeals to
central public authorities

secs.t: Central e-gov programmes - ministry and purpose (NeGP, e-Kranti, UMANG, e-Office, GeM, CPGRAMS, MCA-21, Jeevan Pramaan, e-Pramaan)

x: Exam angle: "NeGP 2006 identified how many MMPs?" -
; e-Kranti = 44.
e-Courts
is identified as an Integrated MMP. e-Panchayat is an MMP, while IT for Jobs and Early Harvest Programmes are Digital India pillars.
NeGP aimed to make government services accessible locally through common service delivery outlets, with transparency, reliability, efficiency and affordable cost.
UMANG is under MeitY; e-Office is a MeitY-NIC platform; GeM belongs to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry; CPGRAMS is associated with DARPG.
CPGRAMS is the DARPG grievance platform offering 24x7 online redressal through the web, app and UMANG.
Jeevan Pramaan is a MeitY initiative providing
Aadhaar-based biometric Digital Life Certificates for pensioners
VAHAN handles vehicle registration, Bhavishya supports pension processing, Jeevan Pramaan provides digital life certificates, and e-Hospital supports online patient services.

secs.t: AP flagship e-governance - e-Pragati, CARD, RTGS, BhuSeva, Mana Mitra

x: Exam angle: "Which app was introduced on 30 Jan 2025 in AP?" -
Mana Mitra

The Real Time Governance Society is associated with Data Lake, Data Lens, a Command and Control Centre, Nara Lokesh as minister in charge, and an approximately ₹100 crore allocation in the 2026–27 Budget.
Mana Mitra enabled more than 500 services, used WhatsApp-based conversational governance, and had an Outcome Budget target of up to 1,000 services.

secs.t: MeeSeva - meaning, launch, service categories, delivery model

x: MeeSeva was launched in 2011 in undivided Andhra Pradesh and succeeded e-Seva, which began in 2001.
e-Seva
, launched in 2001, was the first integrated citizen service-centre initiative in India and preceded MeeSeva.
MeeSeva centres provide certificates such as caste, income and residence certificates, along with land-record extracts and registration-linked services.
MeeSeva follows a single-window service-delivery model through MeeSeva centres.

secs.t: Full forms of e-gov platforms (UMANG, CARD, NeGP, MMP, SWAN, SDC, DACNET)

x: SDC stands for State Data Centre.
NeGP is the
National e-Governance Plan
MMP stands for Mission Mode Project, not Mission Monitoring Portal.

secs.t: National Conference and National Awards on e-Governance

x: 28th National Conference on e-Governance (NCeG) 2025
Visakhapatnam;
organised by
DARPG
with MeitY and the host state.
DARPG's
State Collaboration Initiatives
(revised 2015-16) fund replication of PM-awarded and National e-Governance-awarded initiatives.
NeSDA
benchmarking started

secs.t: E-governance concepts - Gartner model, pillars, G2C/G2B/G2G, role of ICT

x: ICT enhances citizen engagement and improves service delivery, including through transparency and real-time monitoring.
Technology can improve transparency and real-time monitoring, while internet shutdowns can disrupt services that depend on digital connectivity.
High-speed internet, cradle-to-grave digital identity, Common Service Centre access and cloud locker are examples under digital infrastructure as a core utility.

secs.t: NeGP infrastructure - SWAN, State Data Centres, Common Service Centres

x: SWAN, or State Wide Area Network, provides
a converged backbone network for data, voice and video across the State
All four statements correctly describe the roles of SWAN, SDC and CSCs and their combined contribution to G2G, G2C and G2B service delivery.
SWAN, State Data Centres and Common Service Centres together enable seamless Government-to-Government, Government-to-Citizen and Government-to-Business services.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The reported UMANG flaw exposed EPFO Universal Account Numbers (UANs) and Aadhaar numbers in plain text.
Sanjeevani is scheduled for August 2026 and combines ABHA IDs and a wellness app with links to PHCs, 108, 104, e-Aushadhi and telemedicine.
Data security of aggregator portals is a significant criticism, particularly because multiple services and datasets may be brought together on one platform.
The digital divide concerns unequal access to digital services; in this context, the issue specifically includes access to assisted service delivery.

secs.t: Aadhaar - first number, first village, UIDAI, Aadhaar Act uses, open APIs, biometrics

x: By 31 July 2025, 142 crore Aadhaar numbers had been generated and 133.65 crore remained live after accounting for deaths.
Aadhaar supports DBT under the JAM trinity, Jeevan Pramaan digital life certificates, and bank and mobile KYC.
The Institute of Banking Personnel Selection was allowed voluntary Aadhaar authentication of candidates in 2025 under the Aadhaar Authentication for Good Governance Rules, 2020.

secs.t: UPI and NPCI products - BHIM, Bharat QR, e-RUPI, UPI Lite, international acceptance

x: UPI allows one application to route payments from several bank accounts through a Virtual Payment Address such as name@bank.
UPI 2.0 includes overdraft-account linking, pre-authorised payments, signed merchant QR codes and a daily limit of Rs 2 lakh.
UPI Lite is an on-device wallet intended for small-value payments without requiring a UPI PIN for each transaction.

secs.t: Digital payment systems - operator, wallets, iPay

x: FASTag (NETC) is operated by NPCI with NHAI and IHMCL, not by RBI alone.
AePS enables cash withdrawal and balance enquiry at micro-ATMs using Aadhaar-based authentication.
New Umbrella Entities are intended to introduce competition and
end NPCI's monopoly in retail payments
Digital-payment transactions rose from 2,071 crore to 22,831 crore over the stated period, corresponding to a 41% compound annual growth rate.

secs.t: Aadhaar-based delivery in AP - sole identifier, e-PoS ration

x: DBT was inaugurated at Gollaprolu in East Godavari on 6 January 2013 by Jairam Ramesh along with Chief Minister Kiran Kumar Reddy.
e-Seva was introduced in 2001 and constituted the first integrated citizen service centres in India.

secs.t: Nodal responsibility for digital payments - ministry, Digital Payments Index

x: Digital payments currently come under the Department of Financial Services in the Ministry of Finance, which also gives the Digital Payments Awards.
The RBI Digital Payments Index uses March 2018 as its base period with a base value of 100 and is published half-yearly.

secs.t: Digital public infrastructure - India Stack, open-source platforms, ONDC, Account Aggregator

x: India Stack comprises Aadhaar for identity, eSign and DigiLocker for paperless services, UPI for cashless payments, and DEPA/Account Aggregator for consent-based data sharing.
CoWIN, Aarogya Setu, DigiLocker and DIKSHA
are identified as other open platforms.
ONDC is an open e-commerce network intended to reduce dependence on dominant platforms and break platform monopolies.
Account Aggregators operate under the
DEPA
framework, which emphasises consent-based data sharing.

secs.t: DBT - JAM trinity, DBT Mission, schemes, savings

x: DBT routing uses CPSMS, now known as PFMS, and NPCI’s Aadhaar Payment Bridge.
The cumulative amount transferred through DBT was reported as approximately
Rs 44 lakh crore
by May 2025.
The cited figures are 58.77 crore PMJDY accounts and deposits of Rs 3,12,414 crore; more than half of the accounts were held by women.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: UPI recorded a FY 2025–26 record and accounted for 49 percent of the world’s real-time payments.
Both statements are true, and biometric failures among elderly persons and labourers directly explain how digital systems can create exclusion-related concerns.
The IMF reported that UPI handled approximately
of the world's real-time payments in 2025.

rows.title: Government schemes promoting ICT - BharatNet, PMGDISHA, MeghRaj, Digital Village

secs.t: Language and access - Bhashini, BhashaNet, Universal Acceptance, accessibility standards

x: BhashaNet was launched to promote digital inclusion by advancing Universal Acceptance, including support for diverse languages and scripts.
Universal Acceptance requires domain names and e-mail addresses in any language or script, including Indian-language domains, to work properly in every application.
Bhashini is MeitY's National Language Translation Mission, uses AI-based translation, and supports the SAMADHAN DIDI chatbot of DARPG.

secs.t: Digital literacy missions - NDLM, DISHA, Vidya Vahini, ICT@Schools

x: NDLM and DISHA refer to the digital literacy initiatives that preceded PMGDISHA, with DISHA expanded as Digital Saksharta Abhiyan.
E&ICT Academy Phase-II is a five-year MeitY initiative targeting 1,35,000 faculty through 14 agencies, including IITs, NIT, NIELIT and CDAC.
e-Pathshala was launched in November 2015 by
MHRD and NCERT
to provide e-textbooks and other educational resources.

secs.t: BharatNet - phases, implementing agency, GP target, amended programme

x: The BharatNet network has been laid by the CPSUs BSNL, RailTel and Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL).
The Amended BharatNet Programme provides for a PPP model, a greater role for States, revenue sharing, last-mile connectivity and links with 5G.
The stated scope includes upgrading 1,692 Phase-I gram panchayats, covering 11,254 Phase-II villages and adding 480 new gram panchayats.

secs.t: PMGDISHA - target group, coverage, age, certification

x: PMGDISHA was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at
Gandhinagar
PMGDISHA targeted six crore rural households, with one person from each household, in the age group of 14 to 60 years.
At closure, PMGDISHA had 7.35 crore registered beneficiaries, 6.39 crore trained beneficiaries and 4.78 crore certified beneficiaries.

secs.t: MeghRaj GI Cloud - architecture, empanelment

x: MeghRaj is the GI Cloud initiative started by the Department of Electronics and Information Technology (DeitY).
MeghRaj provides a common pool of cloud infrastructure and applications that departments can access on demand.
The five characteristics are on-demand self-service, ubiquitous network access, metered use, elasticity and resource pooling.
MeitY empanels private Cloud Service Providers for government use.

secs.t: Digital Village pilot - CSC-led services

x: The Samriddh Gram pilots include Narakoduru in Andhra Pradesh, Ari and Umri in Madhya Pradesh, and Chaurawala in Uttar Pradesh.
The AP Samriddhi Kendra offers passport and Aadhaar services, bill payments, soil testing, drone spraying and AI training.
Gujarat's Digital Seva Setu brings 321 services to more than 14,078 gram panchayats through e-Gram centres.

secs.t: Rural connectivity funds - USOF / Digital Bharat Nidhi, LWE towers, PM-WANI

x: USOF is a non-lapsable fund intended to support telecommunications in
commercially unviable rural and remote areas
USOF funded NOFN and was renamed Digital Bharat Nidhi under the Telecommunications Act, 2023.
Five percent of Digital Bharat Nidhi collections, approximately Rs 500 crore per year, goes to the Telecom Technology Development Fund.
Digital Bharat Nidhi
runs the Memoranda of Cooperation for the Amended BharatNet Programme.

secs.t: Electronics manufacturing - PLI, SPECS, EMC 2.0

x: India was described as the world’s second-largest mobile maker, while electronics was identified as the third-largest export category.
SPECS is the scheme providing incentives for
electronic components and semiconductors
EMC 2.0 is the modified Electronics Manufacturing Clusters scheme, introduced in 2020.
MPMS is the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme; it is not a scheme for NeGP Mission Mode Projects.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh signed the Amended BharatNet MoC in
February 2026
The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet cleared the rollout roadmap in
May 2026
The assessment indicated that about 38% of Indians were still offline.
Both the assertion and reason are true, and reaching more than 4,000 tribal hamlets directly explains the significance of AP FiberNet for digital inclusion.

rows.title: ICT in Andhra Pradesh - e-Pragati, RTGS, Mee Seva and state digital initiatives

secs.t: AP e-governance projects - department + service, vs other states

x: MeeSeva
succeeded e-Seva as a single-window G2C delivery mechanism.
Registration Service Kendras provide property-registration services on the
Passport Seva Kendra model
, but statutory powers remain with the SROs.
HIMSWAN belongs to Himachal Pradesh; Digital Seva Setu and GSWAN belong to Gujarat; and Seva One is Karnataka's digital citizen-services initiative.
Digital Seva Setu covers 321 services through 14,078 Gram Panchayats.

secs.t: Mee Seva - meaning, service categories, departments, channels, launch

x: Category A services are over-the-counter services issued on the spot; certified copies are an example.
The EDS Department prints MeeSeva certificates, while the Education Department issues migration certificates to passed candidates.
MeeSeva services are delivered through MeeSeva franchise centres as well as the online portal.
MeeSeva also serves as an enrolment channel for schemes such as
Aarogya Raksha

secs.t: AP citizen and police apps - department + purpose

x: Pura Seva is a Municipal Administration and Urban Development application for grievances, building plan approval and vacant land tax; electricity bills are not its stated function.
Disha SOS serves women's safety, AP Police Seva provides citizen police services, Sanjeevani provides an ABHA-linked profile, and Pura Seva handles municipal services.
Mana Mitra includes services such as
rice card eKYC
, electricity bills, 1-B Adangal, APSRTC tickets and temple darshan services.

secs.t: AP IT policies and institutions - IT and GCC policy, skills university, data centres, Quantum Valley

x: The AP Cyber Security Policy was formulated in 2017 to establish a secure cyber ecosystem for citizens, businesses and government.
Kaushalam is an AI-powered platform for employability and skill verification.
Effective Governance and AI-based Public Services
” is one of the pillars of Swarna Andhra @2047.
The monitoring framework tracks KPIs and uses OBD/IVRS calls and bulk WhatsApp for feedback.

secs.t: NIC-AP solutions - user institution

x: MEDHAS is the NIC-AP State Centre's all-in-one solution for
Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences
e-Office is NIC's paperless office product used in the AP Secretariat and departments. e-Granthalaya is the library management software with Web OPAC and Unicode features.

secs.t: RTGS - command centre, dashboards, Village and Ward Secretariat delivery

x: RTGS uses Artificial Intelligence, Big Data, GIS, IoT and real-time dashboards.
RTGS operates through its
Data Lake, Data Lens and Command & Control Centre
, supported by real-time dashboards.
The July 2026 directions included redrafting the Business Rules and strengthening
crowd-sourced grievance tracking

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All four developments and their stated time references are correctly matched: RTGS and Registration Service Kendras in July 2026, Mana Mitra temple revenue in June 2026, and the amended BharatNet MoC for 13,426 panchayats in February 2026.
The debate concerns the impact of RSKs on document writers’ livelihoods, while the State has assured that Sub-Registrar Offices are not being privatised.

rows.title: Netiquettes - digital etiquette, digital literacy, misinformation and fake news

secs.t: Online safety practices - passwords, friend requests, privacy settings, 2FA, verify before sharing

x: Exam angle: "which is NOT a safe practice" and odd-one-out questions.
Accepting friend requests from unknown persons without caution
is not a safe online practice.
Passwords, biometrics and multi-factor authentication
are authentication methods used to verify a user's identity.
Nomophobia is the
irrational fear of being without one's mobile phone
, including situations involving no signal, low battery or insufficient balance.

secs.t: Fact-check mechanisms - PIB FCU, tip lines, IT Rules amendments, Sahyog portal, court challenges

x: The PIB Fact Check Unit was set up in November 2019 to debunk fake news concerning the Government of India, its ministries, public sector undertakings and central bodies.
The PIB Fact Check Unit flagged more than 50 deepfakes or manipulated videos in
one month
; many were associated with Pakistani propaganda handles.
WhatsApp
launched a tip line to help curb fake news ahead of the 2019 Lok Sabha election.

secs.t: Digital literacy - levels, Computer Literacy Day, NSS data, school curriculum

x: PMGDISHA promotes digital literacy among rural people, with the aim of having one digitally literate person in every family; it was launched by the Prime Minister at Gandhinagar.

ULLAS covers adults aged 15 years and above during 2022–27 and includes digital and financial literacy under Critical Life Skills; Himachal Pradesh was the fifth State/UT to achieve full functional literacy.

secs.t: Online behaviour terms - cyber venting, trolling, cyberbullying, doxxing, cyberstalking, remedies

x: Doxxing involves publicly sharing private information such as a real name, location or workplace online without consent, generally to harm or shame the person.

Section 66E of the IT Act concerns privacy violation, Section 67 concerns obscene material, and Section 78 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita covers stalking, including monitoring electronic communication.

secs.t: Netiquettes - rules for email, social media, online meetings, forums (dos and don'ts)

x: A clear subject line, polite greeting and verification of recipients are appropriate email practices.
Posting another person's photograph or data without consent violates social-media netiquette.
Joining on time and avoiding recording without permission are proper practices.
Digital freedom is linked with responsible conduct, including constructive online dialogue and respect for privacy.

secs.t: Digital citizenship - rights, responsibilities, digital footprint

x: A responsible digital citizen identifies misinformation, verifies sources, protects personal data, respects privacy and participates in civil discourse.
Online grievance redressal
, e-consultations and access to open government data are rights-related aspects of digital citizenship.
AP Grama and Ward Sachivalayam is an example associated with digital-governance rights and services, including online grievance redressal and citizen consultations.

secs.t: Misinformation vs disinformation vs malinformation - terms, deepfakes, echo chambers

x: All three statements correctly distinguish the terms: misinformation lacks deceptive intent, disinformation is deliberately false, and malinformation uses genuine information harmfully.
Algorithms can prioritise content matching a user’s preferences and thereby isolate the user from other viewpoints, producing filter bubbles or echo chambers.
Measures for responding to deepfakes include the ECI advisory on mandatory labels for AI content in campaigns, DPDP Act penalties and I4C takedowns.

secs.t: Media literacy initiatives - election misinformation measures, platform self-regulation

x: Media literacy, fact-checkers and platform policies to remove or down-rank fake content are counter-measures.
The stated platform duties under the IT Rules, 2021 include due diligence, prompt removal of harmful content and grievance processes, especially for content harmful to children.
Minors may lack the skills needed to distinguish truth from misinformation.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Doxxing involves the unauthorised exposure of personal information and raises concerns relating to privacy and online safety.
Both statements are true, and the risk of executive overreach explains why regulation intended to curb fake news must also protect free speech.
In chronological order, the figures refer to 25.15 crore connections in 2014, 11.74% in FY23, the projected 13.42% in FY25 and 96.96 crore connections in 2024.

rows.title: Cyber security concerns - types of cyber crime, malware, ransomware, phishing, social engineering
sub: Group-II M2-B-21: Cyber security concerns - cyber crime types, threats to critical infrastructure and data breaches

secs.t: Malware types → mechanism (virus, worm, trojan, ransomware, spyware, adware, rootkit, keylogger, botnet)

x: Exam angle: "self-replicating without user action" = worm; "no self-replication, disguised" = trojan.
A
Trojan
is disguised as legitimate software, does not self-replicate and may open a backdoor for unauthorised access.
The AIIMS Delhi attack of 2022 is cited as an example of
ransomware
, which encrypts files or systems and demands payment for restoration.
A rootkit gains deep administrator-level access and conceals other malicious components, making it particularly difficult to detect.
A botnet consists of infected ‘zombie’ devices controlled remotely and may be used for DDoS attacks, spam or crypto-mining.

secs.t: Named malware and attacks → type + origin (Creeper, Brain, Elk Cloner, WannaCry, Petya, EternalBlue, Stuxnet, Pegasus, StrandHogg), FIRST virus

x: Exam angle: "Petya and WannaCry are related to" -
Ransomware
Elk Cloner, created by Rich Skrenta, is regarded as the first virus in the wild and affected Apple II computers in 1982.
Stuxnet was a worm containing rootkit components that sabotaged Siemens PLC-controlled uranium centrifuges at Iran’s Natanz facility.
Pegasus is state-grade zero-click spyware associated with Israel’s NSO Group and can exploit zero-days without requiring user interaction.
StrandHogg is an Android vulnerability that allows malware to impersonate genuine applications and steal user data.
The 2016 breach involved 3.2 million debit cards, Zomato faced data theft in 2017, and NotPetya affected Ukraine in 2017.

secs.t: Cyber threats → description matching (phishing, spam, e-mail bombing, spoofing, MITM, DoS/DDoS, SQL injection, zero-day, social engineering)

x: A
zero-day exploit
targets an unknown, unpatched vulnerability; developers have had effectively zero days to fix it.
In a
supply-chain attack
, a trusted vendor or supplier is compromised to reach the ultimate target; SolarWinds is a cited example from 2020.
A
man-in-the-middle attack
involves secretly intercepting, and potentially altering, communication between two communicating parties.
CERT-In conducted 115 exercises involving about 1,500 organisations; Cyber Suraksha is a 12-day DRDO-led Armed Forces exercise; and October is Cyber Security Awareness Month.

secs.t: Cyber crime types - identity theft, sextortion, digital arrest, cyber slavery, dark web

x: Digital arrest is a criminal intimidation technique in which impostors claim that the victim is under arrest and demand money, often while keeping the victim on a video call.
Cyber slavery involves trafficking victims and coercing them to operate cyber-fraud schemes, frequently from scam centres.
The Telangana case involved trafficking for cyber fraud, scam centres were linked to Myanmar and Laos, and FIU-India flagged Rs 800 crore in cross-border laundering.
The dark web is a hidden part of the internet commonly accessed through tools such as Tor.
The complaints declined from 1,23,672 in 2024 to 58,249 in 2025 and stood at 16,377 up to 30 June 2026.

secs.t: Security tools - firewall, antivirus, VPN, 2FA, passwords, honeypot, indigenous software → developer

x: Antivirus addresses malicious infections, VPNs protect traffic through an encrypted tunnel, 2FA uses independent proofs, and honeypots attract attackers for observation.
BOSS Linux is associated with C-DAC, Maya OS with Chakravyuh with the Ministry of Defence, M-Kavach with C-DAC Hyderabad, and CERT-In with CVE numbering for products made in India.

secs.t: Cryptography terms - encryption, decryption, symmetric vs asymmetric, digital signature, hashing

x: Encryption converts readable plaintext into ciphertext, while decryption converts ciphertext back into plaintext using a key.
Symmetric systems are generally fast, but securely sharing the common secret key is a key-management problem.
A digital signature is generated with the sender's private key and verified with the corresponding public key; it helps prove the message's origin and integrity.

secs.t: Cyber attacks on Indian public systems → target + state

x: The e-Nagarpalika portal was attacked as an online civic tax payment system; AIIMS Delhi suffered ransomware; Kudankulam's administrative network was affected by malware; Cosmos Bank faced ATM/SWIFT fraud of about Rs 94 crore.
The 2018 Cosmos Bank incident involved an ATM/SWIFT fraud of about Rs 94 crore and was associated with Pune, Maharashtra.

secs.t: Information security principles - CIA triad, cyber insurance for individuals

x: Exposure compromises confidentiality, alteration compromises integrity, and denial of access compromises availability; together they cover all elements of the CIA triad.

secs.t: Financial cyber frauds - SIM swap, UPI and QR fraud, loan apps, crypto-jacking

x: SIM manipulation allows fraudsters to control the victim's mobile connection and divert OTPs, often after posing as bank officials through voice phishing.
Illegal loan apps may harvest contacts and photographs and use the collected information to extort borrowers.
Crypto-jacking is the unauthorised and concealed use of a victim's computing device to mine cryptocurrency; botnets may also be used for this purpose.

secs.t: Security basics - firewall, encryption, passwords, virtual keyboards, CIA triad

x: Virtual keyboards help protect against
keyloggers
by reducing the usefulness of recording physical keyboard keystrokes.

secs.t: Cyber warfare and espionage - state-sponsored APTs, cyber terrorism

x: State-sponsored cyber espionage commonly uses spear-phishing, advanced malware and zero-day vulnerabilities.
Cyber terrorism seeks to disrupt critical infrastructure.
VPNs, proxies and botnets can obscure the true source of an attack, making attribution difficult.
All three statements are correct according to the cited assessment of state-linked operations and targeting patterns.
Cyber espionage is often state-sponsored and may employ spear-phishing and zero-days.

secs.t: Cyber crime data - NCRB trends, top states
Universal angles

x: AI-powered malware is capable of adapting to evade antivirus protection, malicious autonomous agents threaten Zero Trust, and AI-enabled phishing of Instagram accounts was noted in June 2026.

The Andhra Pradesh Police and IIT Tirupati entered into a Memorandum of Understanding in February 2026 for a Cyber Crime Investigation and Training Academy, with emphasis on digital forensics and blockchain tracing.

rows.title: Cyber security architecture - IT Act 2000 and amendments, CERT-In, NCIIPC, Cyber Swachhta Kendra, I4C
sub: Group-II M2-B-22: National Cyber Security Policy and institutional framework - CERT-In, NCIIPC, I4C, IT Act

secs.t: IT Act 2000 - purpose, concepts introduced, Controller of Certifying Authorities, e-transactions

x: Exam angle: Section 4 = e-records, Section 5 = e-signatures (CGPSC 2022 match).
The
Controller of Certifying Authorities
, or CCA, is the statutory regulator of electronic signatures.
The Act contains provisions on electronic records, intermediary due diligence and adjudication, but it does not establish a separate cyber legislature through a constitutional amendment.
Section 4 concerns electronic records, Section 5 electronic signatures, Section 43A protection of sensitive personal data, and Section 66F cyber terrorism.

secs.t: Cyber security portals and drills → organiser + venue (MySecurity.in, scenario-building exercises)

x: The stated current figure is 115 cybersecurity exercises, including tabletop exercises, involving about 1,500 organisations.
Cyber Surakshit Bharat, associated with MeitY and launched in 2018, focused on training
Chief Information Security Officers
Cyber Surakshit Bharat was launched by MeitY in 2018 with industry partners to train CISOs and front-line IT officials of government bodies.

secs.t: Digital signature and PKI - definition, certifying authority, legal validity

x: A digital signature uses asymmetric cryptography together with a hash function to support verification of the signed electronic document.
Digital signatures provide authentication, integrity and non-repudiation, but a signature by itself does not guarantee confidentiality or secrecy of the document.
A digital certificate contains identification and issuer-related information, while a digital signature is the electronic signing mechanism that supports authentication and integrity.

secs.t: CERT-In - parent ministry, mandate, mandatory incident reporting

x: CERT-In collects, analyses and disseminates incident information, issues forecasts and alerts, and coordinates emergency responses; conducting elections is not its function.
The 2022 CERT-In Directions require specified entities to report cyber incidents within six hours of noticing them.
VPN providers are required to maintain subscriber data for
five years
, while ICT logs have a 180-day retention requirement.
CERT-In operates Cyber Swachhta Kendra, serves as a CVE Numbering Authority for Indian products, and has empanelled 200 IT security auditing organisations.

secs.t: IT Act sections → offence or power, 2008 amendment, Shreya Singhal

x: Sections 66C, 66D and 66E respectively deal with identity theft, cheating by personation using a computer, and violation of privacy.
Section 79 provides safe harbour, but it may be lost when the intermediary fails to act on
actual knowledge in the legally recognised form
The 2008 amendment added offences relating to sexually explicit material, video voyeurism, data leakage by intermediaries and e-commerce fraud; it did not create the NCCC.

secs.t: NCIIPC and Cyber Swachhta Kendra - parent body, critical sectors, free tools

x: Cyber Swachhta Kendra is the
Botnet Cleaning and Malware Analysis Centre
, set up and operated by CERT-In.
Cyber Swachhta Kendra provides free tools for detecting and removing botnets and malware.
Cyber Swachhta Kendra was reported to cover about 98% of Indian internet users and 1,415 organisations as of July 2025.

secs.t: I4C - parent ministry, components, National Cyber Security Coordinator

x: The
National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal
, cybercrime.gov.in, is used for reporting cyber crimes, especially those against women and children.
The January 2026 CFCFRMS SOP permits banks to refund frauds below
without a court order.
The Money Restoration Portal involved 57 banks, 36,290 cases and ₹18.05 crore, while e-Zero FIR was functional in 19 States.
ITSSO tracks sexual-offence investigations, the cybercrime portal accepts online complaints, 1930 is the cybercrime helpline and ERSS uses 112.

secs.t: AP cyber crime set-up - cyber police stations, AP CID cyber cell, state CERT

x: APTS undertakes capacity building, supports critical-infrastructure security through APCSOC and audits government applications.
The centre included
a cyber radar wing and a laboratory
; plans also included a cyber war room and cyber guard policy.
APTS
is the first CERT-In-empanelled organisation in Andhra Pradesh and is also identified as the first CERT-In-empanelled auditor in the State.

secs.t: Cases - Shreya Singhal (Section 66A)

x: The Supreme Court struck down Section 66A for violating freedom of speech and expression under
Article 19(1)(a)
, and held that it was not saved by Article 19(2).
The Court struck down Section 66A, read down Section 79 and upheld Section 69A.

secs.t: International - Budapest Convention, UN cybercrime convention, GCI rank

x: The Budapest Convention is associated with the
Council of Europe
India, Russia and China
were identified as non-signatories to the Budapest Convention.
The Global Cybersecurity Index 2024 placed India in Tier 1 with a score of 98.49.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: e-Zero FIR was functional in 19 States, only 14 States had notified State Cyber Crime Coordination Centres, and CERT-In incidents reached 29.44 lakh in 2025.
The Supreme Court directed the formulation of standard operating procedures concerning digital-arrest scams.
The debate concerns surveillance and takedown powers versus free speech, with the wider discussion also linked to Section 66A, Section 69A and VPN regulation.

rows.title: National Cyber Security Policy 2013 and the national cyber crime policy framework

secs.t: National Cyber Security Policy 2013 - vision, objectives, workforce target, nodal agency

x: The policy aimed at resilient cyberspace, trained manpower, research and development, indigenous security technology and an Information Security Assurance Framework.
A draft National Cyber Security Strategy
followed the 2013 policy; some descriptions refer to it as an updated NCSP 2020.
The policy envisions
a secure and resilient cyberspace for citizens, businesses and government

secs.t: National Cyber Security Strategy draft - pillars, pending status

x: The draft National Cyber Security Strategy was prepared under the
National Cyber Security Coordinator
The draft strategy remains pending and has not been notified.

secs.t: Crisis Management Plan - CISOs in ministries

x: The Cyber Crisis Management Plan is a MeitY framework for countering
cyber attacks and cyber terrorism
CERT-In had conducted 205 Cyber Crisis Management Plan workshops by July 2025.
Every ministry, department and organisation must designate a
Chief Information Security Officer
, or CISO.
NCCC supports
situational awareness and timely information-sharing
in the cyber domain.

secs.t: Cyber Crime Prevention against Women and Children (CCPWC) scheme - components, forensic labs

x: The CCPWC scheme has an outlay of Rs 132.93 crore and provides cyber forensic-cum-training laboratories in 33 States and Union Territories.
Cyber Shakti is a programme for
women government officials
, with 305 participants at the beginner level and 53 at the advanced level.
The stated Cyber Shakti figures are 305 beginner-level participants and 53 advanced-level participants.

secs.t: Sectoral cyber frameworks - RBI, SEBI CSCRF, power-sector CERTs

x: Urban Co-operative Banks are required to have a dedicated cyber team, a board-approved policy, MFA, an incident plan and to report all cyber attacks to RBI.
The second edition of the MeitY Digital Threat Report 2025–26 provides an 18-month roadmap towards continuous cyber resilience for BFSI.
The Money Restoration portal covered 57 banks and all 36 States/UTs, involving 36,290 cases and Rs 18.05 crore.

secs.t: International cyber cooperation - bilateral dialogues, Quad, Counter Ransomware Initiative

x: The
Cyber Diplomacy Division
of the MEA is the nodal point for these cyber-related international matters.
APCERT is a coalition of Computer Security Incident Response Teams from 13 economies.
India participates in the Quad cyber mechanisms, is a member of the US-led Counter Ransomware Initiative and has been urged to conclude faster CERT-In agreements with foreign counterparts.

secs.t: ITU Global Cybersecurity Index - India's tier and rank

x: India received a score of 98.49 and was strong in all five pillars.
India was ranked 10th in the
GCI 2020
India was placed in Tier-1, described as ‘Role Modelling’, and secured a score of 98.49 in the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index 2024.

secs.t: Awareness and workforce - ISEA, cyber hygiene campaigns

x: ISEA stands for
Information Security Education and Awareness
ISEA is a capacity-building project of the
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
(MeitY).
CERT-In trained 12,014 IT professionals through 23 trainings in 2024.
NM-ICPS supports
cybersecurity and artificial intelligence
research.
The Telangana Cyber Security Bureau launched the #OnlineButUnafraid campaign for
women journalists

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Supreme Court order concerned standard operating procedures for digital arrests and restoration of victims' losses.
The 2013 policy was criticised for never having been updated, and coordination among CERT-In, the MHA portal and State police was described as weak.
Securing critical government infrastructure
is one of the four verticals of the Andhra Pradesh Cyber Security Policy 2017.

rows.title: Data protection and privacy - Puttaswamy judgment, Digital Personal Data Protection Act, data localisation
sub: Group-II M2-B-23: Data protection and privacy - the DPDP Act and related concerns

secs.t: Global frameworks - EU GDPR, right to erasure, right to be forgotten

x: RTBF concerns the
removal, masking or de-indexing of outdated, irrelevant or harmful personal information
The RTBF originated in
Google Spain v AEPD
The Indian understanding of RTBF does not erase judicial records; it can limit name-based searches in appropriate circumstances.
The DPDP Act comparison specifies financial penalties of up to
Rs 250 crore

secs.t: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v Union of India (2017) - bench, right, basis, tests

x: In
K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
, decided in 2017, the Supreme Court held that privacy is intrinsic to life and personal liberty under Article 21 and protected under Part III.

Kharak Singh is associated with early privacy concerns under Article 21; Gobind recognised privacy as part of personal liberty; Puttaswamy affirmed privacy as a Fundamental Right and informational privacy.

secs.t: Aadhaar judgment 2018 - provisions struck down and upheld

x: The Aadhaar judgment was delivered by a five-judge Bench on 26 September 2018 by 4:1, with Justice D.Y. Chandrachud dissenting.
The judgment upheld Aadhaar linking with
PAN and income-tax returns under Section 139AA of the Income-tax Act
Mandatory linking with bank accounts and mobile SIMs, as well as requirements relating to CBSE, NEET, UGC and school admissions, was struck down or not upheld.

secs.t: Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 - terms, Board, penalties, exemptions

x: Notification as a Significant Data Fiduciary is based on factors such as the
volume and sensitivity of data
, along with associated risks.
Children’s data obligations carry ₹200 crore, additional SDF duties ₹150 crore, residual breaches ₹50 crore and false information by Data Principals ₹10,000.
The Board can decide complaints and references, order urgent remedial action and impose penalties up to ₹250 crore.

secs.t: DPDP Rules 2025 - phased implementation

x: The final DPDP Rules were notified on
14 November 2025
; 3 January 2025 was the date of release of the draft Rules.
Board provisions came into force immediately in November 2025, Consent Manager provisions in November 2026 and full operational compliance in May 2027.
The Rules require clear, specific and informed consent, plain-language notices, purpose limitation, data minimisation and retention controls.

secs.t: Srikrishna Committee - PDP Bill history and withdrawal

x: The Bill was withdrawn in 2022 citing
compliance burden and ambiguity
, after which a narrower DPDP draft was released.

The A.P. Shah Group dealt with privacy, the Srikrishna Committee with the Personal Data Protection Bill, the Kris Gopalakrishnan Committee with non-personal data and the A.K. Bhargava Committee with net neutrality.

secs.t: Data localisation - RBI payment data mandate, cross-border transfers

x: The RBI’s April 2018 mandate required all payment-system data to be stored only in India.
The DPDP Act uses a blacklist or negative-list approach, under which transfers are allowed unless the Central Government restricts particular countries.
The standards focused on
data sovereignty, algorithmic bias and privacy
and were aligned with the DPDP Act.

secs.t: RTI-privacy debate - amendment to Section 8(1)(j)

x: The amendment permits authorities to refuse all personal information, thereby removing the earlier public-interest override and the ‘no relationship to public activity’ test.
Section 44(3) removed both the earlier public-interest override and the public-activity relationship test, allowing personal information to be refused outright.
Section 7, dealing with ‘legitimate uses’, allows the State to process data without consent.

secs.t: Surveillance and privacy - Pegasus inquiry, interception provisions

x: The committee found malware on five of the 29 phones examined, but could not conclusively establish that it was Pegasus.
Interception is associated with Section 69 of the IT Act and Section 5(2) of the Telegraph Act, 1885, with the latter framework now under the Telecommunications Act, 2023.
The challenge concerned Delhi Police use during NEET-UG protests, NAFRS operates without a statute, and surveillance must meet the Puttaswamy tests.

secs.t: Rights and duties of Data Principals

x: A Data Principal does not impose criminal penalties on a Data Fiduciary.
A Data Principal must not provide false information or impersonate another person.

secs.t: Children's data - consent and tracking

x: The framework requires verifiable parental consent for persons under 18 years of age.
Tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertisements aimed at children are prohibited.
A breach relating to children’s data may attract a penalty of up to
₹200 crore

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The AI4AP pilot is associated with
Chittoor, Guntur and Annamayya
, and raises DPDP compliance issues.
The DPDP framework is described as narrower and lighter than the GDPR, with a financial-penalty-based enforcement approach.
The Delhi High Court case Laksh Vir Singh Yadav v. Union of India set a framework for de-indexing name searches of acquitted persons.

units.title: Technology in Space and Defence - Indian Space Programme, ISRO, Satellite Programmes, IRNSS, IRS, Defence and Academic Satellites, DRDO

rows.title: Evolution of the Indian space programme - INCOSPAR, Vikram Sarabhai, key milestones

secs.t: Early satellites and experiments → vehicle/site + date + designer (Aryabhata, Bhaskara, Rohini, APPLE, SITE, STEP), chronology

x: Exam angle: "Which cosmodrome launched Aryabhata?" -
Soviet
; chronological ordering of Aryabhata-Bhaskara-Rohini-APPLE.
Rohini was launched on
18 July 1980
by SLV-3 from Sriharikota, making India the sixth nation to launch a satellite using its own rocket.
Rakesh Sharma was the first Indian in space and flew aboard
Soyuz T-11 in April 1984
, under the USSR programme.

secs.t: Milestones - FIRST (indigenous launch, GEO satellite, lunar, Mars, docking, ASAT)

x: SpaDeX is
a space-docking technology demonstrator involving two small spacecraft launched by PSLV
PSLV-C60 launched the SpaDeX spacecraft on
30 December 2024
, and docking was completed on 16 January 2025.
SpaDeX made India the fourth docking nation; LVM3-M6 carried the 6,100 kg BlueBird Block-2 on 24 December 2025; and Skyroot's Vikram-1 reached orbit on 18 July 2026.

secs.t: Founders and chairmen - father of the programme, ISRO chairmen and launches

x: Vikram Sarabhai was the first ISRO Chairman and served until his death in 1971.
Sarabhai received the Padma Bhushan in 1966 and the Padma Vibhushan
posthumously in 1972
Vikram Sarabhai served from 1969–71, Satish Dhawan from 1972–84, U.R. Rao from 1984–94, and K. Kasturirangan from 1994–2003.
Annapurni Subramaniam won the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal in 2026.

secs.t: Indian Space Vision 2047 - space station, crewed lunar landing, next missions

x: Gaganyaan is planned to carry a crew of three to an orbit approximately 400 km above Earth for three days, followed by splashdown in Indian waters.
Chandrayaan-4, Chandrayaan-5 and the Venus Orbiter Mission are identified as next missions in the roadmap.
The stated targets are 50 launches annually, a 44-billion-dollar space economy and more than 440 space start-ups.

secs.t: International cooperation milestones - Soyuz T-11, Indo-French and Indo-US

x: Shubhanshu Shukla flew to the International Space Station on Axiom-4 during June-July 2025.
SITE was conducted with NASA cooperation during
The ISRO-ESA Technical Implementing Plan concerns
ground-tracking support for Gaganyaan

secs.t: Universal angles

x: India has 56 active space assets, permits up to 100% FDI in non-sensitive segments, and has launched more than 400 foreign satellites on Indian rockets.
ISRO was formed in 1969, SITE occurred in 1975-76, Rakesh Sharma flew in 1984, and NISAR was launched in 2025.
IN-SPACe stated that ISRO’s role was by no means diminishing, even as the policy encourages non-governmental participation in operational and commercial activities.

rows.title: ISRO - organisational structure, major centres and their functions
sub: Group-II M2-B-4: Evolution of the Indian space programme and the organisation of ISRO

secs.t: SDSC-SHAR Sriharikota (AP) - district, lake, launch pads, gallery, third launch pad

x: Exam angle: "Sriharikota is in which district?" - answer by the date of the paper (Nellore earlier, Tirupati now).
Sriharikota was selected because of its east-coast location, proximity to the equator, sea corridor for spent stages and relatively thin population.
NARL at Gadanki is an autonomous Department of Space research body concerned with atmospheric radar, lidar and monsoon dynamics.
SHAR was established in 1971, renamed in 2002, the Public Launch View Gallery opened in 2019, and the Third Launch Pad was approved in January 2025.
The 100th launch from Sriharikota occurred on 29 January 2025 and was the
17th GSLV flight

secs.t: ISRO centres - full form, location, function

x: The
Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre
(VSSC), located at Thiruvananthapuram, is the lead centre for launch-vehicle design and development.
The National Remote Sensing Centre (
NRSC
), located at Hyderabad, handles satellite data reception, processing and distribution.
MCF operates from Hassan and Bhopal for geostationary-satellite control, while ISTRAC at Bengaluru performs tracking, telemetry and command functions.
VSSC handles launch-vehicle design and development; URSC handles satellite design and building; NRSC handles satellite data; ISTRAC tracks launch vehicles and satellites.

secs.t: IIRS and training bodies - former name, year, location, disciplines

x: IIST is located at
Thiruvananthapuram
IIST was established in 2007 as a deemed university under the Department of Space.
CSSTEAP is affiliated to the United Nations, was established in 1995 and is hosted at IIRS, Dehradun.

secs.t: ISRO outreach and academia - YUVIKA, SPARK, STCs, RACS

x: YUVIKA means Yuva Vigyani Karyakram, is a school-student programme launched in 2019, and its second batch was held in 2022.
There are 9 Space Technology Cells, 6 Space Technology Incubation Centres, 6 RACS and UNNATI was launched in 2018.
The Satish Dhawan Centre for Space Sciences is located at the
Central University of Jammu

secs.t: ISRO ground network - ISTRAC stations abroad, tracking MoUs

x: ISTRAC is headquartered at Bengaluru and operates the telemetry, tracking and command network used to track launch vehicles during ascent.
Mauritius, Brunei and Biak in Indonesia are overseas ISTRAC stations.
The Indian Deep Space Network is located at
Byalalu near Bengaluru

secs.t: Hierarchy and leadership - Space Commission, DoS, ISRO, chairmen

x: INCOSPAR was formed in 1962, ISRO was established in 1969, the Space Commission and DoS were created in 1972, and SpIN was launched in 2022.
IN-SPACe was established in 2020 with headquarters at Ahmedabad, NSIL became the 2019 CPSE commercial arm, and Antrix is the older commercial arm.
Sarabhai chaired INCOSPAR, Kalam directed the SLV-3 project, SHAR honours Satish Dhawan and URSC honours U.R. Rao.
Vikram Sarabhai was the father of the Indian space programme, first ISRO Chairman and founder of PRL.
M.G.K. Menon preceded Satish Dhawan, Satish Dhawan preceded U.R. Rao, and K. Kasturirangan preceded G. Madhavan Nair.
ISRO replaced INCOSPAR in 1969, was brought under the Department of Space on 1 June 1972, and the Department of Space functions directly under the Prime Minister.

secs.t: DoS autonomous bodies - function

x: The National Atmospheric Research Laboratory (NARL), located at Gadanki, undertakes atmospheric research.
PRL is at Ahmedabad, NE-SAC is at Shillong and SCL is at Mohali.
IIST is a deemed university devoted to space education.
All three pairs are correctly matched.

secs.t: Second spaceport for SSLV - location and reason

x: The SSLV Launch Complex is at Kulasekarapattinam in Thoothukudi, also known as Tuticorin, district of Tamil Nadu.
Kulasekarapattinam allows a direct southward trajectory into polar and sun-synchronous orbits, avoiding the fuel-costly manoeuvre around Sri Lanka required from Sriharikota.
The complex is designed mainly for SSLV launches and is expected to support increasing participation by private players.

secs.t: Milestones - INCOSPAR, TERLS, ISRO, DoS

x: Space research was placed under the Department of Atomic Energy in 1961, INCOSPAR was established in 1962, ISRO was formed in 1969, and the Space Commission and Department of Space were established in 1972.
NSIL was established in 2019 as a CPSE and commercial arm, space-sector reforms including IN-SPACe followed in 2020, and the Indian Space Policy was issued in 2023.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: ISRO stated that it would not be privatised, while India is encouraging private participation through space-sector reforms and a growing start-up ecosystem.
The stated plan is to expand the space economy from about $8.4 billion to approximately
$44 billion
by 2033, alongside the growth of more than 450 space start-ups.
As of 2026, India still does not have a comprehensive Space Activities Act, although the country has introduced policy and institutional reforms for the space sector.
