rows.title: Launch vehicles - SLV-3, ASLV, PSLV variants, GSLV Mk-II, LVM3/GSLV Mk-III, SSLV
sub: Group-II M2-B-5: Launch vehicles of India - PSLV, GSLV Mk-II, LVM3, SSLV and future vehicles

secs.t: Satellite → launch vehicle + flight number

x: Two LVM3 missions, designated M2 and M3, launched a total of 72 OneWeb satellites.
EOS-N1 or Anvesha was a DRDO hyperspectral satellite launched with 15 co-passengers by PSLV-C62 on 12 January 2026; the mission failed because of a third-stage anomaly.
GSLV-F16 launched NISAR on 30 July 2025 and was the first GSLV launch to a sun-synchronous polar orbit.

secs.t: Launch vehicle → stages + propellant per stage

x: All four statements correctly describe GSLV Mk II: its HTPB solid first stage, Vikas-powered liquid second stage, LH2-LOX cryogenic third stage and four liquid strap-ons.
The development sequence proceeds from SLV-3 to ASLV, PSLV, GSLV Mk II, LVM3 and SSLV.
PSLV
is widely described as ISRO's workhorse and was the first Indian launch vehicle with liquid stages.

secs.t: Record and landmark launches

x: PSLV-C61/EOS-09 on 18 May 2025 and PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 on 12 January 2026 both failed in the third stage; ISRO described them as “marginally missed”.
BlueBird Block-2 is associated with LVM3-M6, weighs 6,100 kg and is described as the largest commercial communication satellite in low Earth orbit.
GSAT-9 was launched in May 2017, CMS-03/GSAT-7R relates to November 2025, and BlueBird Block-2 is associated with LVM3-M6 and APPCA 2026 thereafter.

secs.t: Full forms and orbits served

x: SSO stands for
Sun-Synchronous Orbit
, a type of polar orbit for which PSLV has special capability.
PSLV serves SSO, LEO and GTO missions, including Chandrayaan-1 and the Mars Orbiter Mission.
GSLV Mk II
is designed to place 2–2.5 tonne communication and navigation satellites into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit.
MEO stands for
Medium Earth Orbit
; GPS is given as an example of a system using this orbital region.

secs.t: SSLV - design goals, payload, launch-on-demand, first flight

x: SSLV is designed for low cost, short turnaround, launch-on-demand missions and minimal infrastructure.
SSLV is designed to place a payload of about
500 kg
into a 500 km Low Earth Orbit.
Hindustan Aeronautics Limited
(HAL) won the ₹511 crore SSLV Transfer of Technology agreement.
The dedicated SSLV spaceport is located at Kulasekarapattinam in Thoothukudi district of Tamil Nadu.

secs.t: Sounding rockets - Rohini RH series, Thumba milestones

x: M-100 was associated with Russia, Centaure with France, indigenous sounding rockets began in 1965, and the Rohini Sounding Rocket Programme began in 1975.
The three operational Rohini versions carry payloads of about 8–100 kg and reach apogees ranging from 80 to 475 km.
Rohini sounding rockets carry payloads for atmospheric research and are also used to test and qualify systems intended for larger launch vehicles.

secs.t: Launch vehicle chronology - order and first payload

x: SLV-3’s successful payload was Rohini RS-1, PSLV’s first successful payload was IRS-P2, and GSLV’s first payload was GSAT-1.
The first flights occurred in the order SLV-3 (1979), ASLV (1987), PSLV (1994) and GSLV (2001).
The PSLV’s first successful flight was PSLV-D2 on 15 October 1994, carrying
IRS-P2
CARE was a
suborbital experimental payload
launched by LVM3 on 18 December 2014.

secs.t: Launch direction and site physics

x: An eastward launch receives an additional velocity from Earth’s rotation, thereby reducing the fuel required to attain orbital speed.
The rotational speed of the Earth is greatest near the equator, so equatorial or near-equatorial sites provide the maximum eastward-launch advantage.
Polar and Sun-synchronous launches generally follow a
southward
trajectory from Sriharikota; a dog-leg is used to avoid Sri Lanka.

secs.t: Payload capacity and PSLV variants

x: The
PSLV
has an approximate capacity of 1,750 kg to SSO and about 1,425 kg to GTO.
The stated LVM3 capacity is about
4 tonnes to GTO and 8 tonnes to LEO
, although some descriptions cite approximately 10 tonnes to LEO.
PSLV-C62 flew as the
PSLV-DL
variant, which uses two strap-on boosters.

secs.t: Reusable and future vehicles

x: NGLV is described as about 90 m tall, with an approximately 1,000-tonne lift-off mass, and is linked to the 2035 space-station and 2040 crewed lunar-landing goals.
The human-rated LVM3, designated
HLVM3
, is intended for the Gaganyaan crew mission to a 400 km LEO orbit for three days.
SOLVE is a
suborbital test vehicle using a solid motor
; its motor was ground-tested at SHAR in July 2026.

secs.t: Cryogenic and semi-cryogenic engines

x: CE-7.5 and CE-20 are cryogenic engines using LH2 and LOX, whereas the semi-cryogenic SCE-200 uses refined kerosene and LOX and is planned for LVM3 upgrades and NGLV.
Russia supplied cryogenic engines for early GSLVs; following technology-transfer denial in the 1990s, India developed its own engine, whose first success was GSLV-D5 in 2014.

secs.t: Orbital terms

x: GSO has a one-day period, while GEO is the equatorial form of such an orbit in which the satellite appears fixed relative to the sky.
A sun-synchronous orbit is generally near-polar and passes over a given location at approximately the same local solar time, which is useful for consistent imaging conditions.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: ISSAR 2025 reported
315 successful launches worldwide and 4,651 objects placed in orbit

The Third Launch Pad is planned to support NGLV and semi-cryogenic LVM3 missions and is associated with the objectives of establishing the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and achieving a crewed lunar landing by 2040.
Rohini RS-1 was launched in 1980, GSLV-D5 succeeded in 2014, PSLV-C61 failed in May 2025, and PSLV-C62 failed in January 2026.

rows.title: Propulsion and future vehicles - cryogenic engine, semi-cryogenic, reusable launch vehicle, scramjet

secs.t: Reusable launch systems - RLV-TD, Pushpak, foreign reusable rockets

x: Pushpak is ISRO’s reusable winged vehicle and is intended to contribute to a Two-Stage-To-Orbit system.
Falcon 9 and Starship are SpaceX vehicles, New Glenn is associated with Blue Origin, and Zhuque-3 with LandSpace.
Starship is described as fully reusable and using about 1,200 tonnes of liquid methane and LOX.
Starship is indicated to require
more than 10
in-orbit refuellings for NASA’s Moon-landing mission.

secs.t: Additive manufacturing - 3D-printed engines → private firm

x: Agnilet was flown in 2024 from Dhanush at Sriharikota, described as India’s first private launch pad.
Agnite is described as a single-piece 3D-printed engine made of Inconel for the Agnibaan booster stage.
Astrobase’s EVEREST is described as India’s first private
800 kN full-flow staged combustion LOX-methane engine
Agnikul achieved the first launch from a private pad, named Dhanush, using a single-piece 3D-printed engine.

secs.t: Green and electric propulsion - green propellants, Hall thrusters, POEM

x: The test involved a 300 mN Stationary Plasma Thruster, a Hall-type thruster using xenon.
The thruster is intended for replacing chemical propulsion on future
communication satellites
LOX-methane is considered cleaner and cheaper, and methane can be produced from Martian resources.
POEM, or PSLV Orbital Experimental Module, reuses the spent PS4, the fourth stage of the PSLV, as an orbital platform.

secs.t: Cryogenic technology - propellants, uses, countries, GSLV, Russian deal, MTCR

x: The very low density of liquid hydrogen, about 0.071 g/ml, necessitates large tanks and makes long-term storage difficult.
Glavkosmos agreed to sell engines and technology in 1991, but US MTCR-based sanctions in 1992 stopped technology transfer; Russia supplied seven engines only.
The sequence is 1991 agreement, 1992 sanctions, 2006 full-stage test and 2014 GSLV Mk II flight with the indigenous stage.

secs.t: Rocket engines → propellant combination

x: CE-7.5 is a 75 kN staged-combustion LOX–LH2 engine used in the GSLV Mk II cryogenic upper stage.
CE-20 is a 200 kN-class gas-generator LOX–LH2 engine for the LVM3 C25 upper stage.
Bootstrap mode starts the engine using its own propellant flow without external gas and is important for in-space restart capability.

secs.t: Propellant categories - examples

x: Refined kerosene and LOX are semi-cryogenic, while LH2 and LOX are cryogenic.
Hypergolic propellants
ignite on contact and are useful for spacecraft manoeuvring
, although they are highly toxic.
Solid

The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways’ AIS-140 rule made NavIC-enabled location trackers compulsory in public transport vehicles.
Smart devices, vehicle tracking and fleet management are identified applications.

The NVS series adds
a civilian L1 signal

40 nanoseconds

24 satellites in six orbits at about 20,200 km altitude

300 metres
, illustrating the importance of atomic clocks in navigation.

secs.t: GAGAN - SBAS concept, ground stations, developers, aviation

x: An SBAS broadcasts real-time corrections for orbit, clock and ionospheric delay, improving accuracy, integrity and availability.
The GAGAN ground segment includes Indian Reference Stations (INRES), the Indian Master Control Centre (INMCC) and uplink stations (INLUS).
GAGAN supports
precision approach and landing for civil aviation
by providing augmented navigation information over the Indian Flight Information Region.

secs.t: IRNSS satellites - launch, NVS series, clock issues

x: First-generation IRNSS satellites used rubidium clocks supplied by Swiss firm SpectraTime, which repeatedly failed; ISRO switched to indigenous clocks in 2018.
After the last clock on IRNSS-1F failed, only IRNSS-1B, IRNSS-1I and NVS-01 remained PNT-capable—three satellites, below the four needed.
Although IRNSS-1F lost its navigation capability after the clock failure, it continued
one-way messaging

secs.t: Limitations - coverage, receivers, failures

x: NavIC is a regional system, while GPS is global.
Receiver adoption was constrained because L5 and S bands were not commonly supported in phone chipsets; the newer civilian L1 signal helps address this limitation.
Repeated atomic-clock failures and the NVS-02 launch failure
reduced the effective constellation, preventing NavIC from fully replacing GPS over India.

secs.t: Other SBAS → region

WAAS serves the USA/North America, EGNOS Europe and GAGAN India.

secs.t: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites

x: Exam angle: "match series with function" and "which satellite uses SAR / serves fishermen".
IRS-P2
was the first IRS satellite launched on PSLV from Sriharikota; the earlier IRS-1A, 1B and 1C missions used Soviet rockets from Baikonur.
Cartosat supports high-resolution mapping, Cartosat-3 provides about 25 cm imagery, and its data have applications in Smart Cities, Gati Shakti and border surveillance.
RISAT-1, RISAT-2 and RISAT-2B use
Synthetic Aperture Radar
(SAR), enabling all-weather, day-and-night imaging through clouds.
EOS-04, formerly RISAT-1A, is a SAR satellite capable of observing crops even under cloud cover; it was also used in the CROP wheat estimate for 2024–25.
NISAR was launched on GSLV-F16 on 30 July 2025 and carries NASA's L-band and ISRO's S-band radars, making it the first dual-frequency radar satellite of its kind.
SARAL is an ISRO-CNES altimetry mission using the AltiKa Ka-band altimeter to measure sea-surface height; hyperspectral agricultural imaging is associated with HySIS.

secs.t: Remote sensing fundamentals - components, EMR, sensors, resolution

x: Remote sensing obtains information about the Earth without physical contact by detecting reflected or emitted electromagnetic radiation.
The remote sensing chain includes illumination, atmospheric transmission, target interaction, sensor recording, data processing, interpretation and application.
After collection and reception at a ground station, remote sensing data are processed at the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), Hyderabad, which functions as the nodal centre.
Optical sensing uses reflected visible or near-infrared light, SAR uses microwave energy that penetrates cloud and darkness, and thermal infrared detects emitted heat.
Hyperspectral sensing uses hundreds of narrow spectral bands, enabling identification of materials and their chemical characteristics.
EOS-05 sensors span visible, near-infrared, short-wave infrared and long-wave infrared portions of the electromagnetic spectrum.

secs.t: EO in news - land subsidence, landslide atlas, glacial lakes

x: The Landslide Atlas of India was released by the
National Remote Sensing Centre
NRSC mapped the Joshimath subsidence using
Cartosat-2S
images in 2023.
CROP stands for Comprehensive Remote Sensing Observation on Crop Progress and uses EOS-04 SAR to track sowing, growth and harvest near real time.
Bhuvan uses
RISAT and INSAT-3DS
data to provide flood-inundation maps and cyclone tracks.

secs.t: Cartosat series - first mapping satellite, resolution, vehicles, Cartosat-3

x: Cartosat-1, launched in 2005, was intended for topographic mapping and supplied stereo images for 3D maps and elevation models.
The Cartosat-2 series, operational from 2007 onward, provides sub-metre resolution imagery for Smart Cities, transport, border management and infrastructure corridors.
Cartosat-3 imagery supports Smart Cities, PM Gati Shakti, border surveillance and heritage applications including KASTURI and Bharat Darshan.

secs.t: Remote sensing techniques → what each maps

x: InSAR
maps ground deformation, including subsidence, earthquake-related movement and volcanic uplift.
LiDAR uses laser ranging to derive elevation, three-dimensional terrain and forest canopy height.
Thermal infrared sensing
records emitted heat and is therefore useful for volcanic eruptions, forest fires and urban heat mapping.
InSAR maps deformation, LiDAR maps elevation and 3D terrain, NDVI maps vegetation health, and thermal infrared maps heat.

highly elliptical
orbit around Mars.

Critics have described ISRO as being weakened, whereas the government has said that it is being freed to focus on Chandrayaan-4, BAS, and Venus and Mars missions.

rows.title: Human spaceflight - Gaganyaan programme, Bharatiya Antariksh Station roadmap
sub: Group-II M2-B-9: Human spaceflight - Gaganyaan and the Bharatiya Antariksh Station roadmap

secs.t: Gaganyaan - modules, orbit, duration, crew, launch vehicle, timeline

x: Gaganyaan is designed to carry a crew of
three
astronauts to a 400 km low Earth orbit for three days.
The human-rated LVM3 uses redesigned GSLV Mk-III structures, and the Vikas engine for its human-rated L110 stage completed three tests totalling 730 seconds.

The Orbital Module consists of the Crew and Service Modules; the Crew Module houses the crew and survives re-entry; the Service Module provides on-orbit support and de-orbits the vehicle; and HLVM3 injects it into orbit.

secs.t: Astronaut-designates - service background, training

x: Exam angle: "which name is NOT a Gaganyatri" (e.g., Pankaj M. Sinha is not).
The four Gaganyatris named in February 2024 were
Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair, Ajit Krishnan, Angad Pratap and Shubhanshu Shukla
NASA
has also trained the Gaganyaan astronaut candidates, in addition to basic training in Russia and training at ISRO's facility in Bengaluru.

secs.t: Indians in space - FIRST Indian, Indian-origin astronauts, Axiom-4

x: Kalpana Chawla was the first Indian-born woman in space, died in the 2003 Columbia disaster, and Sunita Williams is an Indian-origin NASA astronaut associated with long ISS stays.
IIST supplied seed studies, ARISS enabled a ham-radio interaction with students, and HSFC coordinated the Indian microgravity experiments.
Anil Menon, an Indian-origin NASA astronaut, is associated with
Soyuz MS-29 to the ISS for an eight-month mission
involving Expeditions 74–75.

secs.t: Human spaceflight infrastructure - launch pads, HSFC, expos

x: The Third Launch Pad costs about ₹4,000 crore and is planned for the NGLV and future human spaceflight; the NGLV is about 90 metres tall and has about 1,000 tonnes of lift-off mass.
The latest flight, LVM3-M6, carried
the 6,100 kg BlueBird Block-2
, described as its heaviest payload.
The Third Launch Pad, approved in January 2025, and the SSLV Launch Complex at Kulasekarapattinam are intended to add capacity for private launches.

secs.t: Analogue space missions - first site, partners, purpose

x: HOPE, or Himalayan Outpost for Planetary Exploration, was located in Ladakh because of early-Mars-like conditions such as high UV flux, low air pressure, cold extremes and saline permafrost.
Mission MITRA is a behavioural study at Leh conducted with the IAF’s Institute of Aerospace Medicine, testing crew under hypoxia, cold and isolation.

secs.t: International Space Station - partners, modules, retirement, Tiangong

x: The ISS is operated by NASA, Roscosmos, JAXA, the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Canadian Space Agency (CSA).
Gagarin’s Vostok flight occurred in 1961, Zarya was launched in 1998, continuous ISS habitation began in 2000, and Tiangong was completed in 2022.
Soyuz MS-29 carried Indian-origin NASA astronaut
Anil Menon
to the ISS for an eight-month stay.

secs.t: Microgravity effects on the human body

x: Spaceflight osteopenia can cause approximately 1–1.5% loss of bone mass per month without mechanical loading.
Muscle atrophy
in microgravity weakens postural muscles.
Microgravity causes body fluids to shift towards the head, producing a puffy face and comparatively thinner-looking legs.
Space Adaptation Syndrome
is the space motion sickness commonly experienced during the initial days of spaceflight.

secs.t: Test missions - TV-D1, G1, Vyommitra, crew escape, air drops

x: IADT-01 involved the 4.8-tonne dummy module, IADT-02 the 5.7-tonne module and ten parachutes, CARE tested re-entry, and SOLVE tested the solid motor.
Vyommitra is an AI-enabled, female-form semi-humanoid robot intended to fly on the uncrewed G1 and G2 missions before the crewed flight.
SOLVE tested a solid motor derived from
PSLV strap-ons
, intended to loft the crew module to 10–17 km for ten-parachute tests.

secs.t: Bharatiya Antariksh Station - modules, first module, completion

x: BAS is India’s planned
modular space station in Low Earth Orbit
SpaDeX, Axiom-4 and Gaganyaan are identified as precursor missions for the BAS roadmap.
SpaDeX was launched on 30 December 2024, docked on 16 January 2025, the docking made India the fourth nation to dock in space, and BAS-1 is targeted for 2028.

secs.t: Supporting institutions - HSFC, IAM, ISTRAC

x: The Human Space Flight Centre (HSFC), Bengaluru, is the new ISRO vertical leading Gaganyaan.
IAM of the Indian Air Force in Bengaluru undertakes
crew selection, aeromedical training and MITRA
-related work.
ISTRAC
, based in Bengaluru, provides tracking and ground-network functions; ESA adds stations to the network.
HSFC is located at Bengaluru and is responsible for the
Gaganyaan
programme.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Gaganyaan crew-module qualification tests are associated with
July 2026
TV-D1, both air-drop tests, all Gaganyaan launches and the Third Launch Pad are associated with Sriharikota.
IADT-01 was conducted at SDSC-SHAR, and IADT-02 was associated with April 2026.
Repeated slippage from 2021 to 2023 and then 2027 makes projected launch dates unreliable and subject to variation across examination years.

rows.title: Satellites for defence and for academic purposes - GSAT-7 series, EDUSAT, RISAT for surveillance

secs.t: RISAT series - radar band, all-weather imaging, launchers, co-passengers

x: Exam angle: launcher-satellite pairs (RISAT-1/PSLV-C19; RISAT-2BR1/PSLV-C48) and the band (C vs X).
RISAT-2 used X-band radar, RISAT-1 used C-band SAR at 5.35 GHz, and RISAT-2B was an X-band surveillance satellite.
RISAT-1
, launched in 2012, was India's first fully indigenous radar imaging satellite and carried a C-band SAR.
RISAT-2B performed a collision avoidance manoeuvre against a defunct US satellite using
NETRA
data.

secs.t: Student and academic satellites → institution + FIRST

x: WESAT
, built by the LBS Institute of Technology for Women in Kerala, was the first Indian satellite fully built by women students.
Jugnu was built by IIT Kanpur, SRMSAT by SRM University, SATYABAMASAT by Sathyabama University and Kalamsat-V2 by Space Kidz India.
Kalamsat-V2, built by Space Kidz India and launched on PSLV-C44 in January 2019, was the first to use the PS4 stage as an orbital platform and was the lightest.

secs.t: Foreign co-passenger and educational satellites on PSLV → country

x: PSLV-C37 launched 104 satellites on 15 February 2017, including Cartosat-2 series, two ISRO nanosatellites and 101 foreign nanosatellites.
The PSLV-C37 mission had a total payload mass of 1,378 kg and placed the satellites in a 506 km sun-synchronous orbit.
PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 was the 64th PSLV flight, the 105th launch from Sriharikota and the ninth dedicated NSIL commercial mission.

secs.t: Military satellites → service user + nickname

x: GSAT-7 serves the Navy, GSAT-7R/CMS-03 is its naval replacement, and GSAT-7B is proposed for the Army.
GSAT-7R, or CMS-03, was launched on
LVM3-M5 on 2 November 2025
as a replacement for GSAT-7 in naval service.
RISAT-2 supports radar border surveillance, Cartosat provides high-resolution border imagery, and EMISAT supports electronic intelligence.

secs.t: EDUSAT - purpose, FIRST, launch, users

x: GSAT-3, popularly known as EDUSAT, was India's first satellite dedicated to education and provided two-way satellite communication to classrooms.
EDUSAT was launched on
20 September 2004 by GSLV-F01
from Sriharikota.
EDUSAT served
schools, colleges and distance-education networks
through virtual classrooms.
EDUSAT had a lift-off mass of 1,950.5 kg, was placed at 74°E in geostationary orbit and launched from Sriharikota.

secs.t: Space-Based Surveillance, Defence Space Agency, DSRO

x: SBS-3 comprises 52 satellites, including 21 by ISRO and 31 by private industry.
The financial outlay approved for SBS-3 is
The DSA is a tri-service agency established at Bengaluru in 2019.
DSRO is the R&D arm associated with the Defence Space Agency and develops space-warfare systems and technologies for it.

secs.t: ISRO capacity-building for students - UNNATI, YUVIKA, CubeSat

x: UNNATI was launched in 2019 to commemorate
the 50th anniversary of UNISPACE-I
YUVIKA is ISRO's summer programme on space science for school students studying in Class 9.
Student CubeSats may fly on PSLV POEM, the PS4 orbital platform, or as rideshare payloads.
The ATL Space Challenge is an initiative involving the
Atal Innovation Mission, ISRO and CBSE
for school students.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: EOS-05 is intended for geosynchronous orbit at approximately 36,000 km and supports observation of floods, cyclones, fires and security-related events.
The reported relevance referred to two consecutive PSLV failures: C61 in 2025 and C62 in January 2026, which affected surveillance satellites.
The StudSat consortium included colleges from Andhra Pradesh, when the State was undivided.

rows.title: Space policy and commercialisation - Indian Space Policy 2023, IN-SPACe, NSIL, private launch sector
sub: Group-II M2-B-10: Space sector reforms - Indian Space Policy 2023, IN-SPACe, NSIL and private participation

secs.t: Private satellite firms and constellations → company; manufacturing units

x: Skyroot’s Vikram-1 carried Skyroot’s SCOPE, Grahaa Space’s SOLARAS S3 and Cosmoserve’s Embrace to 450 km low Earth orbit.
Pixxel leads the IN-SPACe-approved PPP Earth-observation constellation, whose partners include Dhruva Space, SatSure Analytics India and Piersight Space; it is identified as LENSD.
Digantara
, based in Bengaluru, works in space situational awareness, including tracking debris and other objects.

Ananth Technologies is associated with the first private satellite integration facility; Azista with the first commercial small-satellite launch from Indian soil; GalaxEye with Drishti; and Digantara with space surveillance.

secs.t: Private launch and propulsion firms → products + FIRST

x: Agnibaan was developed by
Agnikul Cosmos
and was launched from the private launch pad named Dhanush at Sriharikota.
Vikram-1 carried the
SOLARAS nanosatellite with VIT-AP University's VISWA-M solar-spectrum payload, built with Grahaa Space
All four statements correctly describe Bellatrix Aerospace, its Bengaluru base, green propulsion and electric-thruster work, the POEM-3 demonstration, and Technology Development Fund support.
Skyroot Aerospace is based in Hyderabad; Vikram-1 is India's first private orbital rocket; a VIT-AP payload flew on Vikram-1; and Sriharikota is India's only operational spaceport.

secs.t: NSIL - demand-driven missions, DTH leasing, vs Antrix

x: Under the demand-driven model, NSIL builds, owns and operates satellites against assured or committed customer demand, unlike the earlier supply-driven approach.
Ten satellites were transferred in 2022, taking NSIL’s operating fleet to 11 communication satellites, about 300 transponders and more than 150 lease agreements.
Antrix was established in September 1992 and became a Miniratna in 2008, while NSIL follows the demand-driven model and Antrix had a supply-driven commercial role.
NSIL undertakes technology transfer, launch services and satellite services, and its demand-driven model includes building, owning and operating satellites against committed demand.

secs.t: IN-SPACe - function, HQ, authorisations

x: IN-SPACe performs all four functions: promotion, authorisation and supervision of non-governmental entities, along with facilitating their access to Department of Space facilities.
IN-SPACe authorised Vikram-S, operates a Seed Fund Scheme, approved the Pixxel-led EOS constellation and enabled SSLV technology transfer to private consortia.
The PPP EOS constellation was led by Pixxel and involved Dhruva Space, SatSure and PierSight.

secs.t: Space legislation - Space Activities Bill

x: Both statements are true, and the absence of a statutory framework for liability, dispute resolution and risk-sharing directly explains the uncertainty faced by private entities.
The Liability Convention of 1972 makes the
launching State
liable for damage caused by a space object.
The proposed legislative framework is expected to cover dual-use regulation, treaty compliance, private-activity licensing and statutory arrangements concerning liability and risk-sharing.

secs.t: Indian Space Policy 2023 - roles

x: ISRO is assigned advanced research and development, deep-space activities and human spaceflight, while gradually moving away from operational and commercial satellite and rocket production.

NSIL commercialises mature ISRO technology; the Department of Space handles policy and cooperation; non-governmental entities undertake end-to-end activities; and ISRO focuses on advanced research and strategic missions.

secs.t: Space sector reforms 2020 - FDI limits

x: Manufacturing of satellite components and subsystems is permitted up to
through the automatic route.

The automatic route permits 74% in satellite manufacturing, operations and data products, 49% in launch vehicles and spaceports, and investment above the applicable limits requires government approval.

secs.t: Space economy - size, target, venture fund

x: The ₹1,000 crore Venture Capital Fund for space start-ups is to be managed through
SIDBI
over a period of five years.
Downstream data services are expected to generate approximately
of future space-sector revenues.
The stated objective is to raise India’s share of the global space economy to about 8%, along with expansion from approximately US$8 billion to US$44 billion by 2033.

secs.t: AP space manufacturing policy and space cities

x: Andhra Pradesh has announced Space Policy 4.0 and is developing dedicated space cities to promote space manufacturing and related activities.
The Tirupati Space City is planned over approximately
3,000 acres
near Sriharikota.
The Tirupati Space City is intended for launch-vehicle assembly, satellite manufacturing and avionics.
The AP Space Tech Summit-2026 was held at Vignan’s University in Vadlamudi, Guntur.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All three statements describe concerns associated with India's space-sector ecosystem: the absence of a Space Activities Act, dependence on imported space-grade chips exceeding 90%, and the lack of sovereign-backed insurance for long-gestation ventures.
Eighteen collision-avoidance manoeuvres were carried out in low Earth orbit in 2025, reflecting the growing problem of LEO congestion.

rows.title: Applications of space technology - agriculture, disaster management, telemedicine, tele-education, navigation
sub: Group-II M2-B-11: Applications of space technology in agriculture, disaster management, navigation and governance

secs.t: Remote sensing in disaster management - can/cannot monitor, satellites, fire hotspots, DMS

x: Exam angle: "which CANNOT be monitored" - answer is always the human-health event.
Resourcesat and Oceansat use naturally available radiation in passive remote sensing, while RISAT employs its own radar signal and is an active system.
Bhuvan combines RISAT/SAR flood-related imagery and INSAT-3DS cyclone-track information to support flood-inundation mapping and cyclone warnings.
Fire hotspots are detected using thermal-infrared sensors, particularly MODIS on NASA's Terra and Aqua satellites and VIIRS on Suomi-NPP.

The DMS Programme uses INSAT and IRS, is recognised as an INSAT application, and provides satellite imaging and communication support for floods, cyclones, droughts, fires, landslides and earthquakes.

secs.t: Bhuvan geoportals - versions, developer, SVAMITVA, Gati Shakti

x: Bhuvan Panchayat supports Gram Panchayat planning; Yuktdhara concerns MGNREGA assets; SVAMITVA uses drone mapping and provides property cards; PM Gati Shakti is the National Master Plan GIS platform.
SVAMITVA involves drone mapping of rural inhabited properties in association with the Survey of India and supports the issue of property cards.

secs.t: Spectral indices and bands - NDVI, cloud-covered areas, InSAR

x: Microwave radar and SAR signals can penetrate clouds and operate in darkness, making them suitable for all-weather observation.
InSAR can map ground deformation associated with earthquakes, land subsidence, landslides, volcanoes and glacier movement.
Assam is reported to be cloudy for about
half the year
; SAR is useful because it can observe through cloud cover.

secs.t: Agriculture - drought monitoring, FASAL, CHAMAN, soil moisture

x: FASAL
provides pre-harvest crop acreage and production forecasts using space, agro-meteorological and land-based observations.
Microwave and SAR sensors are particularly suitable for soil-moisture measurement; NISAR uses L-band and S-band radar for such applications.
L-band and S-band
radar are the bands mentioned for NISAR’s soil-moisture-related sensing capability.
The CROP framework estimated rabi 2024–25 wheat production at
122.724 million tonnes
using EOS-04, EOS-06 and Resourcesat-2A.

secs.t: Fisheries and maritime safety - PFZ, safety devices, surveillance

x: Nabhmitra is a satellite-based fishermen safety device developed by ISRO’s Space Applications Centre, Ahmedabad, and tested at Neendakara in August 2023.
GEMINI sends
PFZ, Ocean State Forecast and disaster alerts
to fishermen at sea, using GAGAN-related capability.
The RTGS hub at Vijayawada provides satellite-based alerts to coastal fishermen about
cyclones, high waves and fish shoals

secs.t: GIS - components, data layers, situational awareness

x: Computers, digitizers, scanners, GPS receivers and plotters are examples of GIS hardware.
GIS data includes spatial data such as vector points, lines and polygons and raster satellite images, along with attribute tables.
Situational awareness uses real-time layers for disaster response, including flood alerts and mineral-vehicle tracking, as well as shoreline mapping.

secs.t: Agency → remote sensing role

x: The
National Remote Sensing Centre
(NRSC), Hyderabad, receives, processes and supplies satellite data, runs Bhuvan and supports States in disaster management.
IIRS provides training and education; NESAC serves the North-East; SAC works on sensors and applications; and the five RRSCs undertake regional projects for States.
APSAC is associated with drought monitoring using the Vegetation Condition Index (VCI), while YESTECH is associated with yield estimation.

secs.t: Weather and lightning alert apps → developer

x: The City Flood Alert application has all three features: the stated institutional collaboration, AI-based forecasting and the specified warning periods.
The system was first implemented in
Vijayawada
, using satellite digital elevation models and Budameru flood data.
City Flood Alert involves RTGS, APSDMA and IIT Gandhinagar, provides six-hour warnings, and was first implemented in Vijayawada.

secs.t: Telemedicine and tele-education - networks, Village Resource Centres

x: Village Resource Centres are single-window centres combining tele-education, telemedicine, weather information and remote-sensing-based land and water advisories.
INSAT and GSAT
satellite communication systems have enabled tele-education, telemedicine and Village Resource Centres.
Swayam Prabha provides 40 free DTH channels through GSAT-15.
The ISRO Telemedicine Network links
border posts and rural clinics
through satellite-enabled medical services.

secs.t: Remote sensing applications - what can/cannot be measured; NDVI

x: Remote sensing can assess land cover, forest cover and crop area or yield, but it cannot measure an
individual bank-account balance
Healthy vegetation reflects strongly in the near-infrared band
, which is why NIR is used in vegetation indices such as NDVI.
The NH Green Cover Index is
India’s first satellite-based green-cover assessment of highways
and uses chlorophyll detection.

secs.t: Navigation applications - devices, fishermen alerts, tracking, GPS uses

x: Nabhmitra is an ISRO-SAC
fishermen
-safety device, tested at Neendakara in Kerala in August 2023.
IRNSS-1F
continued one-way messaging despite its clock failure.
The Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicle Tracking System fitted 50,000
mineral vehicles
with AIS-140 tracking devices.
Satellite time is used by banks to time-stamp transactions and by power grids to synchronise their phase.

secs.t: AP Space Applications Centre (APSAC) - state mapping

x: APSSDI standardises GIS layers and supports spatial mapping; the satellite-based lightning alert application is not its stated function.
APSAC undertakes YES-TECH yield estimation in
Nandyal and Kakinada
with ISRO and the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
APSSDI standardised 74 GIS layers at a cost of Rs 15.76 crore, with a 70:30 Centre–State sharing ratio.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The clock of IRNSS-1F failed on
13 March 2026
, contributing to the reported reduction in NavIC's PNT capability.
Swayam Prabha, telemedicine and KASTURI heritage tours
are cited as examples of space technology being used in governance and public services.
KASTURI heritage tours are associated with
Cartosat-3
, demonstrating the use of space technology for heritage-related governance applications.

rows.title: Space debris, space situational awareness and international space law

secs.t: Space situational awareness - IS4OM, Project NETRA

x: Exam angle: "NETRA - which agency / what aim" → ISRO / safeguard Indian space assets.
Project NETRA aims to provide indigenous space situational awareness and
safeguard Indian space assets from debris and collisions
IS4OM, or ISRO System for Safe and Sustainable Space Operations Management, tracks debris, predicts trajectories and protects Indian satellites.

secs.t: Debris Free Space Missions - target year, POEM de-orbiting

x: Inflatable sails are drag-augmentation devices that help POEM re-enter within months rather than remaining in orbit for decades.
PSLV-C62 was planned to restart PS4 and de-boost it into a re-entry trajectory after payload injection.
The planned ADR mission involves a servicer craft equipped with a robotic arm or net to capture a defunct Indian rocket body; it is being tested at URSC.

secs.t: Space debris - sources, Kessler syndrome

x: Defunct satellites, spent rocket stages, tools lost during spacewalks and ASAT tests are all sources of space debris.
Kessler Syndrome is the self-sustaining cascade of collisions caused by high debris density, potentially making orbital regions unusable.
Mission Shakti was a DRDO kinetic-kill anti-satellite test that destroyed the Indian satellite Microsat-R at approximately 300 km altitude, raising debris concerns.

secs.t: Outer space treaties - India's status

x: Article VI deals with national responsibility, including responsibility relating to private actors.
The Rescue Agreement, 1968 deals with the return of astronauts and objects.
India has signed the Moon Agreement, 1979, but has not ratified it.
The Outer Space Treaty does not recognise sovereignty or ownership merely through landing.

secs.t: UNCOPUOS and IADC - India's membership

x: The UN Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space was established in 1959, and India is a founding member.
UNCOPUOS guidelines on long-term sustainability and debris mitigation guide India's
Department of Space
IADC was established in 1993, and ISRO is a member.
The Zero Debris Charter was signed by 12 nations.

secs.t: Artemis Accords - India's signing

x: The Artemis Accords were launched by the United States in 2020 and set out non-binding principles for peaceful and transparent exploration.
The Artemis Accords had more than 60 signatories by 2026.

secs.t: Space traffic management - collision avoidance manoeuvres

x: RISAT-2B performed a collision avoidance manoeuvre to avoid
a defunct US satellite
Regular CAMs involved Cartosat, Resourcesat and GSAT during 2021–25, 18 CAMs were recorded in 2025, and their purpose is collision avoidance and satellite safeguarding.
The rules turn the soft-law guidance of the Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee (IADC) and UNCOPUOS into domestic requirements.

secs.t: Weaponisation of space - PAROS, ASAT test moratorium

x: PAROS expands to Prevention of an Arms Race in Outer Space, is a UN Conference on Disarmament agenda item and is supported by UNGA resolutions.
The United States
declared the moratorium on destructive direct-ascent ASAT tests in April 2022, and the issue was subsequently taken up in a UNGA resolution.
The proposed measures include limits on destructive ASAT tests and deliberate debris creation, behaviour-based norms, SSA data-sharing and confidence-building measures.

secs.t: Private debris tracking firms in India

x: Digantara is a Bengaluru-based space-situational-awareness start-up that is building space-surveillance satellites and generating debris-tracking data.
The policy push encourages private LiDAR satellites and expansion of NETRA with radars and telescopes; it does not restrict debris tracking exclusively to government agencies.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All three developments are identified as current-relevance factors: ISSAR 2025 was released in April 2026, re-entry rules were introduced in August 2026, and the BRICS HoSA meeting in Bengaluru discussed space sustainability and debris-free missions.
Many space treaties date from the 1960s and 1970s and do not adequately address cumulative harm or the challenges posed by mega-constellations.

rows.title: DRDO - vision, mission, structure, major laboratories and technology clusters
sub: Group-II M2-B-12: DRDO - structure, vision and mission

secs.t: DRDO laboratories - full form, location, field

x: Exam angle: "RCI, Hyderabad stands for?" (Research Centre Imarat) and "DFRL is at?" (Mysuru). Hyderabad is the missile hub: DRDL, RCI, ASL, DMRL and DLRL are all there.
The
Aeronautical Development Establishment
(ADE), Bengaluru works on UAVs such as Rustom/TAPAS BH-201, Nishant and the Lakshya target drone.
The Defence Institute of Physiology and Allied Sciences (DIPAS) is located in Delhi and studies soldier physiology, including high-altitude and cold conditions.
Research Centre Imarat (
RCI
), Hyderabad specialises in missile guidance and avionics, including IIR seekers, Ku-band RF seekers and navigation systems.

secs.t: DRDO-academia centres - host institution

x: DIA-CoEs are a network of 15 DRDO Industry Academia Centres of Excellence at premier institutions such as IITs, IISc and central universities.
The proposed division was for academia to undertake early-stage R&D, with laboratories, start-ups and MSMEs helping take products to deployment.

JCBCAT was referenced in 2018, the Young Scientist Laboratories were established in 2020, the DIA-CoEs network is identified as a 15-centre network, and the five laboratories and fifteen centres were referred to in 2026.

secs.t: Spin-off technologies for civilian use - lab

x: Lukoskin is a polyherbal product used for leucoderma or white patches and was developed by DIBER at Haldwani.
Bio-toilets or bio-digesters for human-waste treatment in railway coaches were developed by
DRDE, Gwalior and DRL, Tezpur
2-DG, or 2-deoxy-D-glucose, is an
oral anti-COVID drug developed by INMAS with Dr Reddy's

secs.t: DRDO - formation, predecessors, motto, parent department

x: Exam angle: motto-matching questions. Tejasvinavadhitamastu is not DRDO's motto; Balasya Mulam Vigyanam is.
The hierarchy is Ministry of Defence, Department of Defence R&D, Secretary DD R&D who is also Chairman DRDO, Director Generals and then laboratory directors.
The current vision of DRDO is
to empower the nation with state-of-the-art indigenous defence and security technologies
All four statements describe elements of DRDO's mission, including production-oriented development, indigenous capability, combat effectiveness, troop well-being and Aatmanirbharta.

secs.t: Technology clusters - constituent labs

x: Aeronautics includes ADE, GTRE, CABS and ADRDE; Missiles and Strategic Systems includes DRDL, RCI and ASL; Naval Systems and Materials includes NSTL, NPOL and NMRL; Combat Vehicles includes CVRDE and VRDE.
The Electronics and Communication cluster focuses on
radar and electronic warfare
and includes laboratories such as LRDE, DLRL, DEAL and CAIR.

secs.t: Technology Development Fund (TDF) - support for industry and start-ups

x: The new TDF policies focus on
deep-tech and cutting-edge technologies
and seek greater participation of private firms in co-development.
DRDO helped ISRO test the Gaganyaan
crew-escape parachute recovery system
Samir V. Kamat has been DRDO Chairman since 2022, also serves as Secretary, DDR&D, and the 2020 reform allowed royalty-free industry access to DRDO patents.

secs.t: DRDO leadership - Chairman and Secretary DDR&D

x: All three statements correctly describe the three-level DRDO hierarchy: Secretary DDR&D and Chairman at Level I, the two DGs at Level II, and lab directors and corporate directorates at Level III.
Dr. Samir V. Kamat
had been Chairman of DRDO since 2022 and continued in office in 2026 while holding the post of Secretary DDR&D.

secs.t: DRDO facilities in AP - purpose

x: NSTL, Visakhapatnam
develops the Multi-Influence Ground Mine and SMART, or Supersonic Missile Assisted Release of Torpedo.
Nagayalanka is the site of the planned DRDO missile test range in coastal Krishna district, intended for flight trials of tactical missiles and sea-skimming trials.
The ADA Aircraft Integration and Flight Testing Complex in Sri Sathya Sai district had its groundbreaking in 2026 and involves an investment of ₹15,803 crore.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: DRDO designed or contributed to systems including
Agni, Prithvi, Tejas, Pinaka and Akash
, forming part of the foundation of Aatmanirbharta in defence.
The AP defence-infrastructure locations highlighted are NSTL at Visakhapatnam, the Kurnool test range, the planned Nagayalanka range and the ADA complex in Sri Sathya Sai district.
The DRDO CBRN Field Training Centre is located in Delhi and is associated with the Institute of Nuclear Medicine and Allied Sciences (INMAS).

rows.title: Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme - Prithvi, Agni, Akash, Trishul, Nag
sub: Group-II M2-B-14: Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme - Prithvi, Agni, Akash, Trishul and Nag

secs.t: IGMDP missiles - type, range class, service

x: Exam angle: "Which is a fire-and-forget anti-tank missile?" The answer is Nag (Prithvi, Akash and Trishul are not).
Akash is a medium-range SAM, Trishul is a short-range low-level SAM, and Nag is a third-generation ATGM.
Akash is a medium-range surface-to-air missile with a range of about 25–30 km, a speed of approximately Mach 2.5 and an altitude capability of 18 km.
The phases were Prithvi and Trishul during 1984–89, Nag and Akash during 1989–92, and Agni during 1992–2008.

secs.t: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status

x: Exam angle: "not correct about Agni-5" → "not exclusively indigenous".
The advanced Agni MIRV test, Agni-1 test and Agni-4 user trial reported in 2026 were conducted under the
Strategic Forces Command
The advanced Agni MIRV test occurred on 8 May 2026, Agni-1 was tested from ITR Balasore on 22 May 2026, and Agni-4 from ITR Chandipur on 6 August 2026.

The sequence is multi-layered BMD and NASM-MR tests in June 2026, the Kusha LR-SAM maiden test in July 2026, and IADWS in August 2025 would actually precede both 2026 events; therefore the correct chronological.

secs.t: Missile variants and successors

x: Akash Prime is an upgraded Akash Mk-I fitted with an indigenous active Radio Frequency seeker.
The Akash Prime trials demonstrated the destruction of high-speed targets at high altitude in
Ladakh
Nag Mk-2 or
NAMIS is a tracked tank killer approved for Army procurement
HELINA is the helicopter-launched Nag variant for Army Aviation, whereas Dhruvastra is intended for the Indian Air Force.
Nag uses an Imaging Infra-Red seeker, whereas Akash Prime uses an active RF seeker and SANT uses Lock-On After Launch.

secs.t: Guidance features - fire-and-forget, top attack, seekers

x: SANT is an air-launched stand-off anti-tank guided missile employing
Lock-On After Launch
guidance.
A fire-and-forget missile guides itself after launch, enabling the operator to seek cover or perform another task.
Nag carries an 8 kg HEAT tandem warhead; NAMICA can carry up to six missiles; and the Nag Missile Carrier is a tracked amphibious vehicle.

secs.t: IGMDP - launch, leaders, closed projects

x: Trishul was closed on 27 February 2008 after failing to meet operational requirements and suffering delays and cost overruns.
The replacements were
Israeli Spyder for the IAF, Barak-1 for the Navy and Akash for the Army
Long-range tracking systems, composites, ring laser gyros and radomes were identified as IGMDP spin-offs.

secs.t: Missile names - meanings; which systems are not missiles

x: Agni means Fire, Akash means Sky, Trishul means Trident and Nag means Cobra or serpent.
Arjun
is a tank, not a missile.
Pinaka is a multi-barrel rocket launcher, Tejas is an aircraft, Lakshya is a target drone, and Nishant is a UAV; none is a missile.
Rustom is an unmanned aerial vehicle.

secs.t: Missile test ranges - names, state

x: The Integrated Test Range is located at Chandipur in Balasore district of
Odisha
The DRDO range near Kurnool in Andhra Pradesh was used for
ULPGM-V3 trials
Coastal ranges in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha support sea-skimming missile trials; Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island is off the Odisha coast, and LRAShM is cited as an example.

secs.t: Missile Technology Control Regime - India's membership

x: India joined the MTCR in June 2016 as its 35th member.
The MTCR concerns missiles and UAVs able to carry a 500 kg payload over a range of 300 km.
India's MTCR membership facilitated BrahMos exports and high-technology imports.

secs.t: Persons in the missile programme → role and title

x: Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was the
Chief Scientific Adviser
at Pokhran in 1998.
Dr Tessy Thomas is known as the “Missile Woman of India”, played a key role in Agni-V and is called “Agniputri”.
Dr V.K. Saraswat was a former DRDO chief and led the Prithvi and ballistic missile defence programmes.

secs.t: Trishul - speed class, outcome, successors

x: The approximate range of Trishul was about
9 km
; another stated figure placed it at 12 km, but the cited approximate value is 9 km.
Trishul was never inducted, and its programme was shut on 27 February 2008 because of delays and cost overruns.
QRSAM
, or Quick Reaction Surface-to-Air Missile, is the later indigenous short-range successor to Trishul.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Trishul
is the IGMDP missile that was never inducted; its programme was shut in 2008.
The IGMDP transformed India from a missile importer into a missile-exporting power and provided the foundation for Agni-V MIRV, ballistic missile defence and BrahMos-era programmes.
The approval provides for transfer of technology of conventional missiles, including Nag, to private industry, while Agni remains in state production.

rows.title: Missiles beyond IGMDP - BrahMos, Nirbhay, Astra, Pralay, hypersonic technology, Mission Shakti (ASAT)
sub: Group-II M2-B-15: Missiles beyond IGMDP - BrahMos, Astra, Nirbhay, hypersonic systems and Mission Shakti

secs.t: BrahMos - partner, name, speed, variants, test sites

x: Exam angle: "BrahMos is developed by India and ___" (Russia). This was asked in APPSC G2 2025.
BrahMos uses a solid booster and liquid ramjet, combines inertial and satellite navigation, and can be fired from a Transport Launch Canister in fire-and-forget mode.
The base system has land, ship, submarine and air-launched versions; BrahMos-NG is a lighter version for platforms including Tejas; and BrahMos-II is planned as a hypersonic missile.
Extended-range BrahMos versions have a range of about 400 km or more, with the range described as approximately 450 km after India’s entry into the MTCR in 2016.

The land-attack version uses mobile Army launchers, the ship-launched version is carried by warships, the submarine version is carried by submarines, and the air-launched version is associated with the Su-30MKI.

secs.t: Mission Shakti ASAT - date, agencies, orbit, target, rank

x: Exam angle: PYQ statement pairs. "Destroyed a live satellite in LEO" is correct. "Done in the upper atmosphere so there is no debris" is wrong.
A DRDO PDV Mk-II interceptor destroyed the live satellite Microsat-R during Mission Shakti.
The BrahMos agreement was signed in 1998, BrahMos was first successfully tested in 2001, Microsat-R was launched in January 2019, and Mission Shakti took place in March 2019.
The interception was conducted at a low LEO altitude so that the resulting debris would decay relatively quickly.

secs.t: Other new missiles - type

x: Pralay is a quasi-ballistic short-range tactical surface-to-surface missile with a 150–500 km range, conventional warhead and manoeuvrable re-entry capability.
Shaurya
is a canister-launched hypersonic surface-to-surface tactical missile with a range of about 700–1,900 km and nuclear capability.
QRSAM, or Quick Reaction Surface-to-Air Missile, forms
the mid-range layer of the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System
LRGB Gaurav was released in April 2025, Pinaka LRGR-120 first flew on 29 December 2025, Pralay's salvo occurred on 31 December 2025, and NASM-MR's maiden flight was on 14 June 2026.
Rudram is the first indigenous anti-radiation missile; Mission Shakti made India the fourth ASAT nation; the Philippines was the first BrahMos buyer; and Indonesia was the first Astra buyer.

secs.t: Jointly developed and imported missiles - partner country

x: Spyder is an Israeli system used by the Indian Air Force and replaced Trishul.
The R-73 Archer is a
Russian short-range air-to-air missile
BrahMos is a joint venture with Russia, while R-73 Archer and S-400 are Russian systems.

secs.t: Foreign missile tests - country

x: Fattah is associated with Iran, Hwasong with North Korea, and Zircon with Russia.
Minuteman III is a United States intercontinental ballistic missile and forms the land leg of the US nuclear triad.
Kinzhal is a Russian air-launched hypersonic missile.
Abdali is a
Pakistan
i 450 km surface-to-surface missile named after Ahmed Shah Abdali.

secs.t: Astra - air-to-air class, variants, platforms

x: Astra is a DRDO-developed family of beyond-visual-range air-to-air missiles using an active radar seeker.
Astra Mk-1 has a range of 80–110 km, a speed of Mach 4.5 and an altitude capability up to 20 km.
Astra Mk-1 is deployed on the Su-30MKI and is planned for integration with the Tejas Mk-1A and Rafale.
The Aeronautical Development Agency test-fired Astra from an
LCA AF Mk1 prototype
on 12 March 2025.

secs.t: Missile classes and hypersonic technology

x: A ballistic missile is powered mainly during the boost phase and subsequently follows a high parabolic or free-fall trajectory.
India's HSTDV flew at above Mach 6 and validated scramjet combustion and thermal protection at temperatures exceeding 2,000°C.
The long-range hypersonic anti-ship missile is intended for naval coastal batteries, has a range of about 1,500 km or more, reaches up to Mach 10, and uses a two-stage solid motor.
SFDR uses atmospheric air for combustion and was demonstrated from ITR Chandipur for application in
long-range air-to-air missiles
In FOBS, the warhead enters a partial low orbit and can descend towards the target from an unexpected or different direction.

secs.t: Nirbhay and ITCM - cruise missile class

x: Nirbhay has an approximate range of 1,000 km, uses a turbojet, can carry conventional or nuclear warheads, and has a payload of about 200–300 kg.
Nirbhay hugs the terrain at low altitude, which helps it evade or reduce radar detection.
ITCM is the successor to Nirbhay and is powered by the indigenous
Manik small turbofan engine
developed by GTRE.

secs.t: Missile exports - buyers, first deliveries

x: The Philippines
became India's first BrahMos export customer through a 2022 deal valued at $375 million.
BrahMos deliveries to the Philippines began from 2024.
The Philippines received BrahMos as India's first export customer, Indonesia was associated with the first Astra Mk-1 export deal, and the UAE was in early-stage talks for BrahMos and Akashteer.

secs.t: Air-defence shields - Sudarshan Chakra, BMD (PAD, AAD, Phase-II)

x: Phase-I exo-atmospheric interception uses PAD/Pradyumna; Phase-I endo-atmospheric interception uses AAD/Ashwin; Phase-II uses AD-1 for exo-atmospheric and AD-2 for endo-atmospheric interception.

AD-1 is the Phase-II exo-atmospheric interceptor, AD-2 is the Phase-II endo-atmospheric interceptor under development, and India has demonstrated multi-layered BMD capability against threats up to ICBM class.
Prithvi Air Defence or Pradyumna is an exo-atmospheric interceptor operating at 50–80 km altitude, while AAD or Ashwin is an endo-atmospheric interceptor operating at 15–30 km.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Ranges along the Andhra Pradesh coast were used for LRAShM validation rounds.
The assessment states that the systems are not yet fully integrated and that the rocket force remains only a concept.
The assessment is that hypersonic technology is still maturing.

rows.title: Missile defence and strategic forces - BMD programme, nuclear triad, SSBN, no-first-use policy

secs.t: Nuclear tests - Pokhran I and II

x: Pokhran-I took place on 18 May 1974 under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and was officially described as a peaceful nuclear explosion.
Pokhran-II was conducted under A.B. Vajpayee, involved A.P.J. Abdul Kalam and R. Chidambaram, and included fission as well as fusion devices.
Pokhran-II, known as Operation Shakti, was conducted on
11 and 13 May 1998
under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

secs.t: Air defence systems - origin and operators

x: IADWS is a multi-layered indigenous system comprising
QRSAM, VSHORADS and a high-power laser directed-energy weapon
Mission Sudarshan Chakra is envisaged as a networked national shield integrating
air defence, cybersecurity and surveillance
Project Kusha is reported as a long-range air-defence project with M1, M2 and M3 interceptors of about
ranges, respectively.

secs.t: Nuclear weapon technology terms

x: A fission weapon splits a heavy nucleus such as U-235 or Pu-239, whereas a fusion weapon combines light hydrogen isotopes.
All three statements correctly state the approximate enrichment levels of reactor-grade LEU, HEU and weapons-grade uranium.
A neutron striking U-235 can split it into two smaller nuclei, such as barium and krypton, while releasing two or three neutrons that sustain the chain reaction.

secs.t: Nuclear submarines - Arihant class, leased SSNs, K-series, ATV

x: The ATV programme involved DRDO, private firms and
Russia
n assistance in developing India's nuclear-powered submarine capability.
The Advanced Technology Vessel project was initiated more than three decades ago by DRDO and private firms, with Russian assistance, to build SSBNs.
INS Chakra was a leased Charlie-class submarine obtained in 1988, while INS Chakra II was the Russian Akula-class boat formerly known as Nerpa.

secs.t: Ballistic Missile Defence - two tiers, interceptors, Phase II

x: In June 2026, DRDO demonstrated a multi-layered BMD system with interceptors destroying targets, placing India among the few countries capable of engaging threats up to ICBM class.
NASM-MR stands for a
naval anti-ship missile of medium range
, whose maiden test took place in the same series as the June 2026 BMD demonstration.

secs.t: Nuclear doctrine 2003 - tenets, NCA, SFC

x: The Political Council is headed by the Prime Minister, the Executive Council by the National Security Adviser, the Strategic Forces Command manages nuclear forces, and civilian political control is supervised by the CCS.
All three statements reflect the stated tenets: massive retaliation, non-use against non-nuclear-weapon states and retention of the nuclear option against a major biological or chemical attack.

secs.t: Non-proliferation regimes - India's status and reasons

x: India considers the NPT discriminatory because it creates an unequal division between recognised nuclear-weapon states and other states, a position often described as opposition to nuclear apartheid.
India has not signed the CTBT because it seeks a link between the treaty and
time-bound global nuclear disarmament
; it nevertheless observes a voluntary test moratorium.

secs.t: Nuclear triad - land, air and sea platforms

x: The air leg is represented by
Jaguar and Mirage 2000
aircraft carrying free-fall nuclear bombs.
Dhanush was fired from ships, including INS Subhadra and INS Rajput; it is distinct from the K-15 and K-4 SLBMs deployed on SSBNs.
SSBNs are difficult to detect and destroy, thereby supporting a reliable second-strike capability that underpins India’s No First Use posture.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: SIPRI counted 12 Indian warheads as operationally deployed in the cited June 2026 assessment, linked to SSBN deterrence patrols and canisterised Agni systems.
The Agni-4 user trial on 6 August 2026 involved a 4,000 km-range, two-stage solid-fuel missile that is road-mobile.
The US triad consists of Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missiles, strategic bombers and Ohio/Columbia-class SSBNs.

rows.title: Defence platforms and systems - Tejas LCA, Arjun MBT, radar and EW systems, naval platforms
sub: Group-II M2-B-13: Technologies developed by DRDO - platforms, sensors, materials and spin-off technologies

secs.t: Aircraft - developer or origin, role, numbers

x: The C-130J is used for tactical transport and special operations; the C-17 for strategic heavy lift; the IL-76 for heavy transport; and the IL-78 as a mid-air refuelling tanker.
The C-295 is a
medium tactical transport
aircraft produced through cooperation between Airbus of Spain and Tata.
The 2025 HAL contract covers 97 LCA Mk1A aircraft, comprising 68 fighters and 29 twin-seaters, at a value of ₹62,370 crore, and was signed on 25 September 2025.

secs.t: Naval platforms - class, type, builder; commissionings

x: The Kalvari class belongs to Project 75, comprises six French-design Scorpene diesel-electric submarines, and INS Vaghsheer is the last boat.
Project 15B consists of Visakhapatnam-class
stealth guided-missile destroyers built by Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders
Project 17A consists of seven multi-mission stealth frigates with CODOG propulsion, speeds above 28 knots, and systems including BrahMos and MRSAM/Barak-8.
TAL is a lightweight torpedo, Maareech is an anti-torpedo decoy, USHUS is an integrated submarine sonar, and ERASR is an anti-submarine rocket.
INS Astradharini is an indigenous torpedo launch and recovery vessel used for trials of DRDO underwater weapons; it was commissioned in 2024 at Visakhapatnam.
The 2026 inductions included ASW shallow-water craft Agray, Malwan and Anjadip, survey vessel Sanshodhak, and NGOPVs Sanghmitra and Shachi.
Project-75(I) concerns next-generation conventional submarines with air-independent propulsion, with Navantia of Spain and L&T signing a teaming agreement in July 2023.
Nilgiri, Udaygiri and Himgiri were delivered in 2025; Taragiri is the fourth ship and INS Mahendragiri is the seventh ship of Project 17A.

secs.t: Shipyards - location, ownership, FIRST

x: Hindustan Shipyard Limited at Visakhapatnam was founded in 1941 by Scindia Steam Navigation and built Jala Usha, the first Indian-built ship, in 1948.
Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders is located in Mumbai and builds destroyers, Project 17A frigates and Scorpene submarines.
Goa Shipyard is located at Vasco da Gama in Goa, is a defence PSU, and builds Adamya-class fast patrol vessels for the Coast Guard.

secs.t: Radar and EW - types, indigenous radars, AEW&C

x: Doppler radar
measures speed through the frequency shift of the returned signal and is used in weather radars.
Active Electronically Scanned Array radar has a transmit/receive module on each element and steers its beam electronically without a moving antenna.
Over-the-horizon radar uses high-frequency waves reflected by the ionosphere, enabling observation beyond the geometric horizon.
Swordfish
is the long-range tracking radar of the ballistic missile defence shield, with a range exceeding 1,500 km.
Surya is a VHF-band surveillance radar designed to track stealth aircraft; long wavelengths are useful against stealth targets.
AWACS is the larger, longer-range platform with full air-battle control, while Netra is a smaller jet offering early warning and command-and-control over a shorter range.

secs.t: Counter-drone and loitering munitions

x: Bhargavastra
is an indigenous counter-drone system that fires 64 micro-rockets at drone swarms.
Akash Tarang is an indigenous anti-UAV EW system using soft-kill jamming, approved for procurement in July 2026 and included in the Sudarshan Chakra layered air shield.
Vayu Astra is
an indigenous loitering munition developed by NIBE Ltd
Electronic warfare uses electromagnetic energy to control the spectrum, deny its effective use to the enemy and protect friendly sensors.

secs.t: Coast Guard - vessel classes and roles

x: The stated figures are
152 ships, 78 aircraft, 42 stations, 11 air stations and 84 radar stations
The Adamya-class vessels are being built by Goa Shipyard and perform surveillance, anti-smuggling and SAR roles.
As an air cushion vehicle, H-561 can operate over mudflats and sandbars, including areas such as the Rann of Kutch and the Sundarbans.

secs.t: Maritime domain awareness - IFC-IOR, coastal radars, ENC in AP

x: The IFC-IOR facilitates the sharing of white-shipping and maritime-security information with partner countries.
The Indian Coast Guard's 84 radar stations form a coastal surveillance network established after 26/11.
INS Dega is the naval air station of the Eastern Naval Command.
The SAGAR and MAHASAGAR visions guide India's maritime and naval capabilities.

secs.t: Land systems - developer or origin

x: Exam angle: "What is PINAKA?" → Indian multi-barrel rocket system.
ATAGS is
a 155 mm towed gun developed by DRDO's ARDE with Indian industry
Dhanush is a 155 mm gun based on the Bofors design and was associated with the Ordnance Factory Board at Jabalpur.
LCA Tejas is a light, multirole fourth-generation fighter developed by ADA with DRDO and built by HAL.
The Mk-1A includes the Uttam AESA radar, an EW suite and air-to-air refuelling capability.
The maiden test of LRGR-120 took place at ITR Chandipur on
29 December 2025

secs.t: Stealth and defence materials

x: Radar cross-section can be reduced through
shaping, radar-absorbent coatings and flush-mounted weapons

high-altitude agriculture and herbal products

Eastern Naval Command
refit yard.

secs.t: Energy Statistics India - publisher and indicators

x: Energy Statistics was published by the Central Statistics Office (CSO), now the National Statistics Office (NSO) under MoSPI.
Energy Statistics covers reserves and potential, installed capacity, production, imports and exports, consumption and energy balance for major energy sources.

The reported CAGR for the increase from 15,296 MJ to 18,096 MJ was about

secs.t: Per-capita energy and electricity consumption - world gap, HDI link

x: All four statements correctly reproduce the 2024 comparison: India 1,418 kWh, China 7,097 kWh, the USA 12,701 kWh and the OECD average a little above 8,000 kWh.
Per-capita electricity consumption acts as a proxy for energy use, and a certain minimum level is required to ensure a minimally acceptable level of well-being.

x: Solar had 157 GW, wind 56.8 GW, nuclear 8.78 GW and small hydro 5.18 GW of installed capacity.
Coal was the largest source with 230 GW, followed by solar with 157 GW, approximately 29% of installed capacity.
Energy crisis refers to the danger of exhaustion of fossil fuels such as coal and petroleum.

secs.t: Primary energy demand - India's global rank

x: India is the world’s second-largest coal consumer, and its energy demand is expected to triple by 2047.

secs.t: Peak demand vs peak met - deficit trend (CEA)

x: Exam angle: "near-zero peak deficit" questions; the evening non-solar peak is the new gap.
Peak demand met was 256.1 GW on 25 April 2026, and about
one-third
of it was met by renewable energy.
Although solar-hour supply has improved, the non-solar evening peak still creates a deficit, making storage important for meeting that period’s demand.

x: Per-capita electricity consumption is projected to increase from 887 kWh to
The NGAP identifies a storage requirement of 174 GW/888 GWh, including 94 GW of pumped storage and 80 GW of battery energy storage systems.

The plan is part of the CEA's resource adequacy process, recommends about 5,588 MW of thermal capacity, and APERC cleared the first 1,600 MW.

secs.t: Sector-wise energy consumption

x: Industry
was the largest consuming sector in the IESS 2012 base, with consumption of 2,367 TWh.
The descending order is industry at 2,367 TWh, cooking at 1,072 TWh, transport at 929 TWh and buildings at 238 TWh.
Cooking demand is expected to fall as clean fuels replace biomass, while industry remains the largest sector with 8,764 TWh under business as usual in 2040.

secs.t: Energy intensity of GDP - trend and NDC link

x: The 2015 first NDC targeted a 33–35% reduction in intensity from 2005 levels and 40% non-fossil capacity by 2030.
The updated 2022 NDC targets 45% intensity reduction and 50% non-fossil capacity by 2030, while the 2031–35 NDC gives 47% and 60% targets respectively.
The Bureau of Energy Efficiency and the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency under NAPCC work through Energy Service Companies under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001.

of coal-based power on 6 August 2026.

The Andhra Pradesh arrangement includes 1,500 MW/6,000 MWh of BESS and an additional 500 MW/1,000 MWh under VGF with NHPC.

x: Electric vehicles, farm pumps, appliances, cooling demand, data centres and telecom operations all contribute to rising electricity demand.
Peak demand increased from 183 GW in December 2020 to more than
250 GW
in April 2026, representing a rise of about 37%.
Data centres and telecom networks require continuous and reliable power, thereby increasing the need for dependable generation and grid management.

secs.t: Peak shortage vs energy shortage - measures, trends

x: Energy shortage refers to unmet energy requirement and is expressed in MU or percentage terms.
The notes record both the historical 10–15% range and the subsequent decline to 0.03%, followed by zero shortage by November 2025.
Time-of-day tariffs and smart meters help manage demand, while battery energy storage systems and pumped storage help store electricity.

x: India's crude-oil import dependence is approximately
, with one cited estimate placing it at 88.6%.

x: The evening peak occurs from about 6 p.m. to 11 p.m. as cooling demand continues while solar output has declined.
Delhi uses
time-of-day tariffs and smart meters
to manage demand during peak periods.
Poor storage and slow transmission
can strand renewable power in some regions, while heatwaves can place additional stress on grids.

of final energy by 2035.

secs.t: Oil consumption challenges - prices, supply shocks, OPEC+, rupee

x: The Strait of Hormuz lies between
Iran and Oman
and is a major route for international oil and LNG shipments.
The Strait of Hormuz carries approximately
15 million barrels
of crude oil per day, about 34% of world crude trade.
Strategic petroleum reserves, ethanol and electric vehicles are responses used to manage oil dependence and external-balance pressure; increasing imported crude dependence is not such a response.

secs.t: Import dependence - crude, LNG, coal, LPG and sources

x: The provisional July 2026 estimate placed India’s crude oil import dependence at approximately
of consumption.
Russia accounted for about 35%, Iraq about 20%, Saudi Arabia about 15% and the United States about 8% of India’s crude imports in 2025.
Russia was the largest supplier in recent years; Iraq and Saudi Arabia were major suppliers; and West Asia and Africa together accounted for approximately 65% of supplies.

secs.t: Import-substitution fuels - methanol, DME, ethanol, CBG

x: Methanol can be produced from biomass, natural gas, high-ash coal, agricultural residue and carbon dioxide captured from thermal power plants.
Methanol can replace petrol and diesel in transport, and it can also be used in diesel generator sets, boilers and partly in LPG and kerosene applications for cooking.
The CBO is intended to promote compressed biogas and substitute LNG imports.

secs.t: Energy security tools - SPR, exploration, overseas equity, diversification

x: Phase I reserves are underground rock caverns at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur, with a total capacity of 5.33 MMT and about 9.5 days of cover at full capacity.
The IEA norm referred to for strategic oil reserves is
90 days of cover
, compared with about 9.5 days at India’s Phase I full capacity.
HELP provides a unified licence for hydrocarbons; OALP concerns upstream exploration; ONGC Videsh is ONGC’s overseas arm; and overseas acreages help augment supply.

secs.t: Domestic reserves - number game

x: India has 26 sedimentary basins, of which only 7 are producing according to the stated figures.
The current estimate identifies India as the world’s
fifth
-largest holder of coal reserves; an older estimate had placed it fourth.

secs.t: Energy import bill - trade deficit impact

x: India’s crude import bill was approximately
$13.7 billion
in July 2026.
The crude import volume was 21.4 MMT, representing a year-on-year increase of 13.3 per cent.

secs.t: Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 - focus areas

x: Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 was adopted by the Government of India in 2000.
Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 promotes a free market and competition; it does not seek complete prohibition of private participation.

secs.t: Diversification - OVL, LNG terminals, pipelines

x: OVL is the overseas arm of ONGC and acquires equity oil and gas assets in foreign countries.
The 2026 proposal involved refiners and SCI, 59 ships and $1.5–2 billion, while IOC pursued Algeria deals and more US crude for 2027.
HELP is based on a single licence, OALP is linked with the CDI approach, and One Nation One Gas Grid concerns gas-grid development.

secs.t: Demand-side measures - ethanol, EVs, city gas

x: The sequence is EBP pilot in 2001, FAME in 2015, PM E-DRIVE in 2024 and the India Electric Mobility Index in 2025.

The E20 target was advanced to ESY 2025–26 from 2030, and E20 with a minimum 95 RON was mandated from 1 April 2026.

secs.t: AP hydrocarbons - KG basin, Visakhapatnam refinery and SPR

x: The KG Basin is an offshore East Coast zone, is among India’s most prolific hydrocarbon zones, and Andhra Pradesh produces gas and crude oil in the Godavari Basin.
IIPE Visakhapatnam was established in 2016, became an Institution of National Importance in 2017, and signed the stated shale-modelling pact with OIL India in April 2026.

over 20 trillion US dollars

PM-KUSUM promotes
solar pumps and decentralised plants
, whereas PM Surya Ghar focuses on rooftop solar for one crore households.
Andhra Pradesh has introduced virtual net metering with a focus on SC/ST households.

to fix Renewable Purchase Obligations.
Linking fiscal incentives to renewable-energy adoption is intended to promote adoption and encourage more power-purchase agreements.

The policy proposed diversification through
coal, nuclear, hydro, renewables and overseas assets
, along with strategic oil reserves.

A, C, B

October 2014
