rows.title: Biodiversity - levels, values, measurement; India as a megadiverse country
sub: Group-II M2-B-52: Biodiversity - meaning and components: genetic, species and ecosystem diversity
Group-II M2-B-53: Values and significance of biodiversity; India as a megadiverse country

secs.t: Species richness patterns - latitudinal gradient, richest biomes, tropical and Himalayan richness, species-area

x: Exam angle: A/R that butterflies peak in the tropics because they cannot tolerate low temperature: both true, and R explains A.
Tropical rainforests or tropical moist forests are the richest terrestrial ecosystems, while coral reefs are the richest marine ecosystems.
Tropical richness is associated with long evolutionary time without glaciation, stable climate, solar energy and productivity.
The Himalayas bring together different biogeographical zones, creating varied habitats and high species richness.
Both statements are true, and intolerance to low temperatures helps explain why butterfly diversity is highest in the warmer tropics.

secs.t: India's biogeographic zones - count, provinces, largest zone

x: The three biomes identified in the IYB classification are
tropical humid forests, tropical dry deciduous forests, and warm deserts or semi-deserts
The
Deccan Peninsula
is the largest biogeographic zone of India and covers about 42% of the country's land area.
The recorded faunal species counts are Trans-Himalaya—3,324; Himalaya—30,377; Desert—3,346; and Semi-arid—7,424.
The faunal species counts are Western Ghats—17,099; Deccan Peninsula—15,539; Gangetic plains—14,640; and North-East—18,527.
The counts are Coasts—11,883; Islands—11,009; Himalaya—30,377; and Deccan Peninsula—15,539.
The Deccan Peninsula is mainly a rain-shadow deciduous plateau, not a permanently snow-covered alpine zone.

secs.t: Values of biodiversity

x: Consumptive use value
refers to direct use by local people without commercial sale, including fuelwood, fodder and wild food.
Productive use value concerns biodiversity products that are commercially marketed, such as timber, fibre, medicines and genetic material for crops.
All four statements correctly describe ecosystem-service, social or cultural, ethical or existence, and aesthetic values of biodiversity.

secs.t: Biodiversity assessments - new discoveries, BSI and ZSI counts

x: India added
709 animal species and 353 plant taxa
The figures were released in Kolkata by the Botanical Survey of India (BSI) and the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI).
The order was Kerala with 98, West Bengal with 76, Karnataka with 67 and Arunachal Pradesh with 65 new animal species.

secs.t: Biodiversity concept and measures - term, levels, alpha/beta/gamma, indices

x: The word ‘biodiversity’ was coined by Walter G. Rosen, whereas E.O. Wilson popularised it.
Beta diversity measures the change or turnover in species composition between ecosystems or along a habitat gradient.
Alpha diversity is local diversity, gamma diversity is regional diversity, and point richness is the species count at a single point.
The CBD definition covers organisms from terrestrial, marine and other aquatic sources, together with the ecological complexes to which they belong.

secs.t: Megadiverse countries - count, members, India's share

x: India, Brazil, China, Colombia, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ecuador, Indonesia and Madagascar are all among the 17 megadiverse countries.
India ranks 10th among plant-rich countries, 11th for endemic higher vertebrates and 6th among centres of crop origin and diversity.
The criteria included at least 5,000 endemic plant species and borders with marine ecosystems.
India contains portions of
four
global biodiversity hotspots: Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, and Sundaland.

secs.t: Zoogeographic distribution - groups present or absent

x: India lies where the Palearctic realm of the Himalaya and the Indo-Malayan realm meet, giving it species from both realms.
Nicobar fauna is closest to Malesian fauna, particularly that of Southeast Asia.
The Nilgiri tahr is restricted to the Western Ghats, not the Eastern Ghats.
The hoolock gibbon is India's only ape and occurs only in the North-East.

secs.t: Agro-biodiversity - Vavilov centres, crop wild relatives

x: The Hindustan or Indian centre is associated with
rice, sugarcane, mango, pigeon pea, brinjal, cucumber and black pepper
Borjuli wetland protects Oryza rufipogon, the wild ancestor or progenitor of cultivated rice, Oryza sativa.
Oryza rufipogon is noted for pest resistance and tolerance of floods and salinity, making it valuable as a crop wild relative.

secs.t: AP biodiversity - Eastern Ghats and Seshachalam

x: The Eastern Ghats contain deciduous, semi-evergreen and evergreen forests, along with savanna, scrub and estuarine vegetation.
The Board shares 5% of Red Sanders sale profits with farmers, works through People's Biodiversity Registers and is preparing a Marine ABS framework for fishers.

About ₹7 crore was shared with farmers from Red Sanders sale profits in three months. ₹82 lakh was the APSBB sanction, ₹120 crore was the Red Sanders contribution to national ABS receipts, and 13,000 relates to BMC strengthening.

secs.t: Species estimates and the largest taxonomic groups

x: All four estimates are stated figures: about 1.5 million described living species, 300,000 described fossil species, Wilson’s 10–50 million estimate and May’s estimate of about 7 million.
Over 70% of recorded species are animals, plants account for about 22%, and insects are the richest group among animals.
The cited record lists about 135 bat species in India, of which 16 are endemic.

secs.t: Levels - genetic, species, ecosystem diversity

x: Genetic diversity is
variation within a species
and is the basic source of biodiversity.
Differences among varieties of the same species represent
genetic diversity
Species diversity concerns the variety of species in an area and includes both species richness and abundance.
One ecosystem cannot simply replace another; boreal conifers cannot do the job of tropical deciduous trees in every context.

secs.t: Species richness vs evenness; diversity indices

x: Species richness is the number of species present, while species evenness indicates how equally individuals are distributed among them.
Functional diversity measures the range of ecological roles.
Functional richness refers to the niches occupied, functional evenness to the spread of abundance across niches, and functional divergence to the dominance of extreme traits.

secs.t: Rivet popper hypothesis

x: The Rivet Popper Hypothesis was proposed by
Paul Ehrlich
The hypothesis compares an ecosystem to an aeroplane and species to its
rivets
; the loss of a key rivet may cause system failure.
The hypothesis highlights the special importance of key or keystone species.

secs.t: Fauna of India - natural range

x: Exam angle: UPSC 2019 answer: only the Asiatic lion is found naturally in India alone.
The
Asiatic lion
is naturally restricted to India, particularly the Gir region of Gujarat.
The hoolock gibbon is India’s only ape, while slow loris and pangolin are associated particularly with the North-East.

secs.t: Economics of biodiversity - TEEB, Dasgupta Review

x: TEEB, or The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity, seeks to make nature’s values visible and bring them into decision-making at every level.
TEEB is hosted by UNEP and originated from a G8+5 initiative in 2007.
The Review treats nature as an asset and points out that GDP does not adequately account for the depreciation of nature.

secs.t: Bioprospecting and biopiracy; TKDL; ABS

x: TKDL documents traditional formulations in several international languages, thereby helping prevent the grant of erroneous patents based on traditional knowledge.
The appetite-suppressant use of Hoodia was based on knowledge of
the San people of southern Africa
, and a benefit-sharing deal followed.
TKDL documents traditional knowledge so that patent offices can treat it as prior art, helping prevent wrongful patents.
The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 regulates access to bio-resources and traditional knowledge and implements the
Nagoya Protocol

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Mining and fires
threaten micro-endemics such as the Golden Gecko and Cycas beddomei, making the Seshachalam core zones important.
ZSI-only counts and combined ZSI–BSI totals differ; therefore, the institution or combination of institutions behind a figure should be stated.
The APSBB gave the
Best Individual Biodiversity Conservator Award-2026
at the Guntur event.
The landscape has 68 tigers and 11 cubs; gaurs are being reintroduced; and four female tigers are planned for translocation from Chandrapur and Madhya Pradesh.

rows.title: Biodiversity hotspots in India; endemism; Biological Diversity Act 2002 and access-benefit sharing
sub: Group-II M2-B-54: Biodiversity hotspots - criteria; global hotspots and the four in India

secs.t: India's hotspots - names, regions covered, common distractors

x: Exam angle: "which of these is NOT a hotspot in India" - the odd one out is usually a desert or the Eastern Ghats.
The Western Ghats–Sri Lanka hotspot has at least 6,000 vascular plants, with more than 3,000, or about 52%, being endemic.
The Western Ghats alone have about 5,000 vascular plants, around 1,700 endemic species, 58 endemic genera and 308 endemic species among 490 low- and mid-elevation tree species.
The number of hotspots reached 36 in 2016 when the
North American Coastal Plain
was added.

secs.t: Endemic species and their regions - AP Eastern Ghats and Seshachalam, Hangul, Asiatic lion

x: Endemism means that a species occurs naturally in one particular region and nowhere else.
The
Golden Gecko
is a micro-endemic species of the Seshachalam hills.
Podocarpus (Nageia) wallichianus is the only endemic gymnosperm tree of the Western Ghats.
Three new plant species were found in
the rocky Eastern Ghats
in Andhra Pradesh in May 2026.

secs.t: Hotspot criteria - thresholds, originator, designating body

x: Norman Myers
introduced the biodiversity hotspot concept in 1988.
A hotspot must contain at least 1,500 endemic vascular plant species and must have lost at least 70% of its original habitat.
About 86% of the original hotspot habitat has been lost, hotspots contain about 42% of terrestrial vertebrates as endemics, and about 1,50,000 endemic plant species occur there.

secs.t: Biological Diversity Act 2002 - enactment, three-tier bodies, 2023 amendment

x: The National Biodiversity Authority performs the national regulatory role; State Boards and UT Councils regulate commercial use in their respective jurisdictions; and BMCs document biodiversity and prepare PBRs.
The State Government notifies Biodiversity Heritage Sites under Section 37 on the recommendation of the State Biodiversity Board and in consultation with local bodies.

The National Biodiversity Authority handles regulation, advice and approvals involving foreign users and IPR; State Boards regulate commercial use by Indian entities; BMCs undertake local documentation and PBR preparation.

secs.t: BMCs and People's Biodiversity Registers - preparing body, Nagoya link

x: BMCs document biodiversity, prepare PBRs and can levy collection fees for access to bioresources within their area.
About
2.72 lakh
People's Biodiversity Registers had been prepared by June 2026; the earlier figure was about 1.5 lakh in 2024.
BMCs contribute to the objectives of the Nagoya Protocol through local biodiversity governance and access-related collection fees.

secs.t: Biodiversity Heritage Sites - state or UT

x: Biodiversity Heritage Sites are notified by
the State Government in consultation with local bodies
under Section 37.
There were 54 Biodiversity Heritage Sites as of March 2026; earlier counts were 45 in February 2024 and 48 in April 2025.
Nallur Tamarind Grove is in Karnataka, Borjuli wetland in Assam, Kasampatty in Tamil Nadu and Ameenpur Lake in Telangana.

secs.t: Western Ghats protection - Gadgil, Kasturirangan, ESA notification

x: The Gadgil-led WGEEP recommended the whole Western Ghats as an ESA, whereas the Kasturirangan-led High-Level Working Group limited the ESA to about 37%.
The 2010 WGEEP recommendation proposed the whole Ghats as an ESA, covering 142 talukas in 44 districts and divided into three ecological sensitivity zones.
Andhra Pradesh is pursuing a Marine ABS framework, the Western Ghats were rated of significant concern by the IUCN in 2025, and Red Sanders is the leading ABS earner.

secs.t: Access and benefit sharing - benefit-sharing cases (Kani tribe, Arogyapacha)

x: Red Sanders accounts for 45%, amounting to approximately
₹120 crore
, of the more than ₹266 crore raised through NBA's ABS mechanism.
For an identifiable repository, 25–40% of ABS funds goes to it and 60–75% goes to local communities through SBBs or UTBCs.
The 2025 Regulations cover Digital Sequence Information, APSBB plans a fishermen-oriented Marine ABS framework, and ₹82 lakh was sanctioned for Red Sanders conservation.

secs.t: Hotspots vs Key Biodiversity Areas vs Global 200 ecoregions

x: Hotspots use endemic plant and habitat-loss criteria; KBAs are significant individual sites; Global 200 consists of representative priority ecoregions.
Conservation International set the hotspot criteria in 1999, WWF developed the Global 200 framework, and the KBA standard is associated with an IUCN-led partnership.
Global 200 selects representative terrestrial, freshwater and marine priority ecoregions, rather than relying only on endemism and habitat threat.

secs.t: Global hotspots - total count, distribution

x: Norman Myers introduced the concept in 1988, quantitative criteria were set in 1999, Forests of East Australia became the 35th hotspot in 2011, and North American Coastal Plain became the 36th in 2016.
There are 36 recognised global biodiversity hotspots.
The Mediterranean Basin, California Floristic Province and North American Coastal Plain are temperate hotspots.

secs.t: Concept origin - proposer and CI revision

x: Myers introduced the concept in 1988; Conservation International adopted it and set quantitative criteria in 1999, with the work published by Myers et al. in 2000.

secs.t: Endemic species - hotspot

x: Nilgiri tahr is associated with the Western Ghats, not the Himalaya.
Nilgiri marten and Malabar spiny dormouse are associated with the
Agasthyamalai
region of the Western Ghats.
The Nicobar pigeon is associated with Sundaland, specifically the Nicobar Islands.

secs.t: Hottest hotspots and coldspots

x: Hottest hotspots are the eight hotspots combining the highest endemism with the greatest threat.
Coldspots have relatively low diversity but are losing habitat rapidly and remain important for rare species, key ecosystem functions and genetic diversity.

secs.t: Threats specific to each Indian hotspot

x: Monocultures, invasive species, tourism and infrastructure are identified threats to the Western Ghats.
All three statements correctly associate the specified threats with the Himalaya, Indo-Burma and Sundaland/Nicobar hotspots respectively.
Odonates are dragonflies and damselflies; their disappearance in the Western Ghats is treated as an early indication of ecological deterioration.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Gadgil versus Kasturirangan debate concerns the extent and manner of protection to be accorded to the Western Ghats.
The Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve extends across Kerala and Tamil Nadu and was included in UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere (MAB) programme in 2016.
The hotspot approach focuses strongly on plant endemism and can therefore miss threatened systems with low endemism, including grasslands and coldspots.

rows.title: Loss of biodiversity - causes, invasive alien species, IUCN Red List categories
sub: Group-II M2-B-55: Loss of biodiversity - causes, consequences and the role of invasive alien species
Group-II M2-B-61: Endangered species of India - IUCN Red List categories and flagship species

secs.t: IUCN Red List categories - order, abbreviations, definitions, nickname

x: Exam angle: "CR stands for?" - Critically Endangered (not "critically extinct"); asked by APPSC in 2023 and 2025.
Critically Endangered
species face an extremely high risk of extinction in the wild.
The Red List measures extinction risk, whereas the IUCN Green Status measures species recovery; they do not measure exactly the same parameter.
The criteria include declining population, geographic range, small population size, very small population or restricted distribution, and quantitative extinction-risk analysis.
Extinction is declared when there is no reasonable doubt that the last individual has died, following exhaustive surveys in known or expected habitat.

secs.t: Causes of loss - HIPPO, Evil Quartet, most important cause

x: Exam angle: "which is NOT a cause" - pick the odd option (appetite, vegetarianism, protected-area expansion).
The Evil Quartet consists of
habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, invasive alien species and co-extinctions
Habitat destruction is not restricted to terrestrial species; destruction of aquatic habitats also causes biodiversity loss.
Habitat fragmentation particularly affects
migratory animals and wide-ranging mammals and birds
because it disrupts movement and separates populations.
Co-extinction occurs when the extinction of one species leads to the extinction of another dependent species, such as a host, food source or mutualistic partner.
Global warming, habitat fragmentation and invasion by alien species are recognised threats to biodiversity.

secs.t: IUCN and Red Data Book - HQ, publisher, colour pages, specialist groups

x: Black denotes extinct, red endangered, white rare, and green formerly threatened but now out of danger.
The
Invasive Species Specialist Group
(ISSG), functioning under the IUCN Species Survival Commission, maintains the Global Invasive Species Database.
Version 2026-1, released in July 2026, recorded 175,909 species assessed and 49,505 threatened species, approximately 28 percent.
Both statements are true, and the assessment of extinction risk and guidance for funding directly explain why the Red List helps set conservation priorities.
The IUCN was established in 1948, the Red List began in 1964, the World Conservation Congress was held in 2025, and version 2026-1 was released in July 2026.

secs.t: Invasive alien species in India - origin and impact

x: The estimated global and Indian impacts are about one in ten Red List species, 40% of known animal extinctions since the seventeenth century and $127.3 billion of damage in India over sixty years, respectively.
Prosopis juliflora, locally called Seema Chintakaya, lowers groundwater in Rayalaseema and raises soil salinity.
Prosopis juliflora has degraded the
Banni grasslands
and is also associated with groundwater depletion and increased soil salinity in Rayalaseema.
The
Bombay Natural History Society
started the programme at Ujani reservoir against suckermouth catfish, tilapia and African catfish.
The
Plant Quarantine (Regulation of Import into India) Order, 2003
requires pest risk analysis and phytosanitary checks.
The Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine and Storage deals with uncertified imports, which are fumigated with
methyl bromide
The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 empowers the Centre to regulate invasive alien species under
Section 62A
CBD Article 8(h) calls for the prevention of introduction and control or eradication of alien species that threaten ecosystems, habitats or species.
In Raimona National Park, Lantana and Chromolaena are invasive plants but also serve as major nectar sources for butterflies, illustrating the management debate surrounding their removal.
The red-eared slider originated in North America and, having spread through the pet trade, outcompetes native turtles.

secs.t: Indian species - Red List category and habitat

x: The Great Indian Bustard and Gharial are Critically Endangered, while Red Sanders and Sangai deer are Endangered.
The Great Indian Bustard inhabits the Thar grasslands and Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary in Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh.
Jerdon's Courser is a Critically Endangered species of Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary, while the Hangul occurs in Dachigam.
The Hangul is included in the
Species Recovery Programme
list of 22 Critically Endangered species.
The Gharial is associated with the Chambal, has been recommended for species recovery, received suo motu judicial attention, and is a Project Crocodile species.
The Irrawaddy dolphin is associated with Chilika Lake in Odisha and the Godavari estuary in Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: New species discoveries in news - region or state

x: In 2025, India added 709 animal species and 353 plant taxa; 483 of the animal species were new to science.
The survey recorded 143 species, of which 40 were endemic, across 144 sites in five States.
ZSI alone described 117 new species and recorded 128 species as new records in 2025.

secs.t: Species declared extinct in India

x: The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952 and is regarded as the only large mammal to have gone extinct in India since Independence.
The 2014 IUCN Red List recorded 784 extinctions over 500 years.
The Asiatic cheetah, classified as Critically Endangered, survives only in Iran.
Five Australian marsupial species were confirmed extinct in 2026.

secs.t: Global assessments - IPBES, Living Planet Index, sixth mass extinction

x: The sixth extinction is the current human-driven episode, while the end-Cretaceous event about 66 million years ago was the fifth mass extinction and eliminated the dinosaurs.
The present human-driven
sixth extinction
has witnessed extinction rates exceeding 100 times the background rate during the last 300 years.
Co-extinction
occurs when the loss of one species causes the decline or loss of dependent species, such as an obligate pollinator or a parasite dependent on a host.
Large body size, small population, low reproductive rate, narrow or specialised niche and endemism are high-risk traits.

secs.t: Deforestation and habitat fragmentation - drivers, edge effects, disturbing vs restoring activities

x: The Amazon, often called the lungs of the planet, is cleared substantially for
soybean cultivation and cattle pasture
Fragmentation breaks large habitats into small patches and is especially harmful to migratory animals and mammals and birds requiring large territories.
The edge effect exposes habitat boundaries to greater light, wind, heat, predators and weeds.

secs.t: Reports and databases - publisher

x: The Living Planet Report is published by WWF with the Zoological Society of London; the IUCN Red List by IUCN; the Global Invasive Species Database by the IUCN SSC Invasive Species Specialist Group; and the Global Assessment by IPBES.
The Global Invasive Species Database and the list of 100 of the World's Worst IAS are associated with the
IUCN SSC Invasive Species Specialist Group

secs.t: Consequences - pollinators, ecosystem services, zoonotic spillover

x: Biodiversity loss disrupts pollination, nutrient cycling, water and soil services.
Once biodiversity is lost, it cannot be recreated in its original entirety
Zoonotic spillover may increase through habitat disruption and wildlife trade.
The estimated economic cost of invasive alien species to India is
US$127.3 billion
over a period of 60 years.

secs.t: AP biodiversity loss cases

x: Encroachment by fish and prawn tanks and unregulated aquaculture have converted wetland and mangrove areas into ponds, causing salinity and loss of breeding grounds.
Prosopis juliflora drains groundwater, crowds out native flora and shrinks grazing land in Rayalaseema and coastal areas.
Demand from
China and Japan
has driven Red Sanders smuggling, illegal logging and associated violence in the Seshachalam region.

secs.t: Climate change as a driver - coral bleaching, range shifts

x: Climate change causes coral bleaching, ocean acidification, shifts in ecosystem boundaries and disrupted migration.
Rising temperatures can alter ecosystem boundaries and shift species ranges, which in turn can raise extinction risk in biodiversity hotspots.

secs.t: Species in news → IUCN category and habitat state

x: The Peacock or Gooty tarantula is Critically Endangered and occurs in the Nandyal/Gooty region, including the NSTR landscape.
The Slender-billed Vulture is Critically Endangered and is associated mainly with North and North-east India.
The Emperor penguin is classified as Endangered, having moved from Near Threatened, and its habitat is Antarctica.
The cited odonates are classified as Vulnerable and are associated with the Western Ghats.

secs.t: AP threatened and endemic species - status and habitat

x: Red Sanders occurs in the Seshachalam, Veligonda and Nallamala hills; Golden Gecko in Seshachalam micro-habitats; Jerdon’s Courser in Sri Lankamalleswara WLS; and Slender Loris in dry scrub forests.
The species has fewer than 300 mature individuals, a range below 100 square kilometres, a dry deciduous forest habitat at 350–600 metres, and CITES Appendix II listing.

secs.t: IUCN - headquarters, founding, Green Status

x: The IUCN is a union of governments and NGOs, but it is not a UN agency.
The Asiatic lion example shows that a species can be recovered while still not being considered fully restored.
The Phoenix Species Project aims to recover 100 of the world’s most threatened species with funding of $200 million.
The project is associated with
Re:wild and the Bezos Earth Fund

secs.t: Flagship, keystone, umbrella, endemic species

x: A
flagship species
is a charismatic species used to generate public support for conservation; the tiger and Asiatic lion are examples.
Protection of pygmy hog habitat also benefits the Bengal florican, hispid hare, hog deer and rhinoceros.
Red Sanders, the Golden gecko and the Gooty tarantula are identified as endemic species of Andhra Pradesh in the cited context.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: More than 1,500 ships stranded by the Hormuz closure
were identified as a possible pathway for spreading hull-fouling invasive species.
In Amrabad Tiger Reserve in the Nallamala region, Lantana is converted into biochar known as ‘Black Gold’ with the involvement of Joint Forest Management Committees.
Jerdon’s Courser is an Andhra Pradesh species of Eastern Ghats scrub, particularly associated with Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary, not Antarctica.
The cited update is IUCN Red List 2026-1 in July 2026, while three new Critically Endangered plants from the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh were reported in May 2026.

rows.title: Conservation - in-situ (protected areas, biosphere reserves) and ex-situ (zoos, gene banks, seed banks)
sub: Group-II M2-B-56: Conservation of biodiversity - in-situ methods: protected areas, biosphere reserves, sacred groves
Group-II M2-B-57: Conservation of biodiversity - ex-situ methods: zoos, gene banks, botanical gardens, cryopreservation
Group-II M2-B-62: Biosphere reserves of India - list, features and those in Andhra Pradesh

secs.t: Ex-situ facilities - locations, cryopreservation and its medium

x: Exam angle: statement questions on seed vaults (Svalbard and India's Ladakh vault), and "cryopreservation uses which medium".
Exam angle: statement-type questions on Svalbard's country and "largest" claims; APPSC G2 2017 key - Norway.
The International Rice Genebank is at Los Baños, NBRI is at Lucknow, the high-altitude seed vault is at Chang La and the Millennium Seed Bank is at Wakehurst in the United Kingdom.

secs.t: Marine conservation - ICMBAs, Hope Spots, NCMB, marine protected areas

x: Successful coral restoration in the Gulf of Mannar Marine Biosphere Reserve has been associated with
Vaan Island
Hope Spots are ocean sites named by Mission Blue, an initiative associated with marine scientist Sylvia Earle, because of their importance to ocean health.
Under SDG 14, APSES identifies expansion of marine protected areas as a priority, and APSBB plans a Marine Access and Benefit-Sharing framework.

secs.t: Community conservation - sacred groves, Bishnoi tradition, community reserves

x: Sacred groves are forest patches preserved by communities on religious grounds, where trees and wildlife are traditionally venerated.
The 1730 Khejarli incident in Rajasthan involved Amrita Devi Bishnoi and 363 Bishnois protecting khejri trees from the Jodhpur king’s men.
The Citrus Gene Sanctuary in Nokrek Biosphere Reserve, Garo Hills, Meghalaya, conserves
crop wild relatives
in situ.

secs.t: Eco-sensitive zones - definition, declaring authority, court orders

x: An ESZ functions as a shock absorber around a protected area, providing a transition from high protection to areas where regulated development may be permitted.
The 2011 MoEF guidelines allow an ESZ of up to
10 kilometres around a protected area
The Supreme Court held that mining is impermissible within 1 kilometre of every National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary; where a larger ESZ is notified, the larger buffer prevails.

secs.t: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30

x: The WDPA is run by
UNEP-WCMC
, based in Cambridge, in collaboration with IUCN, and tracks progress towards the 30x30 target.
Both are established under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, but human activity is regulated and permitted to an extent in a Wildlife Sanctuary; National Parks have higher protection.
An OECM is outside the formal protected-area network but delivers long-term in-situ conservation outcomes and is recognised on the basis of its results.
The four categories are sanctuary, national park, conservation reserve and community reserve; the latter two were added in 2002, while tiger reserves are notified under the NTCA chapter.

A Conservation Reserve consists of State-owned land near or linking protected areas; a Community Reserve is on voluntarily offered private or community land; National Parks have strict restrictions; and tiger reserves are notified under the NTCA chapter.

secs.t: In-situ vs ex-situ - classify methods

x: Captive breeding is suitable when a species' habitat has been permanently lost; bred animals may subsequently be released, as in the reintroduction of Gangetic gharials in several states.
Since ex-situ conservation removes selected organisms or genetic material from the natural ecological setting, it cannot preserve all ecosystem interactions and processes.

secs.t: Protected landscapes and Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas

x: Keibul Lamjao National Park
in Manipur is the world's only floating National Park, situated on the phumdis of Loktak Lake.
Keibul Lamjao National Park is famous for the
Sangai deer
, which is classified as Endangered.
Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas are designated by
BirdLife International
The
Bombay Natural History Society
(BNHS) is BirdLife International's Indian partner for IBAs.

secs.t: Biosphere reserves - count, MAB programme, zones

x: Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve extends across
Tamil Nadu and Kerala
and is associated with the Kani tribe.
The Seville Strategy added social, cultural and economic needs, together with community participation, to Biosphere Reserve criteria.
The core zone is legally protected and generally excludes human activity, although regulated scientific research may be undertaken.
Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve spans Tamil Nadu and Kerala, was established in 2001, and is home to the Kani tribe.
UNESCO's criteria include a protected core, viable populations across trophic levels and participatory management.
Integrated Management Plans are prepared for
five years
in the specified Biosphere Reserves since financial year 2022–23.

secs.t: AP protected areas - Seshachalam, Papikonda, Coringa, NSTR

x: The three national parks are
Sri Venkateswara, Papikonda and Rajiv Gandhi
APSES lists one tiger reserve, Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam, and one biosphere reserve, Seshachalam.
Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve was notified in 2010 and spans the Tirupati and Kurnool Circles.
The reported area of Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve is 4,755.997 square kilometres.
Red Sanders, Cycas beddomei and the Golden Gecko are associated with Seshachalam.
The cited estimate for Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve was
tigers.
Papikonda National Park protects the Papikondalu ranges situated along the Godavari River.

secs.t: Gene banks - institution and location; field gene banks; global crop gene banks

x: NBPGR runs the National Gene Bank for
plant and crop genetic resources
NBAGR deals with livestock, NBFGR with fish, NBAIM with agriculturally important microorganisms and NBPGR with plants and crops.
Field gene banks maintain living collections, especially of
vegetatively propagated crops and crops with recalcitrant seeds
, such as mango, coconut and banana.

secs.t: Cryopreservation - medium, temperature, materials

x: Cryopreservation is generally carried out in
liquid nitrogen at −196°C
, which halts metabolic activity and preserves viability for very long periods.
Cryopreservation can be applied to gametes, embryos, seeds, pollen, disease-free meristems, tissues and DNA.
Liquid nitrogen at cryogenic temperature halts metabolic activity while allowing the preserved material to remain viable for decades or centuries.

secs.t: Botanical gardens - location

x: The Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden, known for the Great Banyan and associated with the Botanical Survey of India, is at Shibpur in Howrah, West Bengal.
The National Botanical Garden of CSIR-NBRI is at Lucknow, Lloyd Botanical Garden at Darjeeling, Government Botanical Garden at Ooty and Kew at London.

secs.t: Zoos and conservation breeding - Central Zoo Authority, programmes

x: Vultures are associated with the Jatayu Conservation Breeding Centre at Pinjore, the Great Indian Bustard with Sam and Ramdevra in Jaisalmer, and the red panda with Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park.
The 2024 Supreme Court order mandated underground power lines in the Great Indian Bustard’s habitat to reduce threats to the species.

secs.t: LaCONES Hyderabad - frozen zoo

x: LaCONES, the Laboratory for the Conservation of Endangered Species, is associated with CSIR-CCMB at Hyderabad and functions as
India’s frozen zoo using assisted reproduction and DNA banking
India’s first bank for DNA, tissues and embryos of endangered wild animals is located at
Nehru Zoological Park
, Hyderabad.

secs.t: Medicinal plant conservation - NMPB, Phyto-Pharma Plant Mission

x: The NMPB was established in 2000 under the
Ministry of AYUSH
and promotes the cultivation and conservation of medicinal plants.
The Phyto-Pharma Plant Mission is associated with CSIR and focuses on rare or threatened medicinal plants and phytopharmaceutical drug development.
The 2024 Rules encourage cultivated medicinal plants, provide faster NBA/SBB approvals, and mention 90 days generally and 180 days for IPR-related matters.

secs.t: AP zoos - breeding programmes

x: The two ZAAP zoos are noted for animal display, conservation breeding and visitor amenities.

secs.t: UNESCO MAB network (WNBR) - Indian BRs included, year of inclusion

x: Exam angle: "All Indian BRs are in the UNESCO network" - false (13 of 18).
The Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve is located in
Himachal Pradesh
and includes areas such as Pin Valley National Park, Kibber Wildlife Sanctuary and Chandratal.

Nilgiri lies within the Western Ghats World Heritage Site; Nanda Devi is linked with Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks; Sundarbans with Sundarbans National Park; and Manas with Manas Wildlife Sanctuary.
Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve is in Uttarakhand and includes fauna such as snow leopard, musk deer and blue sheep.

secs.t: Zonation - core, buffer, transition

x: The core zone is legally protected, often as a national park or sanctuary under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, and permits conservation and monitoring rather than ordinary human activities.
The buffer zone surrounds the core and supports research, education, training, eco-restoration and limited recreation.
The
transition zone
is the outer interface between people and nature and permits settlements, agriculture, forestry and tourism.

secs.t: BRs spanning more than one state

x: The
Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve
extends across Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka and is India's only three-State Biosphere Reserve.
Nilgiri covers Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka; Agasthyamalai covers Kerala and Tamil Nadu; Achanakmar-Amarkantak covers Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.

secs.t: BR vs national park vs sanctuary

x: Wildlife Sanctuaries are notified by the State under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972; UNESCO does not notify them.
Settlements may exist in the transition zone of a Biosphere Reserve.
A Biosphere Reserve is organised into core, buffer and transition zones.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: OECMs can cover effectively conserved areas outside reserve forests, National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries, including sacred groves, greenbelts and wetlands, and thereby support the 30x30 objective.
Gulf of Mannar is the first marine Biosphere Reserve, Palk Bay is the first dugong reserve and Aravalli Biodiversity Park is the first OECM.
Ex-situ conservation serves as a fallback when habitats are lost or unsuitable, conserving species or their genetic material outside the natural ecosystem.
In-situ conservation protects species along with their ecological setting, while ex-situ conservation focuses mainly on species or genetic material outside the natural habitat.

rows.title: Protected areas of Andhra Pradesh - national parks, sanctuaries, tiger reserve and Ramsar sites
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-77

secs.t: Endemic plants → state and protected area

x: Cycas beddomei is endemic to Andhra Pradesh and the Eastern Ghats and occurs in the Sri Venkateswara-Seshachalam region.
Boswellia ovalifoliolata is endemic to Andhra Pradesh and is associated with the
Seshachalam-Tirumala hills
Red sanders, Pterocarpus santalinus, is described as endemic to Andhra Pradesh only.

secs.t: National parks of AP - district and features

x: Sri Venkateswara National Park is located in
Annamayya and Tirupati
districts.
Rajiv Gandhi National Park
, also known as Rameswaram National Park, covers approximately 2.30 sq km and is the smallest national park in Andhra Pradesh.
Sri Venkateswara National Park is part of the Sri Venkateswara protected landscape in the Seshachalam hills and is associated with Cycas beddomei and red sanders.

secs.t: Kolleru Ramsar site

x: Kolleru is a large freshwater lake situated between the
Godavari and Krishna
deltas.
Kolleru is a freshwater lake, supports pelicans and migratory waterfowl, and its sanctuary area is approximately 308.55 sq km.
Operation Kolleru in 2006 demolished illegal fish tanks inside the sanctuary up to the +5 ft contour.

secs.t: Mangrove and elephant habitats

x: Coringa is associated with the mangroves of the Godavari estuary, whereas Krishna Wildlife Sanctuary protects mangroves of the Krishna estuary.
Avicennia and Rhizophora
are the mangrove genera specifically associated with the Andhra Pradesh coastal habitats.
The Andhra Pradesh Socio-Economic Survey 2025–26 describes AP’s mangroves as India’s
second-largest mangrove system
Kaundinya Wildlife Sanctuary
and the Rayala Elephant Reserve are counted as one elephant reserve.

secs.t: Eco-sensitive zones around AP PAs

x: The 2002–16 Wildlife Action Plan suggested a 10 km zone around protected areas.
There are 353 final eco-sensitive zone notifications covering 496 out of 688 protected areas nationally.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A monsoon ban on safari vehicles
in the Nagarjuna-Srisailam Tiger Reserve was reported in June 2026.
The survey in the Nagarjuna-Srisailam Tiger Reserve on 1 May 2026 concerned
the peacock tarantula
Hope Island near Coringa was reported to face a threat from a satellite launch facility.

rows.title: Species-specific conservation projects - Project Tiger, Project Elephant, Gangetic dolphin, Great Indian Bustard, vulture, cheetah reintroduction
sub: Group-II M2-B-63: Indian wildlife conservation efforts - Project Tiger, Project Elephant and species recovery programmes
Group-II M2-B-64: Recent wildlife initiatives - cheetah reintroduction, dolphin and vulture conservation, marine conservation

secs.t: Great Indian Bustard - range, zoological name, Supreme Court case, breeding

x: The Great Indian Bustard is found mainly in
the Thar region of Rajasthan
, although its range also extends into parts of Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka.
Collisions with overhead power lines are a major threat to the Great Indian Bustard, particularly in solar and wind-energy zones.

Both statements are true, but the location of the breeding programme in Jaisalmer is a separate conservation-administration decision and is not logically explained solely by the species’ main geographical range.
The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance to protect
gharial
s in the National Chambal Sanctuary.

secs.t: Gangetic dolphin - national aquatic animal, Project Dolphin, threats

x: 5 October
is observed as National Dolphin Day, corresponding to the date on which the Ganges River Dolphin was declared India’s National Aquatic Animal.
The Ganges River Dolphin is found in the Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna and Karnaphuli-Sangu systems across India, Nepal and Bangladesh.
Pollution, entanglement or bycatch in fishing nets, dams and barrages, poaching, killing for oil and boat traffic are recognised threats.
In January 2026, the Wildlife Institute of India at Dehradun, in the Namami Gange context, introduced the Dolphin Rescue Ambulance and the Aqua Life Conservation Monitoring Centre.

secs.t: Project Cheetah and International Big Cat Alliance

x: Eight African cheetahs were brought from
Namibia
to Kuno National Park on 17 September 2022.
Project Cheetah brought African cheetahs to Kuno National Park and seeks to restore open forest and grassland ecosystems.
The Supreme Court first ruled on cheetah reintroduction in 2012 and set out the reintroduction programme.
Kuno was initially chosen as a second home for Gir's Asiatic lions.
Eight cheetahs came from Namibia in September 2022, twelve from South Africa in February 2023, and two females were released from Botswana in May 2026.
The International Big Cat Alliance was launched in April 2023 to mark
50 years of Project Tiger
The seven big cats are tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma.
The IBCA was opened to 96 range and non-range countries, and 37 countries including India had consented to join.
Saudi Arabia joined as the 26th member and Bangladesh as the 27th member of the IBCA.

secs.t: Other projects - launch years

x: The correct order is Project Tiger (1973), Crocodile Project (1975), Indian Rhino Vision 2020 (2005), and Project Snow Leopard (2009).
The Coast Guard's Operation Olivia has been conducted annually since
the early 1980s
for Olive Ridley protection.
The Baula project is at Dangamal in Bhitarkanika, the Mugger project is associated with Ramatirtha in 1984, and Project Crocodile received FAO and UNDP support.
The five additions were dolphin, Asian elephant, gharial, Great Indian Bustard and Olive Ridley turtle.

secs.t: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP

x: Corbett
was the first tiger reserve under Project Tiger, formally included on 1 April 1973.
Project Tiger was launched on the advice of Indira Gandhi’s task force, had WWF support, and included Palamau among its first nine reserves.
Section 38V(3) requires each State to prepare a
Tiger Conservation Plan for every tiger reserve
The All India Tiger Estimation is conducted every four years and uses both camera traps and the M-STrIPES monitoring system.
The Global Tiger Forum has its headquarters at New Delhi; IBCA and CA|TS are other global efforts, while ITHCP is led by IUCN.
NSTR is described as India’s largest tiger reserve by core area and lies in the Nallamala hills.
NSTR has an approximate core area of 5,443 square kilometres in the Nallamala hills.

secs.t: Migratory species - CMS COP13 listings, Amur falcon

x: The Amur falcon breeds in Southeast Russia and northern China and migrates to southern Africa.
The Amur falcon stops in huge numbers at
Doyang reservoir near Pangti
in Nagaland, known as the ‘Falcon Capital of the World’.
The Amur falcon undertakes a very long raptor migration, crosses the Arabian Sea non-stop and is strongly associated with Pangti.

secs.t: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres

x: Vultures declined sharply after feeding on cattle carcasses containing veterinary
diclofenac
Diclofenac causes kidney failure in vultures, resulting in visceral gout.
Meloxicam
is identified as a safe alternative to diclofenac in the context of vulture conservation.
SAVE
, meaning Saving Asia’s Vultures from Extinction, is the partner consortium associated with these efforts.
Vulture Safe Zones are conservation landscapes intended to protect vultures from threats such as toxic veterinary drugs and related mortality.

secs.t: Project Elephant - launch, reserves, MIKE, biology, AP corridor

x: Project Elephant covers wild elephants, their habitats and corridors, mitigation of conflict, and the welfare of captive elephants.
India has 33 Elephant Reserves in 14 States, and these areas can overlap tiger reserves, sanctuaries and reserved forests.
MIKE stands for
Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants
and is a CITES programme.
Elephant gestation lasts about
22 months
, the longest gestation period among mammals.
The Brahmagiri-Nilgiri-Eastern Ghats Elephant Reserve holds one of the world’s largest Asian elephant populations.
India has about 60% of the world’s Asian elephants; conflict causes over 500 human deaths annually; and 29,964 is the older 2017 count for elephants in 33 reserves.

secs.t: Species recovery programmes - species, funding, duration

x: The programme includes species such as the
snow leopard
, Asiatic lion, Great Indian Bustard, Gangetic dolphin, dugong, vultures, Hangul and marine turtles.
The Species Recovery Programme covers 22 critically endangered species.
Gharial
and sloth bear were recommended for inclusion.
CAMPA funds may be used for wildlife management and addressing human-wildlife conflict.

secs.t: Conservation organisations → logo and headquarters

x: IUCN and WWF are headquartered at Gland, Switzerland; BNHS at Mumbai; and WTI at Noida, Uttar Pradesh.
The Great hornbill is the logo of the
Bombay Natural History Society
(BNHS).
WTI was established in 1998, not 1982.
The Wildlife Institute of India (WII) is headquartered at
Dehradun

secs.t: Tiger estimation - methods, cycle, numbers, M-STrIPES

x: NTCA is statutory under the Wildlife Protection Act, with the 2006 amendment providing its present statutory framework, and it implements Project Tiger under MoEFCC.
The old pugmark technique was replaced by camera trapping and ExtractCompare software, which identifies tigers through stripe patterns.
The 2006 figure of 1,411 precedes the 2022 estimate of 3,682; the upper limit of 3,925 and the reported 6.1% growth rate belong to the fifth-cycle reference.

secs.t: Tiger reserves - total, largest, newest, CA|TS

x: India has 58 tiger reserves in 18 States, covering about 84,488 sq km, or approximately 2.6% of the country’s area.
Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve
in Andhra Pradesh is the largest, covering about 5,443 sq km.
By 2022, 51 reserves had been evaluated; 12 were rated Excellent, with an average score of 78%.
CA|TS stands for
Conservation Assured Tiger Standards

secs.t: Marine conservation - Hope Spots, NCMB, dugong reserve, Olive Ridley in AP

x: Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are the Indian locations identified as IUCN and Mission Blue Hope Spots.
Rushikulya in Ganjam, Odisha, and beaches in Srikakulam and Vizianagaram in Andhra Pradesh are associated with
Olive Ridley mass nesting
, known as arribada.
MISHTI is a
mangrove restoration
initiative launched in 2023, covering approximately 22,561 hectares in 13 States and Union Territories.

secs.t: Project Lion and other translocations

x: Project Lion was launched in 2020 to conserve the world's last free-ranging Asiatic lions in Gir through surveillance, research and disease management.
Project Lion includes modern surveillance, research and disease management for Asiatic lions; construction of a coastal marine reserve is unrelated to it.
Critics argue that Barda Wildlife Sanctuary is too close to Gir to function as an effective separate metapopulation safeguard.

secs.t: Coastal and marine protected areas - species focus

x: Gulf of Mannar is associated with coral reefs, islands and dugong; Malvan with corals and marine life; Coringa with mangroves and the Godavari estuary; and Bhitarkanika with saltwater crocodiles and mangroves.
Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary is located near
Kakinada
in Andhra Pradesh and is noted for mangroves and the Godavari estuary.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh launched Project HANUMAN on 3 March 2026, World Wildlife Day, to
reduce human-wildlife conflict

sub: Group-II M2-B-65: Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 and its recent amendment; Biological Diversity Act 2002 and amendment

secs.t: Forest and wildlife Acts - enactment chronology

x: Exam angle: direct year questions (1865, 1927, 1972, 1980).
The 2023 amendment renamed it the
Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980
The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 contained 66 sections in 7 chapters and was subsequently amended in 1991, 2002, 2006 and 2022.
The statutory definition includes amphibians, birds, mammals, reptiles and their young, along with the eggs of birds and reptiles.

secs.t: WPA 1972 schedules - before and after the 2022 amendment, vermin

x: Under Section 62, the Central Government may declare a wild animal not in Schedule I as vermin for a specified area and period by notification.
Schedule I species receive the highest protection; hunting and trade are prohibited except in special cases permitted by the Act.
The mugger crocodile, rock eagle-owl and blackbuck are in Schedule I. The common crow was included in the former vermin Schedule V, not Schedule I.
A specified plant cannot be
picked, uprooted or traded without permission

secs.t: Indian Forest Act 1927 - forest categories, offence sections, 2017 amendment

x: Reserved forest
s receive the most stringent protection; felling, grazing and hunting are barred unless expressly permitted, and the State controls management.
Bamboo grown on private or non-forest land could thereafter be felled and transported without a permit.
The Act has been criticised for harming forest-dwellers’ livelihoods, contributing to reform efforts focused on community rights.

secs.t: National Forest Policy 1952 and 1988 - objectives and forest-cover target

x: Exam angle: the statement "at least two-thirds of the country's land should be under forest" is
NOT true
. Two-thirds applies only to the hills.
The 1952 policy aimed at one-third of the total land under forest, with 60% forest cover in hills and 25% in plains.
The policy supports ecological stability, conservation, afforestation, social forestry and local needs.
The policy supports protected-area corridors, fuel-efficient chulhas, afforestation and social forestry.

secs.t: Acts protecting wild animals, birds and plants - WPA vs EPA vs FCA, AWBI

x: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is an umbrella law for
environmental protection and pollution control
All three pairs are correctly matched.
The NGT hears cases under seven specified laws, including the FCA 1980, EPA 1986 and BD Act 2002.
There is no Act called the
Nature (Protection) Act, 2000

secs.t: Wildlife Crime Control Bureau - HQ, regional offices, operations

x: The Bureau was constituted in 2007 under the
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
The five regional offices are at
Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, Chennai and Jabalpur
Save Kurma concerns turtles, Softgold concerns shahtoosh, Clean Art targets mongoose-hair brushes, and Thunderbird is INTERPOL-led.
Operation Birbil deals with wildlife crime involving
wild cats and birds

secs.t: Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 - diversion approval, 2023 amendment, AP data

x: The amendment provides an exemption from central approval for strategic projects within
100 km
of international borders, among other specified exemptions.

The Forest Conservation Rules, 2022, which dropped the consent clause, led to a dispute between the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
Equal-area non-forest land is preferred; otherwise twice the degraded forest area is used, along with payment of NPV.
The 2025 rules treat
assisted natural regeneration and plantation
on leased forest land as forestry activities.

secs.t: WPA amendments 2002 and 2006 - bodies and categories added

x: Conservation Reserves are government-owned buffers or corridors.
The 2002 amendment replaced the Indian Board for Wildlife with the
National Board for Wildlife
The 2022 amendment rationalised the schedules and added invasive alien species.

x: Mining is barred within
1 kilometre
of every national park and sanctuary boundary unless a larger eco-sensitive zone is notified.

Article 48A directs the State to protect and improve the environment; Article 51A(g) imposes the relevant fundamental duty on citizens; and Article 21 includes the right to a clean and healthy environment.

secs.t: Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 - year, subject-matter, ownership, hunting

x: Section 39 declares wild animals, trophies and articles derived from them to be
Government property
Section 9 prohibits hunting of scheduled animals, subject to exceptions provided by the Act.
Section 11
provides exceptions to the prohibition on hunting, including situations involving danger to human life or crops.
Section 12 permits specified activities including education, research, scientific management and translocation.

secs.t: Authorities under wildlife and biodiversity laws

x: The State Board for Wildlife is chaired by the Chief Minister of the concerned State.
The relevant years are Animal Welfare Board—1962, National Biodiversity Authority—2003, National Tiger Conservation Authority—2006, and Wildlife Crime Control Bureau—2007.

secs.t: Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act 2022 - key changes

x: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 came into force in
April 2023
The 2022 amendment incorporated
CITES
-related provisions, including provisions concerning management and scientific authorities.
African catfish
is an example of an invasive alien species referred to in connection with the amendment.
The minimum fine for offences involving specially protected animals was raised from Rs 10,000 to

x: Foreign nationals and foreign-incorporated entities
continue to require prior NBA approval.
The NBA passes approximately
85–90 percent
of ABS proceeds to State Biodiversity Boards under the 2024 Rules.
The April 2025 ABS Regulations provide
25–40 percent
for identifiable source institutions and 60–75 percent for local communities through SBBs or UTBCs.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All three statements correctly describe the reported current issue: the Delhi High Court PIL, the clearance rate of over 97%, and the 2025 full-Board meeting after a 13-year gap.
The criticism is that the 2023 amendment takes deemed forests out of the Act’s scope, potentially diluting the Godavarman protection and clashing with the Forest Rights Act.

secs.t: Agroforestry - National Agroforestry Policy 2014, GROW report, CAFRI, Trees Outside Forests

x: Agroforestry diversifies farm income, conserves soil, improves fertility, stores carbon and enhances climate resilience, but it cannot permanently eliminate all climate risks.
The GROW report by NITI Aayog uses the expansion ‘Greening and Restoration of Wasteland with Agroforestry’ and places the agroforestry area at about 8.65% of India’s geographical area.

secs.t: Afforestation schemes - Nagar Van Yojana, NAEB, state schemes

x: The relevant years are 2014 for the National Agroforestry Policy, 2020–21 for the Nagar Van Yojana target period, 2023 for TOFI and 2024 for Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam.
The Green India Mission is one of the NAPCC missions, is implemented through JFMCs and receives partial funding from National CAMPA.

x: Exam angle: CAMPA exists at
both national and state levels
, which is correct. "People's participation is mandatory" under the 2016 Act is
wrong
The agency must pay for compensatory afforestation as well as the NPV of the lost forest ecosystem before the project begins.
CAMPA funds may support regeneration, wildlife management, catchment treatment, relocation from protected areas, human-wildlife conflict management and forest-fire prevention.

secs.t: Afforestation techniques - Miyawaki method, social forestry

x: The Miyawaki method creates dense, multi-layered mini-forests using native species, particularly in urban areas.
The method is named after
Akira Miyawaki
, a Japanese botanist.
Farm forestry, community forestry, extension forestry and agroforestry are components of social forestry.
The suggested correction is to shift from commercial monocultures to plantations containing mixed native species.

secs.t: Compensatory afforestation rules - land banks, Green Credit link

x: Central PSUs, and projects where no non-forest land is available, may use
twice the area of degraded forest land
for compensatory afforestation.
Accredited Compensatory Afforestation permits developers to use plantations raised in advance, effectively creating land banks for meeting obligations.
The 2022 Rules dropped the clause requiring the consent of forest-dwellers before diversion, and the NCST disputed this with the MoEFCC.

secs.t: Joint Forest Management - origin, 1990 guidelines, JFMCs, AP VSS

x: The Ministry of Environment and Forests issued the Joint Forest Management guidelines on
1 June 1990
The National Afforestation Programme runs through village-level
Joint Forest Management Committees
In Andhra Pradesh, the State Forest Development Agency federates 22 Forest Development Agencies and runs the NAP, GIM and NMPB schemes.
The State Forest Development Agency conducts capacity-building camps through
Vana Samrakshana Samithis

land rights and rehabilitation
concerns.

convergence with CAMPA and MGNREGS, now VB-G RAM G
, never happened.
Suggested reforms include limiting CAMPA to historical forest zones and granting Forest Rights Act community titles to pastoralists.
The scheme covers 5,300.97 sq km across Seshachalam, Veligonda, Lankamala, Nallamala and Talakona, with ₹1,729.83 lakh allotted for 2025–26.

rows.title: Climate change - greenhouse effect, greenhouse gases, radiative forcing, evidence and observed impacts
sub: Group-II M2-B-88: Global warming - greenhouse effect, greenhouse gases, radiative forcing and evidence

secs.t: Greenhouse gases - contribution order, distractors, GWP, lifetime, largest contributor

x: Exam angle: "Deforestation is decreasing the amount of CO2" is the
incorrect
statement, because deforestation raises CO2.
CO₂ reached about 423.9 ppm in 2024, described as the highest concentration in approximately two million years; the pre-industrial level was around 280 ppm.

CO2 is associated with fossil fuels, deforestation and cement production; methane with rice paddies, livestock and landfills; N2O with fertilisers and biomass or coal burning; and SF6 with dielectric fluid.
SF6 has an exceptionally high GWP, CFCs/HFCs have a very high range, and water vapour is short-lived with variable GWP.
Sulphur hexafluoride
has a 100-year GWP of approximately 23,900, much higher than CO2, methane or nitrous oxide.
Deforestation does not decrease atmospheric CO2; it reduces carbon uptake and may release stored carbon, thereby raising atmospheric CO2.
Water vapour is the largest natural contributor to the greenhouse effect, while carbon dioxide is the main anthropogenic driver.

secs.t: Greenhouse effect - mechanism, natural vs enhanced, Earth without it

x: The atmosphere allows much incoming short-wave solar radiation to reach Earth’s surface but absorbs outgoing long-wave terrestrial infrared radiation through greenhouse gases.
CO2 and water vapour strongly absorb infrared radiation in the 14,000–25,000 nm range and re-radiate energy in all directions, including back towards the surface.
Human-driven increases in greenhouse gases strengthen the greenhouse effect by absorbing more outgoing infrared radiation, contributing to global warming and climate change.
The natural greenhouse effect raises Earth’s average surface temperature from approximately −18°C to about +15°C, making the planet habitable.

secs.t: Emission sources - sectors, farm sources of CH4 and N2O, top emitters

x: Deforestation and land-use change generally remove or reduce carbon sinks rather than increase them in all circumstances.
Black and brown carbon have a warming effect on the air, whereas sulphate droplets exert a cooling effect.
Deforestation destroys carbon sinks, while burning or rotting trees releases stored carbon.
Synthetic fertilisers release nitrous oxide, while livestock digestion through enteric fermentation and rice paddies are important methane sources.

secs.t: Observed impacts - temperature, ice, sea level, acidification, extremes

x: Both major ice sheets are losing mass, and Arctic sea ice declined by about 3.5–4.1% per decade during 1979–2012.
Greenhouse gases and the ozone hole strengthened the westerlies, which lifted warm Circumpolar Deep Water and initiated a feedback loop that prevents new ice formation.
When oceans absorb carbon dioxide, carbonic acid forms, lowering ocean pH and causing acidification.

secs.t: Radiative forcing, climate sensitivity, feedbacks, tipping points, methane hydrates

x: All three statements describe positive climate feedbacks: reduced ice albedo increases absorption, while additional atmospheric water vapour enhances heat trapping.
Tipping points are thresholds at which small changes can initiate self-perpetuating, non-linear shifts that are not reversible on human timescales.
Warming can destabilise methane hydrates and release methane, a potent greenhouse gas, thereby producing a positive feedback.
Long-lived greenhouse-gas forcing rose by about 54% from 1990 to 2024, with CO2 contributing about 81% of the rise; radiative forcing denotes an energy-balance change.

secs.t: Short-lived climate pollutants - black carbon, methane, tropospheric ozone, Global Methane Pledge

x: The Climate and Clean Air Coalition works to address
short-lived climate pollutants
such as black carbon, methane, HFCs and tropospheric ozone.
Black carbon darkens snow, reduces its albedo and increases the absorption of solar energy, thereby accelerating glacier melt.
Tropospheric ozone is formed through reactions involving nitrogen oxides (NOx) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in sunlight.
Methane has an atmospheric lifetime of approximately 12 years, longer than black carbon but shorter than many long-lived greenhouse gases.
Tropospheric ozone is a short-lived greenhouse gas, harms vegetation and cuts crop yields; its pollution is generally most severe in summer.

secs.t: Measurement and indicators - Keeling curve, CO2 ppm, WMO GHG Bulletin

x: The Keeling curve is the continuous atmospheric CO2 record from Mauna Loa, Hawaii, begun in 1958 by Charles David Keeling.
Ice cores
preserve trapped air bubbles that provide evidence of past atmospheric CO2 concentrations and temperatures.
The WMO Greenhouse Gas Bulletin 2025 reported a CO2 concentration of
The WMO figures for 2024 report CO2 at 152 percent, methane at 266 percent and nitrous oxide at 125 percent of pre-industrial levels.

secs.t: Warming thresholds - 1.5°C and 2°C, carbon budget

x: The UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 projected approximately
of warming even with updated NDCs.
Each carbon bomb can emit over 1 Gt CO2; LINGO identified 425, and their combined emissions would consume the 1.5°C carbon budget twice over.
The Agreement seeks to hold warming well below 2°C and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

secs.t: GHG vs non-GHG identification - largest contributor

x: Nitrogen
is a non-greenhouse gas and constitutes about 78.08 percent of the atmosphere.
The approximate atmospheric proportions are nitrogen 78.08 percent, oxygen 20.95 percent and argon 0.93 percent.
A concentration of 423.9 ppm is approximately
0.04 percent
of the atmosphere.
Deforestation increases atmospheric CO2 because it destroys forests that act as carbon sinks and may also release stored carbon.

secs.t: Carbon accounting and removal terms - footprint, sequestration, CCS, DAC

x: A carbon footprint measures total greenhouse gas emissions associated with a person, organisation or product, commonly expressed in tonnes of CO2 per year.
CCUS captures CO2 from point sources such as factory flue gases for use or underground storage.
Footprint concerns emissions, sequestration concerns storage, DAC removes CO2 from ambient air, and a carbon bomb is a very large fossil-fuel project.

secs.t: Global warming effects matching

x: Global warming is associated with rising sea levels.
Climate change is associated with glacier melt, ocean acidification, extreme weather, coral bleaching, species loss and health risks.
Oil spillage can cause oxygen depletion in water bodies

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The 2009 EPA endangerment finding permitted regulation of vehicle greenhouse gases, followed the significance of Massachusetts v. EPA (2007), and was repealed in 2026.
Agriculture is left out because farm emissions are diffuse, making them unsuitable for treatment as a concentrated source in the CCUS road map.
Agricultural measures such as soil carbon enhancement, biochar and agroforestry fit under
carbon dioxide removal
‘Overshoot, peak and decline’ describes the trajectory in which warming or emissions exceed a level, reach a maximum, and then decrease.

sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-81

secs.t: Ocean acidification - cause, carbonate chemistry, pH change

x: Ocean acidification is called the ‘evil twin of global warming’ or ‘the other CO2 problem’ because anthropogenic carbon dioxide produces a distinct chemical threat to marine systems.
The oceans absorb
about one-third
of anthropogenic carbon dioxide; the estimate is also expressed as roughly 30–40%.
When eutrophic blooms collapse and decay, decomposition can increase carbon dioxide in the water, thereby worsening acidification.

secs.t: Effects on calcifying organisms

x: Pteropod
s are commonly called sea butterflies.
All four pairs correctly describe effects associated with ocean acidification on the respective calcifying organisms.
Effects on calcifying organisms can disrupt marine food webs, which may reduce fish stocks and affect livelihoods dependent on fisheries.

secs.t: Coral restoration methods

x: Biorock uses low-voltage electrical current on steel frames, causing limestone or mineral accretion on which coral fragments can grow faster.
Three-dimensional printed artificial reef modules were developed off Ramanathapuram under
PMMSY
, near the Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve.
Three-dimensional printed artificial reef modules were reported off Ramanathapuram under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (
PMMSY

secs.t: Ocean deoxygenation and marine heatwaves

x: Nutrient runoff promotes algal blooms; when the biomass decays, decomposition consumes oxygen and can create hypoxic dead zones.
Decay of algal blooms consumes dissolved oxygen, causing deoxygenation, and adds carbon dioxide, which worsens acidification.
Dead zones are hypoxic waters in which dissolved oxygen is too low to support normal aquatic life.

secs.t: Monitoring and targets - SDG 14.3, observing, Deep Ocean Mission

x: SDG 14.3 uses
average marine pH at representative stations
as its indicator.
Samudrayaan includes the three-member Matsya 6000 submersible, and the mission has surveyed about 25 seamounts and identified about 39 potentially new species.
The National Centre for Coastal Research (NCCR), Chennai, monitors coral reef health through the D-COIN platform.

x: SDG 14 is not ranked by NITI Aayog, while Andhra Pradesh has plans concerning expanded Marine Protected Areas and sustainable fishing.
Lakshadweep is entirely characterised by atoll reefs.

rows.title: Impacts of climate change on India - monsoon, agriculture, Himalayan glaciers, sea-level rise, extreme events
sub: Group-II M2-B-89: Climate change - observed and projected impacts globally and on India
Group-II M2-B-90: Climate change and Indian agriculture, water resources, coasts and the Himalaya

secs.t: Temperature trends - IMD climate statement, warmest years, states worst hit

x: IMD declares a heat wave when the actual maximum temperature is at least 45°C, regardless of the normal maximum temperature.
Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur
are the Andhra Pradesh districts identified as experiencing increasingly frequent and intense heat waves.
Meandering Rossby waves and the loo over the Gangetic plains are identified causes.

secs.t: Agriculture - rice and wheat yields, NICRA, Climate-Smart Villages, resilient varieties

x: El Niño tends to weaken the south-west monsoon and reduce rice and sugarcane yields, whereas La Niña usually enhances monsoon rainfall.
The FAO–WMO report indicates that extreme heat can reduce dairy milk yield by about
15–25 percent
The El Niño-linked fodder crisis was reported in
Chittoor
, highlighting the need for fodder banks and silage.
ACASA-India, the Atlas of Climate Adaptation in Indian Agriculture, uses GIS-based mapping to assess crop vulnerability.

secs.t: Heat stress and health - wet-bulb limit, Heat Action Plans, vector-borne diseases

x: At a wet-bulb temperature above about 35°C, sweat can no longer cool the body sufficiently, making human survival highly difficult.
Kerala and Tamil Nadu could experience wet-bulb temperatures of about
under the cited projection.
The report found that nearly
40 percent
of districts face high risk from extreme weather.

secs.t: Monsoon changes - variability, extreme rainfall, IMD and MoES observations

x: The
Brahmaputra, Ganga and Krishna
basins have experienced surging flash floods in the stated assessment.
Andhra Pradesh receives about 966 mm of annual rainfall, with roughly two-thirds from the south-west monsoon and one-third from the north-east monsoon.
Both statements are true, and the greater moisture-holding capacity of warmer air helps explain the intensification of extreme rainfall and associated flash floods.

secs.t: Himalayan glaciers - retreat, GLOFs, Sikkim and Uttarakhand, ICIMOD

x: As valley glaciers thin, their tributary glaciers may remain stranded on steep slopes; these are termed hanging glaciers.
The concern arose from the chain in which melting permafrost destabilises hanging glaciers, causing ice-rock avalanches and LLOFs or GLOFs.
The South Lhonak GLOF occurred in October 2023, global glacier mass loss exceeded 9,500 Gt since 1975, and Central Himalayan glacier area declined by more than 20 per cent in three decades.

secs.t: Sea-level rise - INCOIS mapping, erosion hotspots, Uppada

x: Sea-level rise results mainly from thermal expansion of seawater and the addition of water from melting glaciers and ice sheets.
The IPCC SROCC, published in September 2019, stated that the oceans had absorbed over
of the excess heat.
Cyclones can wreck paddy and aquaculture in deltas while supplying water beneficial to rabi crops and tanks.

secs.t: Extreme events - cyclone intensification, urban floods, social tensions

x: Exam angle: "Climate change is increasing social tension in India" (A) with "extreme events threaten food security" (R):
both are true, and R explains A

All four figures and assessments are correctly stated: NICRA assessed 651 districts, 310 were highly or very highly vulnerable, CEEW identified over 75% as hotspots, and NDMA estimated about 68% drought-prone area.

secs.t: Assessment of Climate Change over the Indian Region - publisher, findings

x: The assessment covers
temperature, rainfall and monsoon, droughts, sea level, tropical cyclones and the Himalayan cryosphere
India's first national climate assessment was published in 2020 by the
Ministry of Earth Sciences

secs.t: Climate Risk Index - publisher, India's rank

x: Germanwatch, a German NGO based in Bonn, publishes the Climate Risk Index, which is usually released at the COP.
India was ranked the ninth most climate-affected country, with
430 extreme events, losses of 170 billion US dollars and 1.3 billion people affected

secs.t: Observed global impacts - temperature, ice loss, dead glaciers, sea-level rise, extremes, coral bleaching

x: Oceans hold over 90% of excess heat, 2025 saw marine heatwaves over about 90% of the ocean surface, and ocean heat records continued for nine straight years.
Greenhouse gases and the ozone hole strengthened westerly winds, which lifted warm Circumpolar Deep Water and contributed to Antarctic sea-ice collapse.
The 1.2°C threshold has been crossed, recovery may take over 15 years, and warm-water coral reefs are considered highly fragile.

secs.t: Global climate reports in news - WMO, IMD, Copernicus

x: The report gives a 91% chance of at least one year exceeding 1.5°C and indicates that 2027 may set a record; El Niño is expected late in 2026.
The IPCC was set up in 1988 by WMO and UNEP, assesses existing scientific literature rather than conducting its own research, and shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize.

secs.t: Climate tipping points - meaning, elements, most fragile ecosystems

x: A tipping point is a threshold beyond which small changes may produce large, self-perpetuating and irreversible shifts in a non-linear system.
Beyond approximately
2°C of warming
, parts of the Amazon may shift from rainforest to savanna and turn from a carbon store into a carbon source.
Warm-water coral reefs
are identified as the most fragile tipping element, with their critical threshold already crossed.

secs.t: Biodiversity impacts - ocean vs land species loss, range shifts

x: The Rutgers study found that warming could eliminate about twice as many ocean species from their habitats as land species.
The assessment reported that 40% of amphibians, 33% of reef corals and more than one-third of marine mammals were threatened.
Species are shifting
poleward and upslope
as they track cooler climatic conditions.
Antarctic sea-ice loss disrupts krill populations and contributes to Emperor penguin breeding failure.

secs.t: Impacts on India - heatwaves, wet-bulb temperature, monsoon, extreme rain, east-coast cyclones

x: Under the stated IMD criterion, an actual maximum temperature of
or more constitutes a heatwave irrespective of the normal temperature.
Wet-bulb temperature is the lowest temperature that air can reach by evaporative cooling and combines the effects of heat and humidity.
When relative humidity is 100%, no further evaporative cooling is possible, so wet-bulb and dry-bulb temperatures become equal.

secs.t: Projected impacts - 1.5 C vs 2 C

x: The temperature objective of the Paris Agreement is to keep warming
well below 2°C and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C
Wheat and maize yields are projected to fall by about
for every 1°C rise in temperature.
Sea-level rise by 2100 under the 1.5°C scenario is projected to be approximately 10 cm lower than under the 2°C scenario.

secs.t: Climate migration and small island states - displacement, territory loss

x: Kiribati and Tuvalu
are identified as Pacific island states at risk from climate-related displacement and territory loss.
The Falepili Union treaty provides Tuvaluans with a pathway for climate-related mobility.
The cited World Bank estimate is
45 million
Indians pushed into extreme poverty within 15 years.

secs.t: Heat stress and climate vulnerability - states, DST report, AP districts

x: The AP SAPCC assessment identifies the northern and central regions as very highly vulnerable, the southern coast as moderately vulnerable, and the south-western areas as relatively low vulnerable.
India was ranked the ninth worst-hit country in the Germanwatch Climate Risk Index 2025 for the period 1995–2024.
NICRA assessed 651 agricultural districts, of which 310 were highly or very highly vulnerable; it was not restricted to coastal districts.

secs.t: Water resources - glacier-fed rivers, groundwater, monsoon variability, drought

x: The National Water Mission aims to improve water-use efficiency by
The National Water Mission under NAPCC is dated
30 June 2008
Falling groundwater levels are reported in Punjab, Haryana and parts of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
El Niño usually weakens the southwest monsoon
Glacier meltwater sustains the
Indus basin

secs.t: Fisheries and marine resources - fish stock shifts, marine heatwaves

x: More than
of the oceans experienced marine heatwaves in 2025.
Marine heatwaves lower oxygen levels and harm fish and other marine organisms.
Ocean acidification affects
corals, shellfish and fish
, among other marine organisms.

secs.t: Adaptation measures - insurance, bio-shields, early warning, conflict and migration

x: The Andhra Pradesh Heat Wave Action Plan is cited as a model of early-warning and preparedness action.
The NDC 2031–35 adaptation focus includes
coasts, heat and infrastructure
Belem Adaptation Indicators are associated with climate-change adaptation, as referenced in the NDC 2031–35 context.
Both statements are true, and threats to food security from extreme weather provide the reason why climate change can increase social tension.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The WMO decadal update and UNEP’s assessment indicate that 1.5°C is effectively breached, while a strong El Niño is considered likely in 2027.
The APSDMA Heatwave Action Plan 2026 identifies heatwaves as causing more deaths in Andhra Pradesh than any other natural disaster.
The criticism is that ‘loss and damage’ is being understood locally as merely
disaster relief
, although the concept concerns wider climate-related losses and damages.
