rows.title: Solid waste, plastic waste, e-waste, biomedical and construction waste - rules and management
sub: Group-II M2-B-67: Solid wastes - definition and classification: municipal, industrial, hazardous, biomedical, e-waste, agricultural
Group-II M2-B-68: Methods of disposal and management of solid waste in India - collection, segregation, landfill, composting, incineration
Group-II M2-B-69: Solid Waste Management Rules and the Swachh Bharat Mission (urban and rural)
Group-II M2-B-70: Plastic waste management - rules, single-use plastic ban and extended producer responsibility
Group-II M2-B-71: E-waste management - magnitude, rules and recycling; biomedical waste rules
Group-II M2-B-72: Construction and demolition waste; hazardous waste rules and management

secs.t: Disposal methods → waste type

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2023 match - organic-II (composting), e-waste-IV (recycling), hazardous-I (incineration), glass-III (landfilling).
Anaerobic digestion converts segregated organic waste into methane-rich biogas and slurry manure.
The Bangalore method uses anaerobic pits containing alternate layers of municipal solid waste and night soil and generally takes four to six months.

E-waste is sent for recycling, broken glass pieces are landfilled, biomedical waste is incinerated at a common biomedical waste treatment facility, and high-calorific dry waste is used as RDF or co-processed in cement kilns.
High-calorific plastic, paper and textile waste can be shredded and dried to produce RDF, which may be used as fuel in cement kilns.
Composting is aerobic biological treatment, anaerobic digestion is oxygen-free biological treatment, incineration is combustion, and pyrolysis is heating without oxygen.

secs.t: Swachh Bharat Mission, SBM-U 2.0, Swachh Survekshan

x: Swachh Survekshan is the world's largest annual urban cleanliness survey, conducted by the
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs under SBM-Urban
Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 has 10 sections and more than 160 indicators, along with a separate LENS matrix for river towns.
Indore and Surat jointly
occupied the cleanest-city position in the 2023 edition for cities with more than 10 lakh population.
Andhra Pradesh established Project Monitoring Units in 46 ULBs through the Swachha Andhra Corporation, selected on the basis of Swachh Survekshan 2024 rankings.
Indore topped the 10 lakh-plus Super Swachh League for the
eighth time
in Swachh Survekshan 2024-25.
SBM-Urban 2.0 includes source segregation, legacy-dump remediation and C&D waste management, but does not prescribe
privatisation of all municipal water supply systems
The Garbage Free City certification uses 1-star, 3-star, 5-star and 7-star ratings for waste management.
Indore
is identified as India’s model zero-waste or landfill-free city and has repeatedly ranked first in cleanliness assessments.
India's irrigated paddy emits about 3.9 million tonnes of methane annually, slightly more than Germany's total methane emissions.
The waste sector accounted for
of India's emissions in 2020 according to the Fourth Biennial Update Report.
The stated urban set-up consists of
17 Municipal Corporations, 113 municipalities and 7 cantonment boards

secs.t: E-waste (Management) Rules 2022

x: The Rules cover 106 electrical and electronic equipment items, including solar PV modules, panels and cells.
The Rules permit
only registered producers, manufacturers, refurbishers and recyclers
to deal in e-waste.
The Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 replaced the 2001 rules and cover electric-vehicle, portable, automotive and industrial batteries under EPR.
EPR supports a circular economy by making producers responsible for collection and recycling obligations and by facilitating resource recovery through registered entities.

secs.t: Waste rules - MSW 2000 → SWM 2016 → SWM 2026; C&D; hazardous

x: The 2016 Rules cover all four categories, including urban agglomerations, census towns, industrial townships, transport facilities, SEZs and religious or historical places.
The 2016 Rules provided for user fees, spot fines, extended producer responsibility for producers and brand owners, and prohibited the disposal of untreated waste in landfills.
The four streams are
wet, dry, sanitary and special care
waste, the last category covering domestic hazardous waste.
The 2026 Rules require mapping of legacy dumpsites, time-bound biomining and submission of quarterly reports.
The specified thresholds are
100 kg of waste per day, 5,000 litres of water per day or 20,000 square metres
Bulk Waste Generators must process wet waste on site or obtain an EBWGR certificate as prescribed under the 2026 Rules.
Hill and island local bodies may levy user fees on tourists and regulate tourist inflow as part of waste-management measures.
The hierarchy begins with prevention, followed by minimisation, reuse, recycling, recovery, co-processing and finally safe disposal.

secs.t: Biomedical waste - colour coding, treatment

x: Yellow-category waste includes anatomical, soiled, expired medicine and chemical waste and is treated through incineration, plasma pyrolysis or deep burial.
Contaminated recyclable plastics are placed in the
red
category and are autoclaved or microwaved before shredding and recycling.
Sharps, including needles and blades, are placed in the
white, translucent
category and may undergo autoclaving or dry heat treatment, shredding and encapsulation.
Blood, sharps, cultures and discarded or expired medicines are all examples of biomedical waste; anatomical and chemical waste are also included.

secs.t: 3Rs and circular economy

x: Source reduction
means generating less waste and occupies the top position in the waste-management hierarchy.
Fly ash is used in bricks, cement and roads within 300 km of thermal plants, while steel slag is used as a road aggregate.
Biomining of legacy waste supports the circular economy by recovering materials from old waste accumulations for reuse or further processing.

secs.t: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types

x: Exam angle: APPSC-GS 2021 - 2021 Rules aimed at phasing out SUP by
; EPR guidelines effective
July 2022
The stated progression is
40 microns in 2011, 50 microns in 2016, 75 microns from 30 September 2021 and 120 microns from 31 December 2022
EPR applies to Producers, Importers and Brand Owners, or PIBOs, for plastic packaging not covered by the SUP ban.
EPR first entered Indian waste law through the
E-waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2011
The 2026 amendment includes all four measures: classification into three categories, three-year carry-forward, tradable certificates and specified end-of-life options.
The recycled-content requirement for rigid plastics rises from 30% to
The reuse targets are
10% for small containers and 70% for large water packaging
On the centralised CPCB EPR portal,
recyclers generate EPR certificates and sell them to producers
The reported figures were 69,470 registered producers, 4,402 registered recyclers and approximately 354 LMT of waste recycled across EPR streams.
Tea bags and chewing gum
are among the hidden sources of plastic.

secs.t: AP waste bodies - APEMC, Clean Andhra Pradesh

x: Operation Clean Sweep is the Municipal Administration Department’s campaign for
scientific solid-waste management in Tier-1 and Tier-2 corporations
Anantapur is setting up a 170 tonnes-per-day waste-processing plant.
Ongole is biomining its Guthikondavaripalem waste yard.

secs.t: Biodegradable vs non-biodegradable

x: Exam angle: "which is NOT biodegradable" - tin/metal/glass/plastic; "which IS biodegradable" - wool, peels.
Tin scrap
is a metal and cannot normally be decomposed by microorganisms.
Microorganisms decompose biodegradable matter into simpler substances; oxygen-supported decomposition produces compost, while anaerobic decomposition produces methane or biogas.
Non-biodegradable waste is generally inorganic, is not broken down by microorganisms and accumulates in the environment.

secs.t: Indian municipal solid waste - composition, generation, highest-generating states

x: Biodegradable waste is about 55–60 per cent, recyclable waste 15–20 per cent, and hazardous or non-recyclable waste 15–25 per cent.
The independent estimates and the official SBM-U processing figures refer to different reporting bases.
India ranks third among dry municipal solid-waste generators of
textile waste
, producing approximately 7.8 million tonnes annually.

secs.t: Industrial solid wastes → source industry and reuse

x: Fly ash comes from coal-based thermal power plants, steel slag from steel plants, red mud from alumina refining, and phosphogypsum from phosphoric acid or phosphatic fertiliser plants.
Mine tailings, overburden and waste rock can be reused for
backfilling
Non-ferrous mine tailings may contain heavy metals and can cause acid or alkaline drainage.

secs.t: Solid waste definition and categories

x: The definition includes discarded or abandoned materials that are solid, liquid, semi-solid or containerised gaseous.
Construction and demolition waste is generally inert and includes
concrete, dirt, rocks and debris
Industrial solid waste includes process by-products and is often hazardous.

secs.t: Source segregation categories - item → bin

x: The 2026 Rules, which replaced the 2016 Rules, provide
four
streams: wet, dry, sanitary and special-care domestic hazardous waste.

Wet waste includes food scraps, peels and garden waste; dry waste includes paper, plastics, metals, glass and wood; sanitary waste includes diapers and napkins; special-care waste includes batteries, chemicals and paint cans.

secs.t: Hazardous waste - defining characteristics, household examples

x: The four classic characteristics are ignitability, corrosivity, reactivity and toxicity.
The AP classification adds explosive, infectious and radioactive characteristics to the four classic criteria.
Hazardous waste can occur as solids, liquids, sludges and gases.
Paints and batteries
are household examples of hazardous waste.

secs.t: Waste hierarchy - 3R/5R

x: Reduction at source is the top priority.
Expanded 5R versions may add
Refuse and Repurpose
or, in some versions, Recover.
Every city has a permanent RRR Centre under SBM-U 2.0.

secs.t: Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF)

x: RDF is made by shredding and dehydrating high-calorific MSW, mainly non-recyclable plastic, paper and textiles, after recyclables and biodegradable material are removed.
The APPCB permitted 12 cement industries to co-process incinerable, plastic and municipal waste.
Andhra Pradesh has two Common Hazardous Waste Treatment, Storage and Disposal Facilities, six pre-processing facilities and twelve cement units permitted for co-processing.

secs.t: AP state agency for integrated waste chain

x: Swachha Andhra Corporation
, or SAC, is the state agency running urban sanitation under SBM-U 2.0 in Andhra Pradesh.
SAC operationalised Project Monitoring Units in 46 urban local bodies for Swachh Survekshan 2026.
The Re Sustainability MoU covers all 123 ULBs for scientific e-waste collection, disposal and material recovery facilities.
Biomedical waste is sent to Common Bio-Medical Waste Treatment Facilities for
incineration

secs.t: Collection chain - door-to-door, segregation, transfer stations, MRFs

x: The chain begins with door-to-door collection, followed by segregated transport, transfer station, MRF, processing or recycling, and final residual landfill.
The cited figures are 49.32% of wards with 100% source segregation and MRFs in 101 ULBs.
The cited national gaps were that only 68% of ULBs had notified solid-waste-management by-laws and fewer than 45% had achieved full segregation.

secs.t: Waste-to-energy - WtE, bio-CNG, CBG

x: The cited figures are 21 operational WtE plants producing more than 170 MW and 133 biogas facilities.
The SATAT and GOBARdhan linkage targets 500 new waste-to-wealth compressed biogas plants.
CBG plants convert municipal wet waste into
green fuel
The
Circular Bioenergy Scheme
of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas supports 100% scientific processing in the cited context.

secs.t: Legacy waste - biomining and remediation

x: Legacy waste is old municipal solid waste accumulated in dumpsites over several years.
Biomining involves excavation and separation of legacy waste into recyclables, RDF, bio-soil and inert fill.
The approach requires mapping all legacy dumpsites, time-bound biomining or bioremediation and quarterly reporting.
At Guthikondavaripalem,
1.76 lakh tonnes
out of 2.56 lakh tonnes of legacy waste had been processed.

secs.t: SBM-Grameen - launch, ministry, Phase II, ODF Plus, toilets

x: SBM-Grameen is run by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation under the
Ministry of Jal Shakti
ODF Plus combines sustained ODF status with management of greywater, faecal sludge and plastic waste, along with options such as biogas and composting.
The ten-year Rural Sanitation Strategy for 2019–2029 was prepared by the
Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation

secs.t: Clean Andhra Pradesh (CLAP) programme

x: CLAP was launched on 2 October 2021 under the name
Jagananna Swachha Sankalpam

secs.t: Predecessor sanitation programmes

x: The correct order is Central Rural Sanitation Programme (1986), Total Sanitation Campaign (1999), Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan (2012), and Swachh Bharat Mission (2014).
Integrated Low Cost Sanitation dates to 1980–81, the Central Rural Sanitation Programme to 1986, the Total Sanitation Campaign to 1999 and Nirmal Gram Puraskar to 2003.
The Integrated Low Cost Sanitation programme focused on converting dry latrines into pour-flush latrines and freeing manual scavengers.

secs.t: Allied initiatives

x: GOBARdhan promotes conversion of cattle dung, agricultural waste and solid waste into
biogas and bio-slurry
, supported by a unified portal.
Swachhata Hi Seva has been observed as a fortnight shramdaan campaign every year since 2017.

secs.t: Single-use plastic ban

x: Plastic-stemmed earbuds, straws, stirrers and PVC banners below 100 microns are among the identified banned items.
Enforcement involves State Pollution Control Boards or Pollution Control Committees and local bodies, along with a National Level Taskforce and State Special Task Forces.
The ban covers only about
of total plastic waste.

secs.t: Global plastic bans - FIRST countries

x: Bangladesh was the first country to ban thin plastic bags in 2002.
China's National Sword Policy and Thailand's 2025 measure restrict imports of plastic waste.

secs.t: Microplastics

x: Nurdles are primary microplastic pellets, generally 1–5 mm in size.
The first major nurdle landing in India occurred in Kerala following the MSC Elsa 3 shipwreck.
The stated responses include the microbead restriction and the National Action Plan for Marine Litter.

secs.t: Plastic types and additives

x: PET
is widely used for water and soft-drink bottles and may leach additives when heated.
Polycarbonate hard bottles and containers can release
bisphenol A
, or BPA, an endocrine disruptor.
Tyres contain
synthetic rubber
, and their wear is a source of microplastics.

secs.t: Plastic alternatives and reuse

x: Compostable plastics must meet the
IS/ISO 17088
standard.
The 2024 amendment defined biodegradable plastics and required CPCB certification for their makers.
All four statements describe recognised or promoted routes for plastic-waste utilisation and recovery.

secs.t: Global Plastics Treaty

x: The UNEA-5.2 resolution titled “
End Plastic Pollution
” established the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee.
The INC venues were Punta del Este, Paris, Nairobi, Ottawa, Busan and Geneva in that order.
Production caps, chemicals of concern and finance were the major sticking points.

secs.t: AP plastic curbs

x: Andhra Pradesh bans single-use plastic and carry bags below
120 microns
, with enforcement involving the Revenue Department, Police and Pollution Control Board.
The reported seizures were 5,505.06 kg of carry bags and 3,571.40 kg of single-use plastic.
Guntur’s complete ban was scheduled from 15 August 2026, fines could reach ₹5,000, and the Swachh App was to be used for fines.

secs.t: Hazardous constituents of e-waste - effects

x: Old computers can release beryllium, cadmium, chromium, mercury and lead, besides PCBs and PBBs.
Lead affects the nervous system and kidneys; mercury damages the brain and kidneys and bioaccumulates in fish; cadmium damages kidneys and bones; PBBs are persistent and have endocrine effects.
Improper disposal releases toxic substances into soil and water, thereby damaging ecosystems and biodiversity.

secs.t: Recycling chain - recyclers, dismantlers, citizens, informal hubs, R2

x: The authorised chain begins with the consumer and collection or producer take-back, followed by dismantling, recycling and recovery of materials.
Citizens should use authorised recyclers or collection centres and wipe personal data before handing over old electronics.
Separate handling is required; Seelampur and Moradabad are informal hubs; and CPCB data mention 468 authorised recyclers with 1.6 million tonnes of capacity.

secs.t: E-waste magnitude - India's rank, generation, processing

x: India is the
third
-largest e-waste generator, after China and the United States.
India’s e-waste generation was reported as approximately 2.2 million tonnes in 2025.

secs.t: Global E-waste Monitor

x: The Global E-waste Monitor is published by the International Telecommunication Union and the United Nations Institute for Training and Research.
The Global E-waste Monitor uses
six
categories, including cooling equipment, screens, lamps, large equipment, small equipment and IT equipment.

secs.t: COVID-19 biomedical waste guidelines and tracking app

x: The CPCB issued COVID-19 biomedical-waste guidelines in 2020 and introduced the COVID19BWM tracking app.

secs.t: International conventions → subject + India's status

x: India ratified Basel in June 1992, acceded to Rotterdam in 2005, and has designated authorities in the Chemicals and Fertilisers and Agriculture Ministries.
Transboundary hazardous-waste movement involves the physical transfer of hazardous waste for reprocessing or storage, frequently to developing countries.

The Montreal Protocol has an indirect greenhouse-gas relevance because CFCs are greenhouse gases, while the other statements correctly identify the subjects of the Paris, Minamata and Stockholm instruments.

secs.t: Chemical disasters in news

x: The Bhopal disaster involving Union Carbide India Ltd was caused by
methyl isocyanate
337 tonnes were incinerated, about 900 tonnes of toxic residual ash remained, and the Supreme Court directed the victims’ NGO to approach the Madhya Pradesh High Court.
The EPA of 1986 was enacted after the Bhopal disaster, which occurred in December 1984.

secs.t: Hazardous chemicals in consumer products - PFAS, mercury lamps

x: PFAS are persistent chemicals found in drinking water, food and food packaging.
Fluorescent lamps and CFLs contain
mercury
Mercury-added products are being phased out under the Minamata Convention, which addresses mercury pollution and its risks.

secs.t: Construction and demolition waste

x: Construction and demolition waste is mostly inert and commonly consists of
concrete, bricks, dirt, rocks and debris
The 2016 Rules cover waste arising from building, renovation, excavation, road, flyover, bridge and pipeline activities.
The 2016 framework covers collection, transport, storage and re-processing, permits charges on bulk generators and treats C&D waste as a resource.

secs.t: Environment (C&D Waste Management) Rules 2025

x: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has notified an Extended Producer Responsibility framework for C&D waste under the 2025 rules.

secs.t: Hazardous waste legal framework

x: The framework bans import of hazardous waste for disposal and follows a hierarchy in which prevention precedes safe disposal.
PIC means
Prior Informed Consent
, a control associated with the import and export of hazardous waste.
The Act provides no-fault insurance cover intended to give immediate relief to victims of accidents involving hazardous substances.
The framework requires district half-yearly reports on suspected contaminated sites and identifies 189 hazardous chemicals.

secs.t: Fly Ash Utilisation Notification

x: The notification requires utilisation of fly ash for specified construction purposes within
300 km
of thermal plants, helping prevent dumping on soil.
Fly ash can be used to make building bricks and can partly replace Portland cement in concrete.

secs.t: Hazardous waste disposal - secure landfills, treatment, inventory

x: Landfill is considered the last resort.
The two CHWTSDFs identified for Andhra Pradesh are located in
Anakapalli and SPSR Nellore
APEMC uses
GPS tracking
for monitoring hazardous-waste movement and management.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Operation Clean Sweep was conducted across all 123 Urban Local Bodies from 23 May to 20 June 2026 under the Swarna Andhra-Swachh Andhra initiative.
The Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (
GVMC
) threatened to seal an apartment that did not maintain two segregation bins.
The 2026 campaign of Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen was titled “
Swabhav Swachhata - Sanskaar Swachhata
Rural waste is shifting from predominantly biodegradable waste towards plastic, sanitary and other non-biodegradable waste.
More than 70% of recycled plastic is handled by informal workers, NAMASTE seeks to formalise them, and approximately 15 lakh waste-pickers remain outside formal systems.
Vapes, USB cables and LED accessories
are examples of ‘invisible e-waste’ that may be thrown into regular waste streams.
The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 serves as an umbrella for frameworks including the EIA, Hazardous Waste, Coastal Regulation Zone and Contaminated Sites Rules.
The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 have raised
questions concerning federalism and administrative design

rows.title: Carbon emissions, carbon footprint, carbon sequestration, carbon credits and carbon trading

secs.t: Emitters - largest countries, India's rank, per-capita and sector-wise emissions

x: The roadmaps rely on renewable energy available round the clock, nuclear power and carbon capture, utilisation and storage.
A carbon bomb is a fossil-fuel project capable of emitting more than 1 gigatonne of CO2 during its lifetime.
LINGO lists 425 carbon-bomb projects, with China, the USA, Russia and Saudi Arabia as the leading countries associated with them.

secs.t: Carbon capture and removal - CCS vs CCUS vs sequestration, DAC, rock weathering, ocean alkalinity

x: CCS captures CO2 at stationary sources such as power plants and stores it in geological or ocean formations.
CCUS involves using captured CO2 or storing it permanently and can support coal gasification and hydrogen.
Enhanced rock weathering uses crushed silicate rocks such as basalt, which chemically bind CO2 as carbonate when spread on land.

secs.t: Footprint concepts - carbon (Scopes 1-3), ecological, water

x: The carbon footprint measures total greenhouse-gas emissions from human activities in tonnes of CO2 equivalent per year.
The ecological footprint measures the land and water needed to produce consumed goods and absorb associated waste.
Direct emissions from owned sources are Scope 1, emissions from purchased electricity or heat are Scope 2, and the remaining value-chain emissions are Scope 3.

secs.t: Carbon pricing - carbon tax, agricultural emissions tax, EU CBAM

x: New Zealand was the first country to propose a tax on agricultural emissions, while Denmark is to become the first to actually levy a livestock carbon tax from 2030.
All three figures are stated: revenue exceeded $107 billion in 2025, ETS coverage tripled since 2016, and carbon pricing covered 29% of global greenhouse-gas emissions.

secs.t: Carbon monitoring - National Carbon Project (ISRO-GBP), carbon pools, CO2 satellites

x: The National Carbon Project is implemented under the
ISRO Geosphere-Biosphere Programme
The project assesses carbon pools, fluxes and the net carbon balance of terrestrial biomes, with sub-projects on vegetation carbon, soil carbon and related fluxes.
The five pools are above-ground biomass, below-ground biomass, dead wood, litter and soil organic carbon.
NASA's OCO-2 and Japan's GOSAT
are CO2-observing satellites.

secs.t: Low-carbon power with capture - net-zero gas plants, BECCS

x: NET Power’s Allam-Fetvedt cycle plant is located at
La Porte, Texas
The Allam-Fetvedt cycle burns gas in oxygen, uses supercritical CO2 and captures nearly all the released CO2.
BECCS
means bioenergy with carbon capture and storage; it can generate net-negative emissions.
Nuclear power supplies close to one-third of the world’s low-carbon electricity.

secs.t: Carbon credits and markets - one credit, Kyoto, CERs, Verra/Gold Standard, CCTS 2023

x: The railway siding is the world’s first
modal-shift project
registered with Verra’s Verified Carbon Standard.
All three statements describe the Gujarat in-plant railway siding project: its Verra registration, expected credits and AM0090 methodology.
The programme follows the DST roadmap and concerns industrial carbon credits; it is not a farmer-only scheme.

secs.t: Carbon sinks - forest carbon stock, REDD+, peatlands, blue carbon

x: Blue carbon is stored in coastal ecosystems such as mangroves, seagrass beds and salt marshes.
REDD+ stands for
Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation
, with conservation and sustainable forest management dimensions.
India participates in REDD+, forest conservation can generate tradable credits, and the two named programmes raise forest carbon stock.

secs.t: Carbon-neutral claims - FIRST panchayat, airport, state

x: Palli in Samba, Jammu and Kashmir, was declared India’s first carbon-neutral panchayat in 2022.
Ladakh’s carbon-neutral effort includes solar water lifting, passive solar buildings, geothermal heating and electric vehicles.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The criticism of CBAM as potentially placing India in a rule-taker position is framed as a climate-justice issue.
Agricultural credits face
measurement and credibility gaps
, which affect the reliability of claimed reductions or removals.

rows.title: Recent projects, acts and initiatives to reduce environmental pollution in India
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-90

secs.t: Alternatives to conventional pollution control - green technology, CCS, bioremediation

x: Green technology includes cleaner processes and products, such as efficient kilns with precalciners and dry-process technology.
Bioremediation is eco-friendly and cost-effective, but it is slower and its effectiveness varies with environmental conditions.
Incineration is a conventional waste-treatment method and is not classified as an alternative pollution-control approach in this context.
Electrostatic precipitators, scrubbers and selective catalytic reduction are conventional end-of-pipe tools.

secs.t: AP state measures to check industrial pollution - condition imposed, year

x: APPCB issues siting guidelines for industries near habitations, water bodies and fragile areas.
Andhra Pradesh streamlined clearances through
digitisation and single-window systems
under BRAP.

secs.t: Eco-labels - Ecomark and Blue Flag

x: The notified Ecomark categories included soaps and detergents, paper, plastics, cosmetics and aerosols.
The 2024 Ecomark Rules replaced the 1991 scheme and aim to ensure accurate labelling, prevent misleading green claims and support informed purchases.
PRAMAAN is a voluntary third-party forest and wood certification initiative for sustainable forestry and agroforestry.

secs.t: Recent legal changes - Jan Vishwas amendments, environmental compensation rules

x: The 2023 Jan Vishwas amendment decriminalised minor offences under the
Air Act and Environment (Protection) Act
by replacing imprisonment with monetary penalties.
The Water Act was amended in 2024 in a similar manner
, following the 2023 changes concerning minor offences under the Air Act and Environment (Protection) Act.
The revised categories introduced a new Blue category, illustrated by compressed biogas, and replaced the mandatory 33% green belt requirement with pollution-potential norms.

secs.t: Clean-energy schemes cutting pollution - PMUY, PM-KUSUM, PM E-DRIVE, PM Surya Ghar

x: PM Ujjwala Yojana was launched in 2016 to provide free LPG connections to poor households, promoting clean cooking and reducing indoor smoke.
PM Ujjwala Yojana was launched in 2016, PM-KUSUM in 2019, and both PM E-DRIVE and PM Surya Ghar in 2024; the stated.
The assessment cites PMUY as a model clean-cooking programme and identifies
clean cooking
and heating as South Asia’s leading solution towards 2035.

secs.t: Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage - roadmap, pilots

x: Research on CCS is ongoing for cement plants, and NITI Aayog published a report on a CCUS policy framework in 2022.

secs.t: Industrial clean-up tools - online monitoring, inventories

x: CAAQMS tracks PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NOx, CO, O3 and NH3.
PARIVESH 3.0 functions as a single-window portal for environmental clearances and compliance monitoring.
SAAP, dating from 1992, provides grants to
strengthen Pollution Control Boards
The CPCB made online continuous emission and effluent monitoring compulsory for highly polluting industries in the 17-category classification.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The debates include concerns that decriminalisation and relaxed green-belt norms could reduce deterrence.
Ex-post facto clearances are granted after the relevant project or activity has already begun, making them a subject of environmental debate.
The emerging approach moves beyond end-of-pipe control towards prevention, including clean fuels, eco-labels and market credits.

rows.title: Environmental hazards and disaster management - DM Act 2005, NDMA and NDRF, Sendai Framework, disaster types and mitigation

secs.t: Industrial and man-made disasters - Bhopal gas tragedy, classification of disasters

x: Exam angle: "which category" questions - fire, gas leak, epidemic.
Earthquakes are geological or geophysical; floods are hydro-meteorological; extreme temperatures are climatological; and chemical and industrial accidents are man-made or technological.
Chemical accidents fall under the Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemicals Rules, 1989 and the Chemical Accidents (Emergency Planning, Preparedness and Response) Rules, 1996.

secs.t: Institutions - NDMA, MHA, fire services, NDRF, NIDM, APSDMA

x: Fire services are a State subject, and the DG Fire Services, Civil Defence and Home Guards under MHA has an advisory role.
The southern campus of NIDM was set up at
Kondapavuluru in Krishna district
, pursuant to the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
APSDMA is chaired by the Chief Minister, serves as the State’s chief nodal agency, runs the State Emergency Operations Centre and supports early warning.

secs.t: Global frameworks - IDNDR, Hyogo, Sendai, post-2015 frameworks

x: The four priorities are understanding risk, strengthening risk governance, investing in disaster-risk reduction for resilience, and enhancing preparedness for effective response and to Build Back Better.

The Sendai global targets include increasing the availability of and access to multi-hazard early-warning systems, along with reducing mortality, affected people, economic loss and infrastructure damage.

secs.t: Disaster terms - hazard, vulnerability, risk, resilience, DM cycle

x: A hazard is a potentially damaging event.
Vulnerability is susceptibility to harm and may be physical, social, economic or environmental.
Capacity comprises the strengths and resources available to individuals, communities and institutions to cope with hazards.
Resilience
is the ability to resist, absorb and recover quickly from the effects of a hazard.

secs.t: Disaster types - criteria and mitigation

x: IMD warnings, shelters, evacuation, shelter belts and mangroves are cyclone-related measures.
Coringa and Krishna are associated with mangroves that help mitigate cyclones and storm surges.
The
Ministry of Agriculture
administers drought-related matters along with hailstorm, frost and pest attack.
Floods are mitigated through embankments and forecasting; landslides through zonation and warnings; and the stated thresholds define heat-wave and cold-wave conditions in plains.

secs.t: Community-based DRR - PRIs, volunteers, mock drills

x: The Disaster Management Act gives PRIs and ULBs a legal role in local plans, relief and capacity building.
Aapda Mitra is an NDMA scheme for training community volunteers to act as first responders.
Social media can support communication and community engagement, but it is a complementary tool rather than a replacement for official disaster-management systems.

secs.t: HADR operations - country assisted

x: Operation Vanilla assisted Madagascar following Cyclone Diane in 2020.
Maitri assisted Nepal, Dost assisted Turkey and Syria, Karuna assisted Myanmar, and Sadbhav assisted Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar.
Operation
Karuna
was associated with assistance to Myanmar after Cyclone Mocha in 2023.
Operation Brahma assisted Myanmar following the 2025 earthquake.

secs.t: DRR conferences and early warning - NPDRR, Sachet

x: NPDRR is a multi-stakeholder body chaired by the
Union Home Minister
SACHET is NDMA's Common Alerting Protocol-based alert system, developed by C-DOT.
The 'Resilient India 2047' push is associated with
NDMA and Ministry disaster-management plans

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh released
Rs 277.63 crore
under SDRF/NDRF in 2025–26, compared with Rs 479.01 crore in 2026–27.
The Godavari floods in July 2026 tested NDRF and SDRF operations along with early-warning mechanisms.
The Disaster Management Act, 2005 marked a shift from a primarily relief-oriented approach towards risk reduction and more comprehensive disaster management.

rows.title: Preparedness and response - surveillance, Epidemic Diseases Act, National Health Emergency framework
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-91

secs.t: Geospatial tools in epidemic response - contact tracing, hotspots, vaccine distribution, war rooms

x: Geospatial technology can support
contact tracing
by identifying people who may have been exposed to an infectious disease.
Geospatial technology supports contact tracing, hotspot and containment-zone mapping, and GIS-based real-time vaccine distribution planning.
The GIS-supported COVID war room was set up by the
Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike
(BBMP).
U-WIN is a current surveillance and tracking tool for immunisation.

secs.t: Disaster management cycle for epidemics - classifying measures

x: Pre-outbreak vaccine distribution reduces the potential impact of an epidemic and is therefore a
mitigation
measure.
All four pairs correctly associate epidemic measures with the mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery phases respectively.
The sequence is mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery: sanitation and vector control, surveillance and readiness, isolation and contact tracing, and finally rehabilitation and relief.

secs.t: Institutional framework - nodal ministry, NDMA guidelines

x: The Directorate General of Health Services (
DGHS
) functions as the technical arm of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
NCDC, formerly NICD, is the apex surveillance and outbreak-response agency and runs IDSP.
The
NCDC
sends Outbreak Investigation Teams and runs the National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre.
PM-ABHIM includes
15 Health Emergency Operation Centres and 50 BHISHM Cubes
, which were deployed during Operation Sindoor.

secs.t: AP COVID-era mobile applications and tracking tools

x: The AP Medical and Health Department launched Covid Pharma on 25 April 2020 to track people buying over-the-counter
medicines for cough, cold and fever

secs.t: Legal basis - Epidemic Diseases Act 1897, 2020 amendment, DM Act 2005, draft Public Health Bill

x: The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 provides the legal framework for dealing with biological disasters and epidemics and was used during COVID-19.
The 2020 amendment made violence against health workers cognizable and non-bailable and also gave the Centre powers over inspection at ports of entry.
For grievous hurt, the amendment provided imprisonment from
six months to seven years and a fine of Rs 1 lakh to Rs 5 lakh

secs.t: Disease surveillance - IDSP, IHIP, sentinel sites

x: IHIP was launched in a few states in 2018 and became nationwide from
September 2021
Data are fed into the surveillance system by sentinel sites as well as private sites.
The Centre
asked States to step up IDSP surveillance for Ebola.
AP is preparing the plan under the One Health approach with NCDC, US CDC and Jhpiego.

secs.t: Laboratory network - NIV Pune, BSL-3/4, INSACOG

x: ICMR-NIV Pune is the apex virology laboratory and has BSL-4 containment facilities.
Additional BSL-3 laboratories are being established through Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories and PM-ABHIM.
The Indian SARS-CoV-2 Genomics Consortium was established in
December 2020
By January 2022, COVID testing had expanded to
1,364 government and 1,753 private laboratories

secs.t: PM-ABHIM - critical care blocks, IPHLs

x: There are 631 Critical Care Hospital Blocks, intended for districts with more than five lakh people.
The prescribed scale is 23,224 Rural Health and Wellness Centres and 13,736 Urban Health and Wellness Centres.
At Vijayawada, 10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 Integrated Public Health Laboratories were opened at a cost of Rs 250 crore.

secs.t: International Health Regulations 2005 - PHEIC, India's obligations

x: The IHR (2005) are
a legally binding instrument of the World Health Organization
All three are obligations under the IHR (2005): building surveillance and response capacities, reporting possible PHEICs to WHO within 24 hours, and naming a National IHR Focal Point.
The May 2026 Ebola outbreak was a PHEIC, but it did not meet the criteria for the higher pandemic-emergency tier.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The BRICS New Delhi Declaration set up a sub-working group on an integrated early-warning system for infectious diseases.
The 1897 Act is criticised as colonial and for lacking both a definition of dangerous epidemic disease and adequate rights safeguards.
The Andhra Pradesh-specific measures include the Covid Pharma app and a zoonoses action plan launched in July 2026.

rows.title: Biotechnology - nature, scope, tools; applications in agriculture, medicine and industry
sub: Group-II M2-B-86: Bioremediation - meaning, types (in-situ and ex-situ), phytoremediation and bioaugmentation
Group-II M2-B-87: Scope and applications of bioremediation in India

secs.t: Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes

x: Exam angle: in-situ vs ex-situ; match technique to agent.
Exam angle: "Which is NOT bioremediation?" - burning contaminated soil; composting and bacterial oil clean-up are.
Bioremediation uses organisms such as bacteria, fungi, algae and plants, or their enzymes, to degrade or remove pollutants and restore a contaminated environment.
Bioventing and biosparging are in-situ methods, landfarming is ex-situ, and bioreactors are described as the fastest but costliest systems.
Landfarming, composting and biopiles
require contaminated material to be treated outside its original location and are ex-situ techniques.
In-situ bioremediation
treats contamination at its original site and is generally cheaper and more passive than ex-situ treatment.
The examples include TERI's Chennai port work, CPCB treatment of oil-contaminated soils, CSIR-NEERI heavy-metal technology and biomining of legacy waste.
Biotechnology uses genetically modified microbes and plants for pollution reduction and resource conservation, including oil degradation and plastic breakdown.

Engineered Pseudomonas and algae can target oil spills, PETase-producing bacteria break down plastic, engineered microbes can produce PLA and PHA, and biofilters use microbe-laden beds to treat air or gas streams.
Climate-resilient agriculture
is identified as a key thematic area of the BioE3 policy, whose full form is Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment.

secs.t: Vaccine platforms and indigenous vaccines

x: Cervavac is developed by the Serum Institute of India against HPV and cervical cancer.
mRNA, viral-vector and protein-subunit platforms are all identified as indigenous vaccine platforms in India.
ZyCoV-D was developed by Zydus Cadila and is identified as the first DNA vaccine, targeting COVID-19.
R21/Matrix-M was developed by Oxford University and made by the Serum Institute of India for malaria.

secs.t: Advanced therapies - CAR-T, gene therapy, monoclonals, stem cells, ART

x: The first indigenous haemophilia A gene-therapy trial was conducted at CMC Vellore with support from the Department of Biotechnology.
Hybridoma technology fuses antibody-producing B-cells with myeloma cells to create continuously multiplying antibody-producing cells.
The Guidelines date to 2017, the ART (Regulation) Act to 2021 and the hybridoma technique to 1975.

secs.t: Industrial biotechnology - fermentation, enzymes, bioplastics

x: White biotechnology includes enzymes, biofuels, bioplastics, precision fermentation and green chemicals.
Recombinant
chymosin
is used in cheese production; amylase is associated with bread and pectinase with juice processing.
The targets include fuels from agricultural residue and municipal waste, algal fuels, sustainable aviation fuel and integrated biorefineries.

secs.t: Policy and hubs - BioE3, BIRAC, Bio-RIDE, AMTZ

x: BioE3 stands for Economy, Environment and Employment and promotes
high-performance biomanufacturing
The bioeconomy is stated to have risen from $10 billion in 2014 to
$165.7 billion
in 2024, with a target of $300 billion by 2030.
The DBT was established in 1986 and emerged from the National Biotechnology Board, established in 1982.

secs.t: Agricultural biotechnology - biofertilisers, biopesticides, tissue culture, MAS

x: Azotobacter
is a free-living nitrogen fixer.
All three pairs are correctly matched.
BARC
is associated with tissue-culture applications for banana and pineapple.
Sub1 flood-tolerant rice
is given as an example of marker-assisted selection.

secs.t: Animal cloning

x: Dolly was the first cloned mammal, a sheep produced at Roslin Institute in 1996; Garima was a buffalo cloned at NDRI in 2009; and Noori was a Pashmina goat cloned in 2012.
Ganga is identified as the first cloned Gir calf and was born in 2023.

secs.t: Genomics and data - Genome India, IBDC, DNA fingerprinting, biobanks

x: IBDC serves as the national repository for
publicly funded life-science data
DNA fingerprinting uses variations in repetitive DNA, particularly variable number tandem repeats (VNTRs).
Alec Jeffreys developed DNA fingerprinting in 1984.
India’s first zoo bio-bank is at Padmaja Naidu Zoo, Darjeeling, in collaboration with CSIR-CCMB.
The zoo bio-bank at Padmaja Naidu Zoo stores material at

secs.t: Nature and tools - branches, PCR, electrophoresis, bioreactors

x: The CBD 1992 definition describes biotechnology as using biological systems to
make or modify products
PCR proceeds through denaturation, annealing and extension; extension involves polymerase-mediated synthesis of the complementary strand.
Gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments according to
size
Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sites, ligase joins DNA fragments, and plasmids can function as vectors.

secs.t: In-situ vs ex-situ - site, cost, techniques

x: In-situ treatment may face environmental constraints, require a long treatment time and be complicated by metals or inorganic contaminants.
Ex-situ treatment can require excavation and space and may face abiotic losses, mass-transfer limitations and poor bioavailability.
Ex-situ
bioreactors
can be the fastest option under optimised conditions because they permit rapid kinetics.

secs.t: Technique → pollutant or medium treated

x: Mycoremediation uses fungi, rhizofiltration uses plant roots to remove contaminants from water, biosparging injects air below the water table, and rhizoremediation involves root–microbe interactions in the rhizosphere.
Biostimulation adds nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus, and may also supply oxygen, to enhance the activity of existing microbes in polluted water bodies.

secs.t: Oil-spill microbes - Oilzapper developer, genetically engineered oil-degrading bacterium

x: Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S are bacterial consortia developed by TERI with Indian Oil.
Oilzapper has been used at
Chennai Port
for remediation of oil-contaminated material.
The first genetically engineered oil-eating bacterium was
Pseudomonas putida engineered by Ananda Mohan Chakrabarty
The case Diamond v. Chakrabarty, decided by the US Supreme Court in 1980, is associated with the first patenting of a living organism.

secs.t: Advantages and limitations of bioremediation

x: Bioremediation is often slow, and its results vary with the pollutant, organism, site conditions and co-contaminants.
Bioremediation may require regulation and monitoring; introducing microbes does not make oversight unnecessary.

secs.t: Phytoremediation sub-types

x: Phytoextraction involves uptake and harvesting, phytostabilisation immobilises contaminants, phytodegradation uses plant enzymes, and phytovolatilisation releases contaminants in volatile form.
Phytovolatilisation involves plant uptake followed by release into the air in volatile form; mercury and selenium are examples associated with this process.
Mangroves, estuarine vegetation and wetland vegetation are natural phytoremediators.

secs.t: Hyperaccumulator plants → metal accumulated

x: Pteris vittata accumulates arsenic; Brassica juncea accumulates lead, cadmium and selenium; Thlaspi caerulescens accumulates zinc and cadmium; and Alyssum species accumulate nickel.

secs.t: Bioremediation vs non-biological clean-up methods (thermal, chemical)

x: Microbial degradation, composting and constructed wetlands are biological methods.
Calcium chloride and magnesium chloride used as chemical dust suppressants represent chemical treatment.
The biological breakdown of organic waste by bacteria is microbial degradation and therefore constitutes
bioremediation

secs.t: Indian research bodies → bioremediation products

x: TERI is associated with Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S; CSIR-NEERI undertakes nodal bioremediation R&D; CPCB is associated with oil-contaminated soils; and DBT-BIRAC funds relevant biotechnology start-ups.

secs.t: Legacy dumpsite biomining under SBM-Urban 2.0 - AP cities

x: The Dumpsite Remediation Accelerator is an initiative of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0.
The target of the accelerator is described as “
Lakshya Zero Dumpsites
”, focusing on clearing legacy dumpsites through accelerated bioremediation.
The specified landfill category consists of
non-recyclable, non-energy-recoverable and inert waste

secs.t: Constructed wetlands and phytorid technology

x: Constructed wetlands may be natural or engineered systems where
plants and microbes break down and absorb pollutants
, especially in sewage treatment.
Phytorid is
a constructed-wetland sewage-treatment technology developed by CSIR-NEERI
Phytorid treats wastewater as it passes through
a planted gravel bed

secs.t: Lake and drain rejuvenation using bioremediation - Indian examples

x: Immediate bioremediation and decentralised STPs were proposed as a lower-cost alternative to pumping schemes.
Petitioner
Bollisetty Satyanarayana
proposed immediate bioremediation together with decentralised STPs.
Water hyacinth and duckweed
are used for phytoremediation of ponds.

secs.t: Advantages and limits vs conventional remediation - cost, time, scale

x: Bioremediation is described as scalable and community-applied, whereas conventional remediation is associated with large infrastructure.
Bioremediation uses minimal chemicals and is associated with no secondary pollution in the comparison.
Bioremediation reliability varies with the pollutant, the organism used, site conditions and co-contaminants.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Synthetic biology is a current relevance area, precision biotherapeutics are linked with BioE3, Visakhapatnam was chosen for a marine biomaterials research facility, and AMTZ is associated with Vizag.
The proposed approach includes
national microbe-approval protocols under MoEFCC
, State bioremediation hubs and DBT-BIRAC startup funding.
The US EPA Superfund bioremediation guidelines are cited as a comparative model for India’s bioremediation approach.

rows.title: Eco-friendly technologies in agriculture - integrated pest management, biofertilisers, biopesticides, organic and natural farming
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-92

secs.t: Sustainable agriculture practices - identification vs harmful practices

x: Sustainable agriculture seeks to
produce food while protecting the environment and conserving resources for future generations
The evergreen revolution approach is associated with
ZBNF, organic farming, water conservation and integrated pest management
Unlike a strict organic approach, sustainable agriculture may use synthetic inputs judiciously along with integrated pest management, precision farming and conservation tillage.

secs.t: Organic manures and amendments → composition and benefit

x: Vermicompost
is produced by the digestion of organic waste by earthworms and helps restore soil microbes and organic carbon.
Green manure consists of leguminous crops such as sunn hemp and dhaincha that are ploughed into the soil while green, adding nitrogen and organic matter.
The allocation is sunn hemp (Jilledu) 50,311 quintals, dhaincha (Janumu) 21,291 quintals and green gram 20,316 quintals.

secs.t: Environmental impacts of agrochemicals - soil, water, biodiversity, restricted pesticides

x: Indiscriminate agrochemical use can cause secondary pest outbreaks, pesticide resistance, ecosystem contamination and contamination of soil and water.
Broadcasting granular fertiliser may lose
50–70 percent
of the applied nitrogen through ammonia loss or nitrate leaching into aquifers.
Pesticide residues can bioaccumulate in the food chain, leading to increasing concentration across feeding levels.

secs.t: AP Community-managed Natural Farming - agency, coverage, recognition

x: APCNF was formerly ZBNF, uses jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham, and covers over seven lakh farmers.
The Kenyan delegation visited farms in
Guntur district
and praised APCNF as a climate-resilient model.
The visited farms included crop-diversified plots using
marigold and castor
as trap crops.
NTR district was promoted as a natural-farming model with QR-based traceability for organic produce

secs.t: Biopesticides and IPM components

x: Trichoderma is an antagonistic fungus used against soil-borne fungal diseases, particularly wilt and root rot.
Azadirachtin is derived from
neem
and acts against a wide range of insects, chiefly as an antifeedant.
All four statements describe recognised IPM components: resistant varieties, cultural practices, mechanical or physical methods, and need-based chemical control.

secs.t: Organic farming milestones and schemes

x: MOVCDNER
promotes organic value chains in the North-Eastern Region, whereas PKVY covers the rest of the country.
The reported PKVY figures up to 31 July 2025 were
15.08 lakh hectares, 25.38 lakh farmers and Rs 2,524.68 crore released
All four statements correctly describe PKVY as presented: its cluster structure, certification routes and the addition of 200 tribal-area clusters in Visakhapatnam.

secs.t: Natural farming and permaculture - originator, NMNF, inputs

x: Beejamrutha is used for seed treatment, Achhadana refers to mulching, and Whapasa concerns soil aeration and moisture balance.
Permaculture involves designing ecological habitats and food systems in a site-specific manner.
The term permaculture was coined by
Bill Mollison and David Holmgren in Australia
NMNF had an outlay of
Rs 2,481 crore
, comprising Rs 1,584 crore from the Centre and Rs 897 crore from the States, up to March 2026.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The scalability of Zero Budget Natural Farming has been questioned in debates concerning the wider adoption of natural farming.
Andhra Pradesh
has been described as a global pioneer in natural farming, and a Kenyan delegation undertook a study visit there.
Sikkim holds the distinction of being the first fully organic State, whereas PKVY was the first comprehensive Centrally Sponsored Scheme for organic farming.

rows.title: Precision agriculture, drip irrigation and other resource-efficient technologies
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-92

secs.t: Micro-irrigation - drip vs sprinkler, fertigation, Per Drop More Crop (PMKSY), Micro Irrigation Fund

x: Exam angle: "which technology suits water-scarce regions?" - drip irrigation.
Drip irrigation supplies water to the root zone, sprinklers spray it under pressure, and both help reduce evaporation and runoff losses.
Micro-irrigation helps save water, labour, power and fertiliser; it reduces rather than increases runoff losses.
Drip systems require relatively higher initial investment, while sprinklers are useful on uneven terrain but are more exposed to wind and evaporation losses.
From 2022-23, Per Drop More Crop has been implemented under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (
RKVY
The ₹10,000 crore Micro Irrigation Fund was created with NABARD to
help States mobilise resources for micro-irrigation

secs.t: Protected cultivation - polyhouses, hydroponics, aeroponics, vertical farming

x: Protected cultivation in greenhouses, polytunnels or shade nets provides a controlled environment and protection from adverse weather, pests and diseases.
Aeroponics
suspends plant roots in air and supplies them with a mist of nutrient solution.
Vertical farming
grows crops in stacked indoor layers under controlled conditions and can provide year-round output even in non-tropical or harsh settings.

secs.t: Resource-conserving technologies - zero tillage, laser levelling, DSR, SRI, SSI

x: Zero tillage is associated with sowing wheat without burning previous residue, direct planting of paddy without a nursery, and soil carbon sequestration.
Reduced or zero tillage combined with leaving crop residue helps conserve water.
Laser land levelling creates a uniform field surface, allowing water to spread evenly and thereby saving irrigation water.

secs.t: AP Micro Irrigation Project - coverage, subsidy pattern, state rank

x: The Andhra Pradesh Micro Irrigation Project is implemented State-wide under the
Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana
with financial assistance.
The newer automation-based system uses sensors and data analytics so that irrigation and fertiliser application are based
on precision rather than guesswork
All three statements correctly describe the irrigation and technology priorities identified in the Andhra Pradesh Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25.

secs.t: Precision agriculture tools - GPS, GIS, remote sensing, variable-rate technology, soil sensors

x: The
Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast Centre
has run the ISRO crop forecasting programme associated with FASAL since 2012 and monitors 29 double-risk districts through satellites.
The KISAN project uses space technology for planning Crop Cutting Experiments under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana.
GPS, drones, AI and sensors form the technological core of
the Second Green Revolution and sustainable intensification

secs.t: Drones in agriculture - Namo Drone Didi, Kisan drones, spraying SOPs

x: Kisan drones are used for crop assessment, soil health analysis and spraying, and can reduce human exposure to chemicals.
The stated water-saving potential of Kisan drones is up to
30 percent
Agricultural drones are regulated by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation under the Drone Rules, 2021.
Drone Shakti supports the drone ecosystem through manufacturing and training for Remote Pilot Certificates.

secs.t: Digital Agriculture Mission - AgriStack, Krishi DSS, digital crop survey, AP e-Crop booking

x: The mission’s digital public infrastructure includes AgriStack, the Krishi Decision Support System and the Soil Fertility Profile.
Krishi DSS supports crop mapping, diversification and insurance claims, and is aligned with the National Geo-Spatial Policy.
The digital crop survey records plot-level, real-time crop acreage to improve the accuracy of production estimates.

secs.t: Solar pumps and AI/IoT advisories - PM-KUSUM components, Kisan e-Mitra

x: The
Assam
State Irrigation Plan uses solar pumps.
Kisan e-Mitra uses AI to answer PM-KISAN queries in several languages.
Agritech start-ups offer AI advisories, precision irrigation and crop-health monitoring.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The policy emphasis on higher output with lower ecological cost is described as the
Evergreen Revolution
, associated with M.S. Swaminathan.
The current relevance includes PMKSY at ten years, automation-based micro-irrigation in Andhra Pradesh and APDC drone services in all 26 districts.
APSES 2024-25 identifies
precision farming, drones, IoT, drip and sprinkler irrigation, and rainwater harvesting
as the way forward.

rows.title: Genetic engineering - recombinant DNA, GM crops (Bt cotton, Bt brinjal, GM mustard), gene editing/CRISPR
sub: Group-II M2-B-82: Impact of transgenics on the environment - gene flow, biodiversity and biosafety concerns

secs.t: Other GM applications - Golden Rice, Flavr Savr, transgenic animals, GM mosquitoes

x: Golden Rice produces beta-carotene, which is a precursor of
Vitamin A
and is intended to help combat Vitamin A deficiency and blindness.
Golden Rice contains phytoene synthase derived from daffodil and crtI derived from the bacterium Erwinia uredovora.
A CRISPR-Cas9 gene drive copies itself onto the partner chromosome, causing inheritance in more than 90 percent of offspring instead of the usual approximately 50 percent.

secs.t: GM crops in India - Bt cotton, Bt brinjal, GM mustard, HT Bt cotton

x: Exam angle: Bt brinjal "developed for" - insect resistance; "only GM crop cultivated" - Bt cotton.
The commercially approved Bt cotton involved three hybrids of MAHYCO and was designed primarily to resist the American bollworm.
GM mustard DMH-11 received GEAC approval for environmental release in October 2022, although the matter remained under consideration by the Supreme Court.

secs.t: rDNA technology - steps, tools, FIRST rDNA product

x: DNA is first isolated, then cut at specific sites, joined by DNA ligase to form recombinant DNA, and finally inserted into a host cell.
Polymerase chain reaction, or
PCR
, is used for isolation and amplification of the desired DNA fragment.
Agrobacterium tumefaciens is called nature's genetic engineer because T-DNA from its disarmed Ti plasmid can carry the desired gene into the plant nucleus.

secs.t: Bt technology - gene source, Bollgard, mode of action

x: Bacillus thuringiensis forms crystal proteins called
delta-endotoxins
during sporulation.
The Bt protoxin is activated in the alkaline gut of the larva, binds to midgut cells, creates pores and ultimately kills the insect.
Pink bollworm has developed resistance to Bt cotton, making resistance build-up an important environmental and agricultural concern.
Bt proteins have been shown to degrade in soil

secs.t: Gene editing - CRISPR-Cas9, SDN categories, personalised medicine

x: Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier demonstrated CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing in 2012 and received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2020.
SDN-1 produces a small change without using a template or introducing foreign DNA and is exempt from GM rules under the 2022 guidelines.
ContactSeek uses AI with AlphaFold3 to help
cut off-target edits
, thereby improving the precision of gene editing.

secs.t: Genetic medicine - gene therapy, MRT, recombinant vaccines

x: Engineered viruses and lipid nanoparticles
are used as carriers for delivering genetic material in genetic medicine.

Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy is popularly called the “three-parent baby” technique because mitochondrial material is obtained from a donor in addition to the nuclear genetic material of the parents.
Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy raises ethical concerns because it involves germline changes and is linked to debates over designer babies.

secs.t: Biofortified vs GM crops

x: Biofortification generally increases nutritional value through conventional breeding, while GM crops involve insertion of foreign genes.
Dhanshakti is an iron-rich pearl millet variety associated with ICRISAT.
ICAR released 524 varieties in the stated year, of which 34 were biofortified and 79 were stress-tolerant.

secs.t: Gene flow - transgene escape, superweeds, centres of origin

x: Gene flow occurs when transgenes move through pollen and cross-pollination into non-GM crops or related wild plants.
Movement of herbicide-tolerance genes into weedy relatives can create invasive superweeds and increase weediness.
India is a centre of diversity of
brinjal
, and the presence of wild relatives was an important argument in the concern over Bt brinjal.

secs.t: Loss of crop genetic diversity - monoculture, landraces

x: Genetic homogenisation results when uniform varieties are widely cultivated, reducing agro-biodiversity and increasing vulnerability to new pathogens and climate shocks.
Monoculture and concentration of seed production can displace traditional
landraces and farmer varieties
Genetic modification
has been identified as the technology among these options that was flagged for its potential impact on biodiversity.

secs.t: Genetic use restriction (terminator) technology

x: V-GURT has not been commercialised anywhere and is banned in India under the PPV&FR Act, 2001.
Terminator technology makes the next generation of seeds non-viable, preventing seed saving and replanting and potentially forcing annual purchases.

secs.t: Biosafety concerns - allergenicity, HGT, marker genes, Mon 863

x: Horizontal gene transfer is the
movement of genes between unrelated organisms
Antibiotic-resistance marker genes may contribute to the spread of antibiotic resistance, which is a recognised biosafety concern.
Mon 863 was a Monsanto genetically modified pest-resistant maize variety directed against corn rootworm and was discussed in connection with feeding-study safety.

secs.t: Bt cotton experience - resistance, secondary pests, outcomes

x: The reported yield increased from
190 kg/ha in 2002 to 480 kg/ha in 2023
, although benefits varied by region.
Whitefly and mealybug are examples of sucking or secondary pests that increased as a problem in Bt cotton cultivation.
The reported difficulties included pest resistance, failure to adopt refuges or recommended practices, high input costs and dependence on purchased seed.

secs.t: Effects on non-target organisms

x: Bt toxins or other engineered traits may affect beneficial insects such as pollinators and natural enemies, soil nematodes and microbes, and aquatic organisms.
Although persistence of Bt proteins in soil was feared,
experiments have shown that they degrade in soil

secs.t: Illegal herbicide-tolerant Bt cotton

x: HTBt cotton combines glyphosate tolerance with the Bt trait, but it is not approved in India.
Herbicide-tolerant crops may encourage heavy glyphosate use, which is a major environmental and agricultural concern.
Punjab banned the sale of glyphosate in 2018.

secs.t: Transgenic animals and microbes - GM mosquitoes, GM fish

x: GM mosquitoes may be engineered either to suppress mosquito populations or to block transmission of diseases such as malaria, dengue and Zika.
A gene drive produces super-Mendelian inheritance, allowing an engineered trait to spread through a wild population more rapidly than ordinary Mendelian inheritance.
Gene drives may spread a trait through wild populations, potentially causing population collapse or producing malaria-resistant mosquitoes.

secs.t: Claimed environmental benefits

x: The claimed benefits include reduced pesticide use in Bt cotton, herbicide tolerance, drought tolerance and stress tolerance achieved through genome editing.
Genome-edited Pusa Rice DST1 is associated with
drought and salinity
tolerance and has shown higher yield under stress conditions.
Pusa Rice DST1 has been reported to provide a yield increase of approximately
10–30 percent
under drought or salinity stress.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A noted criticism is that societies tend to accept gene therapy while resisting GM crops, even though GM maize, soy, cotton and canola are widely grown and traded.
GEAC cleared confined trials of Bayer’s herbicide-tolerant and insect-resistant GM maize at PAU during
Kharif 2025
The Bayer GM maize trials at PAU during Kharif 2025 illustrate the field-trial framework requiring a State NOC.

rows.title: Regulation and ethics of biotechnology - GEAC, biosafety, bioethics, biopiracy, IPR and the ethical/social/legal debate
sub: Group-II M2-B-83: Regulation of transgenics in India - GEAC, biosafety rules and GM crop status

secs.t: GEAC - ministry, Act, chair, role

x: The
Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee
(GEAC) is the apex statutory body regulating GMOs in India.
GEAC is chaired by a Special or Additional Secretary of MoEFCC.
GEAC deals with field trials, environmental release, commercial cultivation and large-scale use of hazardous microorganisms and recombinants.
The committee was renamed from Genetic Engineering Approval Committee to Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee in 2010.

secs.t: GM debate - environmental concerns, field trials, TEC report, state bans

x: Insect resistance, harm to non-target organisms, weediness in wild relatives and genetic homogenisation are all recognised environmental concerns associated with GM crops.
Bt cotton was introduced in 2002, the PIL was filed in 2006, the Bt brinjal moratorium was imposed in 2010, and GEAC cleared trials in 2014.
Overlapping mandates among DBT, GEAC, CDSCO, FSSAI and NBA, together with the absence of a biosafety liability law, contribute to delays.

secs.t: IPR in biotech - Patents Act, PPVFR Act 2001, Novartis and PepsiCo cases

x: Section 3(j)
excludes plants, animals, seeds and essentially biological processes from patentability, while microbial processes can be patented.
PepsiCo sued Gujarat farmers over its FL-2027 (FC5) variety, later withdrew the suits, and the PPVFR Authority revoked the registration in 2021.
Farmers may save, use, sow, resow, exchange, share and sell farm produce including seed, but they may not
sell branded seed

secs.t: Seed technologies in controversy - GURT / terminator seeds

x: GURT stands for
Genetic Use Restriction Technology
Terminator seeds produce sterile seeds, so farmers must buy fresh seed each season.
The PPVFR Act bars registration of varieties carrying Genetic Use Restriction Technology.
Farmers' objections include dependency on companies, recurring costs and loss of seed-saving.

secs.t: Bioethics - stem cells, cloning, embryo editing, informed consent

x: “Designer babies” refers to the ethical concern that genetic technologies could be used to select or modify desired traits in human offspring.
He Jiankui’s human embryo-editing experiment in China became widely associated with the “CRISPR babies” controversy in 2018.
UNESCO’s International Bioethics Committee
monitors the ethical implications of genome editing.

secs.t: Rules 1989 under EPA - competent authorities, GM food imports

x: RDAC is a DBT-associated advisory body, IBSC is the institutional biosafety committee, and GEAC is associated with MoEFCC.
The Review Committee on Genetic Manipulation monitors the safety of ongoing research and makes recommendations to GEAC.
The FSSAI GM food framework is associated with 2024, whereas 2002 relates to the Biological Diversity Act and 2009 to the National Biosafety Framework.

secs.t: Biosafety - Cartagena Protocol, BSL-1 to BSL-4

x: The Cartagena Protocol was adopted in 2000, entered into force in 2003, governs safe handling and transboundary movement of LMOs, and includes the Advance Informed Agreement procedure.
BSL-4 is used for lethal agents with no cure, such as Ebola, and the National Institute of Virology at Pune is identified in this context in India.

secs.t: Biosecurity and dual-use research - BWC

x: The Biological Weapons Convention was opened in 1972 and entered into force in 1975.
The
Weapons of Mass Destruction Act, 2005
criminalises biological weapons.
DBT is associated with biocontainment, while NCDC is associated with surveillance in the stated biosecurity framework.
The stated gap is the
absence of a unified national biosecurity framework
, with laws also lagging behind synthetic biology and gene editing.

secs.t: GM crops → introduced trait + source organism

x: Bt cotton Bollgard I uses Cry1Ac from Bacillus thuringiensis to provide
bollworm resistance
The barnase-barstar system in GM mustard DMH-11 is used for
hybrid seed production
, associated with higher yield of 25–30%.
Golden Rice contains genes sourced from
a daffodil and a soil bacterium
to support beta-carotene biosynthesis.
Flavr Savr tomato was engineered for delayed ripening and softening and longer shelf life using an antisense polygalacturonase gene.

secs.t: GM crops approved for commercial cultivation - list, year, states

x: Bt cotton
was approved for commercial cultivation in March 2002.
Three MAHYCO hybrids were initially approved for three years, and Bt cotton remains the only GM crop commercially cultivated in India.
Bt cotton covers approximately 12.5 million hectares, representing over 90% of India’s cotton area.
Maharashtra
is identified as the leading Bt cotton State.

secs.t: Genome-edited crops - SDN-1/SDN-2, released rice

x: Pusa Rice DST1 was developed by ICAR-IARI, Delhi; Kamala by ICAR through IIRR, Hyderabad; and the CRISPR phosphate-uptake rice by NIPGR.
Pusa Rice DST1 is an edited form of MTU1010, designed for drought and salinity tolerance through DST gene knockout using SDN-1.
Pusa Rice DST1
from IARI is set for commercial launch after CRISPR-Cas9 editing of the DST gene in MTU1010.

secs.t: Field trial process - BRL trials, state NOC

x: The process begins with committees’ safety assessments, followed by confined open-plot trials, evaluation of superiority without ecological harm, and only then commercial clearance.
The trials are called
Biosafety Research Level trials
, comprising BRL-I and BRL-II stages.
Commercial clearance is contemplated only when trials show superiority over non-GM varieties without ecological harm.

secs.t: Proposed regulators and policy - BRAI Bill, national GM policy

x: The BRAI Bill, 2013 proposed a single Biotechnology Regulatory Authority of India.
The BRAI Bill, 2013 lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha.
The
BioE3 Policy, 2024
proposes single-window clearance and regulatory sandboxes.
The Supreme Court’s July 2024 direction called for a national GM crop policy after stakeholder consultation.
SDN-1 and SDN-2 are exempted in the stated framework, while SDN-3 remains under tight GM controls.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The exemption has been criticised as a possible back door around the full GM regulatory route, with concerns about biosecurity gaps.
The comparative position described is that the US, Canada, Brazil and India grow GM maize, soy, cotton and canola, while Japan and Australia import GE foods without GM labels.

rows.title: Nanotechnology - nature, scope, applications, Nano Mission, health and environmental concerns

secs.t: Nanoscale - size, surface area, quantum effects, coinage

x: Quantum effects and the high surface-area-to-volume ratio produce enhanced reactivity and unusual optical and electrical behaviour.
Richard Feynman
proposed the foundational idea in his 1959 lecture, “There’s Plenty of Room at the Bottom.”.
Norio Taniguchi coined the term ‘nanotechnology’ in 1974.

secs.t: Generations of nanoproducts - four generations in order

x: Exam angle: "which is a third-generation nanosystem" - match example to generation.
The third generation consists of systems of nanosystems, including complex devices such as nanoelectronics and nanomedicine.
All four pairs correctly represent the four generations: passive structures, active structures, systems of nanosystems and molecular nanosystems.
The four-generation classification of nanoproducts is associated with
M. C. Roco

secs.t: Nano devices - nanogenerators, nanosensors

x: The NCL nanogenerator converts mechanical pressure into electricity through the
piezoelectric effect
Gold-nanoparticle lateral-flow kits can diagnose malaria, dengue and typhoid rapidly, while graphene enables bendable wearable sensors.
The diagnostic nanosensor kits are designed for rapid detection of
malaria, dengue and typhoid
in about 15 minutes.
The Internet of Nano Things is the networking of nanodevices over the internet.

secs.t: Nanomedicine - targeted delivery, CNT carriers, cancer nanoparticles

x: IIT Mandi developed renewable-resource-based natural-polymer nanoparticles for
colorectal cancer
applications.
Nano-cellulose is associated with packaging and filters.
The silver-nanoparticle wound dressings were reported to reduce infections by approximately
The DCGI approved
Pulse Pharmaceuticals
’ nano-carrier Vitamin D3 oral dispersion, described as a claimed world first.

secs.t: Nanomaterials - graphene, fullerenes, CNTs, quantum dots, wells, wires

x: Fullerene C60 is popularly called a buckyball and is associated with Kroto, Curl and Smalley, who received the Nobel Chemistry Prize in 1996.
Moungi Bawendi, Louis Brus and Alexei Ekimov were associated with the 2023 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for quantum dots.
Quantum wells, wires and dots involve confinement in one, two and three dimensions respectively, corresponding to 2D, 1D and 0D structures.

secs.t: Concerns - nanotoxicity, natural vs engineered, environment, agri guidelines

x: Nanoparticles may induce
oxidative stress and inflammation
, with concerns also relating to long-term toxicity, persistence and bioaccumulation.

Nano-cellulose is derived from plant cellulose and is light, strong and biodegradable, with uses in packaging and filters.

Wolbachia acts through cytoplasmic incompatibility, in which mismatched eggs fail to hatch, and through pathogen blocking.

cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A and E, acute diarrhoea, dysentery and polio
Floods can spread
cholera, typhoid, hepatitis and leptospirosis
, in addition to supporting the spread of some vector-borne diseases.
Jal Jeevan Mission, Swachh Bharat Mission and AMRUT

secs.t: Air pollution and health

x: Air pollution primarily affects the
respiratory system
, although it is also associated with cardiovascular disease, stroke and lung cancer.

DALY

The Verily ‘Debug’ approach used Wolbachia-carrying males to suppress
Culex quinquefasciatus
, a vector associated with West Nile and St Louis encephalitis.

secs.t: Antimicrobial resistance - causes, biofilms, antibiotics, NAP-AMR, Red Line

x: AMR is driven by interconnected human, animal, agricultural, veterinary and environmental factors, including pharmaceutical effluents and poor waste control.
Biofilms are microbial or bacterial communities embedded in a self-made slimy matrix, which shields them from antibiotics and, in many cases, from host immunity.
The slimy matrix of a biofilm protects bacterial communities from antibiotics and host immunity, making infections difficult to treat.
The Red Line campaign, introduced in 2016, places
a red vertical line on packs of prescription-only antibiotics
to discourage unsupervised use.

x: Biodiversity loss can increase zoonotic and pandemic risk by disturbing ecological relationships and interactions between humans, animals and pathogens.
One Health uses joint surveillance, animal vaccination, veterinary drug oversight, carcass and waste control, and linked databases.
The National One Health Mission is applicable to rabies, Nipah, avian influenza and AMR, among other linked health threats.
Biodiversity loss can increase zoonotic risk, Mpox is associated with rodents and primates, and rabies may be transmitted by dogs, bats and other wild animals.

of Indian districts are at high risk from extreme weather.

2.5 lakh
additional deaths annually during 2030–2050 from the specified climate-sensitive causes.

is associated with rodents and is transmitted through rat fleas.

Rabies is a zoonotic disease transmitted mainly through animal bites, but it is not classified as vector-borne.

people in ASR and Parvathipuram-Manyam, involving an expenditure of Rs 19.25 crore.

higher than those through Jan Aushadhi.

secs.t: Out-of-pocket expenditure - share, trend, catastrophic spending

x: Childbirth-related OOPE was ₹37,630 in private facilities compared with ₹2,299 in public facilities—more than sixteen times higher in the private sector.
Outpatient care, diagnostics and medicines
account for over half of OOPE because insurance commonly does not cover them.
The “missing middle” refers to more than 40 crore Indians who lack adequate financial protection; NITI Aayog first flagged the term.

secs.t: Insurance landscape - CGHS, ESIS, state schemes, private insurance

x: Government-financed health insurance rose 2.5-fold between 2017–18 and 2025.
NFHS-6 recorded an increase from 41.0% of households to 60.2% having a health-insurance member.
Private insurance may involve premiums, exclusions, waiting periods and co-payments.
The Clinical Establishments Act, 2010 had been adopted in only about
11 States and 6 Union Territories

secs.t: 15th Finance Commission health grants - components

x: The 15th Finance Commission recommended health grants amounting to
₹70,051 crore
through local governments for 2021–2026.
The grants support diagnostic infrastructure for sub-centres and PHCs, block public health units, urban health and wellness centres, and buildings for building-less SCs, PHCs and CHCs.
The grants cover several components, including rural and block-level infrastructure as well as urban health and wellness centres.

secs.t: Government vs private share - NHA estimates

x: Exam angle: statement sets on NHA (SHA 2011 base; GHE highest during COVID; OOPE fell, not rose, during COVID - 39.4% of THE).
The sequence proceeds from the SHA 2011 reference base to the 2013–14 comparison year, then to the COVID-19 period, followed by the later estimate reporting a 43.7% government share.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The parliamentary panel’s discussion on the ‘missing middle’, along with the NHA 2022–23 assessment, confirms that the 2.5% target remains unmet.
Praja Arogya Vedika sought a Right to Health Act and withdrawal of PPPs in government medical colleges.
A stated criticism is that insurance-led models may expand coverage without a corresponding increase in actual care.
