sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-96

secs.t: National Health Mission - NRHM, ASHA, JSY, JSSK, RKSK, Anaemia Mukt Bharat, funding

x: ASHA means Accredited Social Health Activist, and ASHAs and ANMs play a crucial role in linking rural communities with healthcare services.
JSY is fully centrally sponsored, promotes institutional delivery through cash assistance, and recorded 1,76,966 beneficiaries in Andhra Pradesh during the stated period.
Anaemia Mukt Bharat
follows the 6x6x6 strategy, including IFA supplementation, deworming, testing and treatment, fortified foods and behaviour change.

secs.t: Mission Indradhanush and the immunisation schedule

x: Mission Indradhanush is a catch-up immunisation drive for
zero-dose and partly immunised children
under the Universal Immunisation Programme.
Mission Indradhanush targeted
90 per cent
full immunisation coverage.
MR-1, JE-1, MR-2 and the second DPT booster occur in the stated age ranges.
U-WIN digitises
maternal and child vaccination records
and supports immunisation tracking.

secs.t: Digital health - ABDM components, U-WIN, eSanjeevani, telehealth

x: ABDM was launched in September 2021, is run by NHA, and builds a consent-based interoperable ecosystem on Digital Public Infrastructure.
The NMC directed medical colleges to generate and link ABHA IDs for all OPD, IPD and emergency patients, partly to detect fake patients during inspections.
All three statements are correct. eSanjeevani incorporates a Clinical Decision Support System, NextGen eHospital is ABDM-aligned, and AYUSH HMIS was linked to ABHA in 2024.

secs.t: Ayushman Bharat - pillars, PM-ABHIM, Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, insurance cover

x: Primary care through Ayushman Arogya Mandirs is intended to meet approximately
80–90 per cent
of healthcare needs.
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs provide services including non-communicable disease screening, mental health, ENT, eye, oral, geriatric, palliative and trauma care.
These campaigns are associated with
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs
and aim to increase community participation and saturation of health-related services.

secs.t: AP healthcare interventions - telemedicine, Family Physician, village clinics, diagnostics

x: Sanjeevani links PHCs, hospitals, laboratories, e-Aushadhi, 108 emergency services, 104 mobile medical units, telemedicine and AI assistance.
The Sanjeevani Citizen Wellness App is the citizen-facing application associated with the
Sanjeevani digital health programme
Union Health Minister J. P. Nadda inaugurated
10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 Integrated Public Health Laboratories
in Andhra Pradesh under PM-ABHIM.

secs.t: Public health campaigns - Swachh Bharat, Fit India, Eat Right India

x: Swachh Bharat focuses on sanitation, Fit India on daily fitness, and Eat Right India on safe, healthy and sustainable diets.
Eat Right India is an initiative of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, established under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
Together, Eat Right India and Fit India aim to reduce deaths caused by
non-communicable diseases
through healthier diets and increased physical activity.

secs.t: ICMR - history and priorities

x: The Indian Research Fund Association was established in 1911 and was later renamed the ICMR in 1949.
The correct order is establishment of IRFA in 1911, WHO in 1948, renaming as ICMR in 1949, and Eat Right India in 2018.
The Secretariat aims to reduce India’s import dependence in medical devices and diagnostics.

secs.t: Global health bodies and days - WHO

x: WHO headquarters:
Geneva;
founded
7 April 1948
- so
World Health Day is 7 April

secs.t: National Health Policy - years, NHP 2017 priorities and targets

x: NHP 2017 adopted an assurance-based approach and envisaged comprehensive primary care rather than an insurance-only or disease-specific model.
NHP 2017 included NCD, mental health, geriatric and palliative care within comprehensive primary care, along with free drugs, diagnostics and emergency care in public hospitals.
NHP 2017 targeted life expectancy of 70 years, TFR of 2.1, IMR of 28 and MMR of 100 within the specified target years.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The criticism is that insurance-led policies can expand coverage while failing to ensure actual access to health services.
Sanjeevani makes Andhra Pradesh an ABDM-linked, citizen-wide digital health state through digital profiles, ABHA IDs and connected health services.

secs.t: HIV/AIDS - NACP phases, NACO, ICTC, HIV and AIDS Act, 95-95-95, projects, strain

x: NACP Phase V covers 2021–2026 and aims to reduce new HIV infections and AIDS deaths by 80%.
The three 95s refer respectively to knowledge of HIV status, treatment, and viral-load suppression among those treated.
The
Red Ribbon Express
is an awareness train used for HIV/AIDS awareness.
Treatment as Prevention, Test and Treat, PEP within 72 hours, PrEP and condoms are recognised prevention tools.

secs.t: Malaria elimination - national framework, MERA India, malaria-free countries, vaccines

x: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination covers
and targets malaria elimination by 2030.
Sri Lanka, China and Timor-Leste
are the three countries identified as WHO-certified malaria-free in this group.
Only about
of global malaria financing needs are met.
MERA India stands for the
ICMR-led Malaria Elimination Research Alliance

secs.t: Eradication milestones - smallpox, polio, Pulse Polio, bOPV

x: India became free of smallpox in 1977, Pulse Polio was launched in 1995, the last wild polio case occurred in January 2011, and the region was certified polio-free in 2014.
The WHO South-East Asia Region received polio-free certification on
27 March 2014
The switch from trivalent OPV to bivalent OPV took place in
April 2016

secs.t: TB elimination - target year, TB Mukt Bharat, Ni-kshay, India TB Report

x: Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana provides nutritional DBT to all notified TB patients in both the public and private sectors.
The campaign was launched in September 2022, uses Ni-kshay Mitras to adopt patients, and includes food-basket support.
Himachal Pradesh
screens all indoor hospital patients for TB as part of intensified case finding.

secs.t: Elimination missions → target year

x: India has set a target to eliminate sickle-cell anaemia by 2047 and to screen seven crore at-risk people.
Triple-drug IDA consists of Ivermectin, diethylcarbamazine (DEC) and Albendazole.
Malaria, lymphatic filariasis and kala-azar
are the diseases identified for elimination under NVBDCP.
The National Leprosy Eradication Programme provides free multidrug therapy at primary health centres.

secs.t: NCD programme - NP-NCD, screening, IHCI, Cervavac

x: In Andhra Pradesh, the expanded NP-NCD coverage includes mental health, elderly care, iodine deficiency disorders, tobacco control, fluorosis and oral health.
ANMs screen people at home using the ANM AP Health App, and universal NCD-CD 3.0 screening began on 14 November 2024 and covered 53.02 lakh citizens.
The India Hypertension Control Initiative targets hypertension-related deaths from
heart attack, stroke and kidney failure

secs.t: Mental health - Mental Healthcare Act 2017, Tele-MANAS, NMHP

x: DMHP covers more than 90% of districts, 1.73 lakh AAMs include mental health, MANODARPAN supports students, and KIRAN is associated with the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
The National Mental Health Programme dates to 1982, the Mental Health Act to 1987, the Mental Healthcare Act to 2017 and Tele-MANAS to 2022.

secs.t: AP programme performance - TB, HIV

x: Exam angle: programme → launch year and disease → target year matching; the PYQ key:
NVBDCP
handles outbreaks of malaria, dengue, chikungunya.
The state runs
NTEP, NCVBDC, NPCBVI, NLEP, rabies, leptospirosis and snake-bite programmes
Because malaria epidemiology is changing in both tribal and non-tribal districts, sustained surveillance through the relevant vector-borne disease programme is required.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh has set
December 2026
as the target for achieving its HIV cascade objective.
The report titled 'United to end AIDS' noted that new infections had reached a 30-year low, while available funding was $17.6 billion against a requirement of $21.9 billion.
SDG 3.3 specifically seeks to end the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases by 2030.
